title: David Tepper speaks to the media at practice | Carolina Panthers
text: Dave, how are you doing? >> Good. Um, hey, listen, when you when you drafted Bryce, you said he's a guy that can bring multiple Super Bowls here to Carolina. Do you still feel that that way, and if so, why? >> Um, you know what? I think he has a lot of talent. And with the right right right weapons in the right situation, yeah. >> When you when you called on uh Scott Fowler, Dave, thank you for doing this. We We haven't gotten to speak to you much lately. Has that have been a purposeful uh stepping back for you, or are you just as involved, and we just don't hear it? >> just for 2 hours in my office. How do I know it's a long time to talk anybody talk to you? That's I thought it wasn't I wasn't stepping back. I was stepping into you. >> You're right. You're right. But in terms of like answering questions publicly and on the record. >> Oh, okay. >> Yeah. >> Uh no, I mean, I'm I'm willing to do it anytime, Scott. You can come by, and I'll tell you stuff on the record, so. >> Mike Kaye, you talked about Bryce becoming a point guard when you did discuss those Super Bowls, and said that you didn't need to surround him with a lot of stuff. How do you feel with him being contract extension eligible? >> Whoa whoa whoa whoa whoa. Don't surround him with a lot of stuff. >> You didn't need to invest as much into the receiving core. >> No, I never said that. That's wrong. Okay, I don't I never said that. How do you become a point guard without players around you? That makes no sense. >> Did you >> Try again. >> Okay. That you could boost the the talent around him because of his point guard distribution skills. Do you not remember this? >> I said he's a point guard and he can distribute the ball around, but he needs people to distribute around. That's why what you're saying makes no sense. >> Okay. With that said, from what you've seen and how he has played around the weapons that you've given him, how do you feel about him during his first extension eligible season? >> Um, being his first ex- this year or last year? >> This year is his first year. >> Well, listen, he exhibited last year sometimes and I think he should have did it more. You know, we'll see how the health of the offensive line is and he has time, he'll do it. >> Joe Person >> Dave, have you guys offered him an extension and how did if so, how did those preliminary talks go? >> You know, that's a question for Dan Morgan. You know, his If you need his number, I'll give it to you. >> No, I mean you want to bring him over here. >> You can talk to him. You can go grab him. He may talk to you. >> Do you envision What would prompt you guys to offer him an extension? >> I'm not saying we have or we haven't either. So, you should talk to Dan. Look, success is success and you know it when you see it. >> Have you seen >> I mean we want questions for Person. I'll try to be fair to everybody. >> Well, that's a follow-up question. >> I know, but we're not doing follow-ups. >> seen it? >> We're not doing follow-ups. Go back there. >> All right. Um when you came, you said you wanted to build sustained excellence. Um what have you What do you like right now about the direction that this team is heading? >> Well, look, I think that if you look at the team Listen, last year's team, you know, I kind of said that we could be a we're not a playoff team, but we could get in the playoffs. I think we have the all the We're more of a playoff team this year than we were last year coming into it. I think the um Look, the preseason um when you have winning records in the preseason, it's uh it's uh it kind of has it kind of plays into your depth. So, I think Dan's done a good job and the guys have done a good job building the depth on the team. And, you know, I think the pieces are there and we have everything we need. >> Phil Orban >> Does it feel like you are on pace for whatever timeline you had for Dave and Dan and bringing them in and it feels like from the outside there are some additional expectations on this team and how how have you handled that and and how do you handle the expectations that are sort of on this team? >> Well, I mean, I know all the expectation you guys write about. I can see what the odds are that we have 7 and 1/2 wins this season. So, those are the expectations and the expectations are based on last year. Right? So, if we improve on some of those things last year, for instance, we can't have all come from behind wins in the NFL and that's one of the reasons. So, if we get fast starts this year, fast starts to game, we're going to win. >> Mike Solarte You just got asked about the trajectory and are you on the right on the path that you envisioned? What hurdles are in the way for you to get to the goal that you want to have for this franchise? >> Listen, we we are on the path. Um there's always hurdles in the path. You'd like to be totally healthy and not have uh you know, have all your starting players. Those are always hurdles, you know? Now, the hurdles you have, you know they're there, so you got to make up for them. As uh different people have said, like uh Scott Fowler after the Texas practice. You know, so you know you what you have your issues are and you have to deal with them, right? So, those are hurdles. But uh like I said, all the all the pieces are here and hopefully they come together. I'm I'm a believer. >> Alex Zetluh >> According to Hey, Dave. Thanks for >> Hey, hey Alex. How are you? >> Doing great. Um according to NFLPA report cards released last year or perhaps earlier this year, um accommodations have been uh grades have increased and been better across the board besides travel accommodations and home team facilities. Um and that was including grass over turf, obviously. Um in what ways are you taking strides to address those needs specifically for the players? >> Well, listen. I mean, could you turn around for a second? What is that over there? Hold on. Jeez, that's a big building over there. No, listen. We're putting a lot of money into the um into practice facility inside the building, you know, coming up with this week renovation we're doing. Um you know, in all sort of ways. Um, you know, including the what's behind your big ins- inside um field. But, everything, you know, uh from um aquatics and uh from what's there now, it's just going to be vast improvement from what we have now. Bigger bigger and better in a lot of different things. And you can go through it with Brandt or something like that. He'll take you through what we're planning. >> All right, Nick Carboni. Dave, when you look around the league at the quarterback contracts that are being handed out, what >> off your glasses so I can see your face. >> sure. Sure. Uh when you look around the league and see some of these quarterback contracts that are being handed out by teams. Saw Baker yesterday. What does a franchise quarterback look like in in your eyes and mind in terms of making that type of investment? >> I don't know what you think. Do you think uh Baker's a franchise quarterback? >> He is for that franchise, it seems like. Yeah. >> Well, I'm just curious. What do you think a franchise quarterback is? >> Consistent, high-level quarterback that produces winning teams every year. What's your question now? >> I guess you would just ans- I don't know what >> You answered my question, didn't you? You just answered my question. Yeah, that would be that. Yeah, sure. >> All right, Chanel. >> Dave, as far as the expectations >> You talk You stand on the way up here. >> I would love to, but I got >> [laughter] >> You have to head up there. >> As far as expectations go and what's been building here within the last year, just what do you see as far as what Dave and Dan are bringing? Even when guys go down and they're consistently bringing in new guys to step in those roles. >> Well, you asked two different things. So, you know, when you look at the who who we brought in just recently, um I mean, listen, these guys are on top of different things seeing what there is. And we got, you know, they did made a lot of late changes here. So, uh I think Dan and team are are are really on top of it. And you know, they are constantly communication with Dave about it. So, I think they've done a good job to try to bring in to try to help us out. You know, fortunately we have, you know, enough depth um you know, that we did um you know, we did have Rashad in here which would have been a big problem with the with Taylor having a problem here. Um you know, and and some of the other things that they're paying attention we just read uh T Rob in here. I don't know if it's K Rob, T Rob, or whatever it is. >> T Rob. >> T Rob, T Rob. Yeah, he's supposed to be um Yeah, it was I saw him the other day. He's 6'2". He's 6'2" like I'm 6'4" so he's big and he gets underneath people. He's really hard to block. So he's kind of interesting so um yeah, I think think these guys have generally done a good deal. Deal a good a good job filling the gaps and as I said I do think there's a lot more depth on this team. So, you know, we we can go far. We just we we have the possibility. We have we know we can come from behind, right? We know we can come from behind. We got to start fast. We got to start fast the season. We got to start fast games. Right? That's it. If we start fast games, start fast the season and you know, some of the things that Scott Fralic talked about, we know we have issues. We got to make sure we solve for those issues before we get in. You know, we'll be good and we'll win. That's it. >> All right, we'll take a couple more. I'll take a couple more questions. I wanted to go to um Logan. >> Um hi, I'm Logan. Nice to meet you. Thanks for doing this. You said that you believe in this team but what makes you specifically believe in Bryce Young and him being a step forward this year? >> Look, I mean you saw it. You know, he can um and he has, not can, has, you know, performed at a high level against high level competition. Seems to bring the best out of him. You know, Bryce is sort of guy that doesn't feel the pressure. Right? You saw that against the Rams twice. You know, when you have that kind of performance you know it's there. You know, can he bring it every single game? I believe he can. You know it's there. So, you You I'm a like I said I'm a believer. And hopefully it comes true. >> DeSean >> Dave, you referenced a few times your belief in this group. How would you define success this season? >> Listen, I've said it for a long time about the Carolina Panthers and maybe it's in the water. So, I won't say it's just one season. I'd like to have two winning seasons first time in this franchise history. So, I like to win this year and I like to win next year. You know, so I'd like to stream wins. You know, in other sports that we have I only stream wins, winning seasons so happens. This one we have it. This is what I like to see a stream winning seasons. That's success. So, you know, that you know that you're you build it you know, and it's coming and it's here. So. >> Last two, Joe Person and Mike Kaye. >> Um Do you have any interest, you mentioned multiple sports, any interest in trying to bring baseball here? >> Talk to Dundon in Raleigh. I mean, they've should >> Raleigh? >> Listen, you know >> Or being part of a partnership with him. you know, it's it's it's just very political with baseball, right? And this is uh you know, in this state. So, you know, I mean, I think it may come to North Carolina. It'll be a harder sh- job with that legislature to bring it here versus Raleigh, quite frankly. I mean, that's the truth. So, yeah. I mean, you know, I'm watching it. >> Dave, last question for Mike Kaye. >> over the last three years. >> You got to know Brad >> Is it over the last three years or two years? What did you think of Dave's decision to hand over play calling and how do you think that can impact the the product on Sunday? >> I think it it frees Dave up to really look at everything that's happening during the game. And, you know, um what you hope is that he, you know, that we are faster in some of the things that we should be doing like making the adjustments. So, I'm going to you know, my friend's got follow her again. So, if you have it and you start out the, um you know, start out with the, um, um, that you don't anticipate the other team, that you make the Dave's out there not with his head in the in the playbook, that he can see what's going on and make the help make those adjustments sooner. Cuz that's the name of the game here, you know, making those adjustments. So, realizing it and making those adjustments. We're not going to be perfect every time we come in. We're not going to know what We don't know what the heck Ben Johnson's going to do this week, right? You know what Ben Johnson's doing this week? Well, maybe Ben Johnson doesn't even know what he's doing yet this week. So, yeah, but whatever he does, you know, if we guess it right, that's great. And if we don't guess it right, fix it. And fix it, don't fix it before too long in the game. And I think I think that's one of the things that that really helps for him not to have his head in the playbook. So, yeah. I'll give you one more question for somebody. >> one. Nate Wimberly. Nate Wimberly, is there a message you want to send to Keep Pounding Nation before the season starts? >> Listen, normally I have my Keep Pounding hat every single day on. I love wearing it to golf, and by the way, just like the material, but I do. So, I just tell them to keep pounding. You know, we're making progress. We're going to continue to make progress. You know, you know, I believe in a winning season this year. It's Listen, nothing's easy in this NFL. Seriously, it's not. But I believe we we have everything here to win this year. And I believe we'll have everything to win in the future, too. And I do think we're on the right track, and I do think we have very good people here in, uh, Dan and and Dave and Brandt. So, I think we have a good, you know, good head team, good management team over in that side of the building. I trust them. I don't feel the need to be around as much here because I trust them so much. And, uh, I'm very Like I said, I'm optimistic. I'm realistic, though, okay? So, but I'm optimistic. >> All right, thank you very much, everyone. [snorts] >> [music] [music]

Uh but he was out there practicing today and again limited for him meant the same thing. It was probably not his, you know, four to six uh reps per rack. It was probably something like two or three. Um but he was able to get through it and I checked with him afterwards and he said he felt fine. No, with no Pat Jones, what does how much more responsibility is that put on Jaylen um on Sunday? And just in general, uh like what makes you confident that Jaylen can handle that that extra responsibility? >> They were starting opposite sides, so nothing really changes for Jaylen. Um it's more really princely, Trevvis, Thomas picking up some of the different roles that he plays in different packages. >> Dave, uh we just talked to uh Ter and one of the things he talked about is getting off to fast start. Yeah, >> I know that's something you've preached on too, but specifically Bryce has had slow starts, too. And I wonder if in looking at the last couple years that you've been with him, is there a common theme to some of his early season struggles? >> Really, the message for Bryce, the message for the whole group is consistency. And what we've seen is we can play really great quarters at times. Can we play full games consistently week in and week out? That's my messaging. That's the goal uh for it. And with consistency means, hey, if we can play this well, you know, down the stretch of a game or or we score more points in the second quarter, how about we just be consistent with all of it across the board? And that includes the first quarter, guys. We don't need to wait around to kind of feel it out and see what's happening. Let's go get it. We know what we're doing. Um and which the confidence and the knowledge of what of how we're trying to employ things really just leads to fast football. And we have all that. We have guys that have been in the system, guys that know what they're doing, and so my expectation is the guys come out and play great from snap one to the end. >> To follow up, did did you tweak anything in preeason or in camp with the idea that this team would be maybe a little better prepared in week one? >> The emphasis for me is just about how we enter the practice field, how we step on the grass. There can't be a gradual easing into a practice. Um, body readiness. You got to be ready when you step on the grass. You can't be waiting around for Josh Hinks to get the dynamic warm-up going for you to be ready. That process starts in the locker room. And we have a number of guys that lead by example in that regard. They they're in there um working on their body, different things that have affected them over the course of time. They spend a little more attention on that. They're out on the field 15 minutes before we even start the practice just moving around. you know, it's Corey Thornton, it's JC Horn, Mike Jack, Chuba Hubard to to think off the top. Uh Devin Lloyd, these guys are out there just working on their craft and also just kind of wake up waking up their uh central nervous system so that they're ready to go when we start practice. It's no different than the game. Um on Sundays, they go through a process to get their body right and their mind right. The pregame, what everybody sees as our pregame isn't our warm-up. the guys are ready to play when we go into that, you know, and there's really not a full team stretch that happens. They're doing all the readiness inside. So, my challenge to the guys was replicate what it feels like to get your body ready so when you hit the grass, we're ready to go. I just think it's a muscle memory and a focus of like when I'm ready to go, it's full speed and we got to get going. >> Dave, I understand that the unofficial depth chart is the unofficial depth chart, but seeing Lee Hunter with that starting group, >> Yeah. >> I don't think EJ has started a rookie week one. What has he done to impress you guys and show you that he deserves to kind of be at the head of that rotation? >> Yeah, I mean it's twofold. First and foremost, you know, Lee just locking him into that nose position. Of course, when you're four down, he's got to play a shade. He's got to play a three depending on what the where the front moves and all that. Um, but they did a great job, Coach Wash, Ean, those guys did a great job of just really shrinking the package down for him so he could just get at one part and he started making plays. Um, started to take to the to the technique that we're looking for. Um, so that's that's a big part of it. And then the other side of it is necessity. We need Lee to go right now, you know, and and Turk's not ready to go. And he stepped in there and showed us that he can play quality snaps, you know, and that competition that was happening in there with he and Cam Jackson, you know, and and Lee did the work and made strides to be able to put himself out there as a starter. Between >> him and Monroe, you've got a couple of rookies starting on Sunday. I mean, there's always going to be nerves going into that first game. Do you talk to them ahead of time to keep them calm or just kind of let them do their own thing? I talk to them, you know, we just talk about it plainly and uh at the end of the day, it's just football and they've played a lot of football in their lifetime. So, lean on those experiences, lean on the coaching, uh default to your fundamentals and that'll carry you through. Um and just to convince the guys like you belong, you belong here, you belong out there on Sunday. and uh you know just having those those small sidebar conversations you know of of encouragement of challenging and then also I mean they're getting their butts coached off by their position coaches you know to to gain the technique and the the different you know the awareness that's required to play on Sundays and so and and it'll be a process and there will be some some great plays by them and there'll be some plays they're going to want to have back and um and that's all part of it. >> Dave, you talked about the readiness and kind of getting the central ner nervous system ready. Week one is a small size, but what does it mean to get a week one win? This is a program that hasn't had one in, I think, four straight seasons. What kind of confidence can that give a group when you get a first win? >> I really don't try to weigh them any different. Um, you know, preseason games, regular season one, you practice to win. You practice for that game. And this is the first opportunity to play a really good opponent and to see where we're at and also to just play our football. And it's a it's a growth curve from week one all the way to the end of the season where we're trying to find lessons in it. What are we doing really well and what do we need to improve on? And uh it's going to give us a lot of great information. Heck yeah, I want to win this game. Um absolutely. That's the whole point. We put all this time in and all that. But you know, I I just have a habit of I don't I don't put a lot of stock on any one moment. They're all important to me. They're all championship opportunities and I want our players to be thinking the same way. >> You had a pretty incredible atmosphere for the playoff game. How important is that to just continue when you get a home opener and to to kind of start this season off with that same experience? >> That's the exciting part. You know, I take a lot of pride with with the coaches as well. Um we take a lot of pride of being able to put out a brand of football that we're proud of that the Panthers fans are proud of and especially the ones who get to show up on Sunday um to see their team and to see what we could look like at times last year. But to see us do that consistently um it's going to be important and we got to be able to feed off that energy. I'm excited to get back in there. Bank of America Stadium um with the whole thing live and everyone's excited, everyone I've run into in town, everyone's fired up to see us get back to football. >> When you have five months where you know who your opponent is, what's the danger? Is there any danger in overpreparing, overthinking yourself? Like, how do you handle that? >> You got plenty of time to go through scenarios um to try to have contingency plans for things with that. We don't know what they've been practicing. They didn't show all their stuff in the preseason games where the starters played. Um, but the core principles were there. So, we can count on those things showing up. But there are things there's wrinkles we've been working on. There are wrinkles that the Bears have been working on throughout camp, throughout the offseason. So, while we got to take stock in what did they do last season, we also know there is there are going to be some adjustments that are going to need to be made in in the middle of the game. So, while you're preparing, you try not to just solidify a game plan way in advance. You just gather information on all the different areas so we can make educated assumptions about what they might be doing and then you go for it. And as we get closer, last week it started and then really honing the game plan on Monday and Tuesday so that we can go through a normal routine. Um, of course with a lot of other thoughts put into it. >> We do a couple more. >> Looking back at last year, what Chicago did and what you've seen implemented on tape in the preseason, what are your overall impressions and what they have coming in the year? extremely impressed. Uh coaching staff, first of all, that I really respect. Uh Ben Johnson, a guy I've studied for years, um watching what he built in Detroit and then got going uh with the Bears and making tweaks to fit his people, to fit Caleb, and to fit his skill group. On the defensive side, Dennis Allen is a guy that I really respect. Um I was able to coach against him in different capacities over the years and then as a coordinator when I was in Tampa. And just different things like that, he's got a lot of experience where he'll keep you guessing. And so, you have to go with the the percentages of what it's supposed to be, but also be ready for some wrinkles. So, um I just respect I respect the uh really just how smart this staff is and then of course the style of which they play. This is not a finesse offense. They run the ball hard. They run the ball with attitude. It's a really good front and some aggressive running backs. That's the challenge. Um we want to have an emphasis of of starting fast. You know, we we've talked about that a lot as a team, as a as a unit, as a organization. Um, but we know that that uh that comes with work. Um, you know, it's about just having the best week we can possible. Um, you know, going into the game with as much commun uh clear communication and uh being on the same page as we can. So, uh, we're excited for that challenge. Again, uh, we just want to go one and0 every week. Coach talks about it. Um, it's the most important game of the season because the next one, that's always his mantra. Um, again, we we have a ton of respect for for the Bears for them coming in. Um, and for us, we have a lot of pride in being able to uh, you know, open up at home. So, excited for the challenge. you're a pretty even temperate guy, but how are you feeling right now heading into week one? Are you excited or where what mental space are you in right now? >> Yeah, definitely excited. Um, you know, this is you miss it so much during the offseason. Um, and it's such a blessing just to be able to have the circumstances, uh, be where I'm at, uh, you know, play this position, you know, in this league. Um, I I don't take that for granted at all. Um, so I'm I'm definitely very excited. Um, and then, you know, you you have to obviously, um, you know, as a leader and as a Q, just you have to be whatever the team needs you to be on a day-to-day basis. Um, I'm I'm I felt like today was a good day. It was a good start. There's still a long week. Still a lot of building blocks we have to put in place. So, you know, I'm I'm I'm all into that. Um, making sure we can give ourselves the best chance on Sundays. But, of course, it's always always exciting when this time comes back around. >> I'm guessing I know the answer to this, but, you know, heading into a pivotal year, do you feel any added pressure? No, I I for me it's, you know, external stuff and and you know, that's stuff that's out of my control. Um, you know, I always play for the people um in this building. Uh we all rely on each other. Uh we all just want to be the best versions of ourselves, have success, uh you know, take it one day at a time, uh and and win each day. So, u you know, I'm not too big of a a big picture thinker. Um outside of that, >> we got a pretty interesting uh look at you and your life through your dad's book, Growing Up Young. What have your thoughts, I guess, in reaction been about that? And what do you hope maybe people can take away from your mindset and your attitude through reading or listening to that story? >> Yeah. Well, I'm I'm first off super proud of my pops. Uh he's worked really really hard on that for a really long time. So, um you know, it's been been cool to uh watch him go through that process to see the reception. Um you know, I'm just I'm super super happy for him. Um and you know I think that you know for for him is just being able to share our journey and um you know share our process and I know for him whatever hopefully he can be able to maybe uh help other people in in similar positions as he was um hopefully um you know help people and and just give a look into like the process uh that I had growing up. But yeah, more so than anything just super super proud of my my pops and it's yeah I'm happy for him. >> Do you think it shows more a glimpse of of who you are? Maybe the outside though that people don't really get to intimately see. Do you feel like that it shows you in that kind of light? >> Yeah. Yeah, I'd say so. Again, obviously a lot of childhood stuff, a lot of stuff that Yeah. You know, it's uh uh yeah, stuff that I don't really get into in here. So, um yeah. Yeah, it's it's cool for something like that to be out and uh yeah, just happy for my pops. How much harder has has the slow starts both to the beginning of the season and in a lot of games made it on you guys offensively and as a team to to come back in the season and to come back in those games? >> Yeah. Well, it's a tough league um you know uh across the across the league. You know, if you're you're not trying, you know, if you're not taking advantage of of every snap, of every opportunity, every quarter, whatever it may be, um you know, you it's hard to dig out of deficits at times. Um, so, you know, obviously that's not something we we ever want to do. But also, we understand that, you know, it's we we hope so, but it's it's tough if everything just goes perfectly um from play one to last play for, you know, however many games we get. Uh, we understand it's it's an adversity league. So, um, again, it's not something you ever want to be accustomed to. We we've we've taken that challenge. Um, and, you know, we want to make sure we have goals, but also, you know, we want to make sure we react. You know, that's part of something that's a good aiming point for us, but football's football. um it's part of it and uh however you know things are we can't you know we can't tuck our tail if things don't go our way in any aspect uh start middle finish anything like that so um you know that that that's part of the game and I'm excited for our our journey >> guys has talked a lot this offseason about your pre-nap operation are there specific things you identified that you feel like you you've made strides in or you're better at now than you were a year ago this time >> yeah uh ju just having more urgency um you know we've talked about um some of whether it be motion timing, just getting getting lined up a little quicker. Um you know, when we're sending motions, um being able to diagnose things a little quicker and uh you know, have have have confidence in that uh and you know, go with my instinct when we do have alerts and checks, being able to get in and out of those quicker, concise communication, uh verbally, all that stuff. That's stuff that, uh kind of coach challenged me with and us with as offense. And I think that's brought the best out of us out of me. Um you know, obviously now it's time for that to translate. um you know to to Sundays which is the next step but I think everyone's done a great job of adjusting to that um you know accepting that challenge and yeah now we have to maintain it. >> I know you're not one to look to the past but did you ever catch yourself this off season sort of in that environment at back of America Stadium in the playoff game sort of like how much do you think about that and and what that stadium sort of became in that game the environment? Yeah, I mean of course you especially during the offseason you you miss you know you missed the sport, you missed the game and obviously that was the last memory of football for so long. Um and you know it's just the support um the atmosphere. It's the bank is going something special. Um and you know we're super grateful for the community, for the fans, for the the Carolinas showing up and making it that way. And um you know we we know that's what they bring to to a game uh for all of us you know uh you know making it harder on the opponents. Um, so you know, we're excited for that again, you know, this weekend. >> Bryce, I know we've asked other players this, but I don't we ever asked you this. Do do you put down individual goals like even if you keep them yourself for, you know, before a season? And if you want to share those, you can, but I mean, I'm just curious if you do or don't. >> Yeah, I don't. Um, you know, I I'm not a long-term goal guy. Um, I'm not a um, you know, for me, I'm I I I put individual goals for a practice or um, you know, I'll I'll have certain things that I'll come into a meeting with and hey, I want to make sure I get this ironed out. Um, but big picture wise, uh, just never been my approach personally. I've always been, uh, just what's tangible, what can I I know I can get done in the here and now. Um, and, uh, that's kind of just always been how my focus is. >> Can I say emphasized emphasized tried to get off to a fast start by like taking care of that at practice, like being ready right when you get out there. Have you noticed the difference with everybody? >> Yeah. Yeah, for sure. Um, you know, coach did a great job. He's kind of switched the structure of practice a little bit to um, you know, to to, you know, back that up and to try to, you know, encourage that. Um, and, you know, obviously he always sees things from a 30,000 uh, foot view, so he knows what he's doing. We trust that. Um, but also for us, you know, we have to make sure we're taking that challenge that, you know, even if if we warm up for an hour straight, uh, that has to be intense. You know, if we whatever it is, if it's Andy, you know, we just have to have that mentality and coach has done a great job of instilling that in different ways. And again, now it's on us to accept that challenge. All the guys are up for it. They're doing a great job. So, uh, you know, we're excited for, uh, an opportunity to to let it play out. >> Appreciate you guys.

title: Bijan Robinson, Kendal Daniels and other Falcons speaks to media post-practice | Press Conference
text: How you feeling heading Sunday? >> Feel great. Um, you know, pre preseason is is fun. Just, you know, to get the the training camp going, but, you know, now now's the real the real thing. And, you know, it's I was just telling uh I was just telling Drake, I was like, when the when the fields turned this way on the field, that means it's it's time to go. So, uh, so I'm I'm I know we're all really excited. I'm really excited to get going. >> Offensively, I mean, how how happy are you with the way where you guys kind of are right now. >> Yeah, I'm I'm very happy. Um, you know, now it's just, you know, we have the product. We've we've been doing it. Uh, it's been looking great in practice, but, uh, now it's time to, you know, go go put it to show and go have fun doing it. And I know Tommy and, you know, everybody on the offensive staff is is ready to, you know, get to the real to the real game, get to the to the real play calling and so we can go just go out there and execute it. But I know for us as a offense, like we're just we're just anxious, man, like to just go out there and just, you know, put it put the product to the to work. >> How do you assess? >> Oh, go ahead. >> When when Tua got here, he mentioned you reached out to him like right away. >> Why was it important to you that? >> I mean, one, it's just it's important to welcome somebody uh and make them feel welcome um as soon as it happens. And I know that, you know, there's a lot of things that go into that. Um, when you join a new team and, you know, when you enter a new a new building. So, you know, for me, like as one of the leaders of the team, um, and just as a brother, uh, of him, you know, I just wanted to make sure that he he just felt comfortable and knowing that like whatever he needed, you know, I got him. Or if he needed like a direction or something like that in in this building, you know, I got him. So, you know, I think it's always good to just make make your teammates feel welcome. um him or anybody else that comes up in here uh because you know we're a family and and they got to feel that family atmosphere you know right away. >> Yeah. How do you assess the uh Steeler defense? People make a big deal of the edges but Patrick Queen sitting there in the middle at linebacker. >> Yeah. I think I think they're really good. Uh respect all all the guys on that defense. You know, they've been playing this game a long time. So, you know, they have one of the best greatest, you know, one of the best defensive players to play the game. and and TJ Watt and just everybody else on that defense that that makes it go. But like you said, I respect Patrick Queen a lot as a linebacker and I can't wait to, you know, go up against him. Um, you know, I think he, you know, is a part of making that defense, you know, what it is and and making it go these these past years. So, you know, I'm ready to go out there and, you know, I love playing against, you know, good great linebackers. Um, so I think it's going to be a it's going to be a fun matchup. >> What's the biggest thing that you have to go through? didn't play in the preseason games and the speed in the games is different and now you're going to be in game speed and you know they're going to be tearing at the ball and all that kind of stuff. What do you remind yourself and what do you have to go through to get yourself ready to play game speed? Yeah, I mean it's it all starts in practice and I appreciate you know Kevin and you know I know that I didn't play the game but um he makes sure he makes sure that the defense is always ripping up the ball thinning up um like it's a like it's a game tackle and you know me making moves uh or getting vertical in real time. So, you know, I know that I haven't played preseason in a long time, but always just make sure that in practice, every single rep that I take is a game rep. And, you know, I'm I'm looking at the defenders and I'm, you know, trying to pick angles and trying to pick quarters and and just slowing the game down in real time in practice because I know when the when the game comes, um, you know, that's when all my things that I practice and all my cues, uh, come to life, um, out there. anybody that's watched you thinks the game moves pretty slow anyway based on what you've shown us the first three seasons. How much has it continued to slow down for you and seeing coverage and seeing how teams want to play? >> Yeah, it's uh it's it's been a great process. Um you know, me and my coach talk coach Petri and like in college that first year in my freshman year the game was fast, everything was moving at full speed and then my second third year like it it completely slowed down for me. And then same thing in the NFL. um you know that first year like I was trying to let the game slow down for me and then the second third year like you know that's what I'm that's what I'm trying to elevate into reading all the coverages reading first second level reads um in the run and pass game and then you know a big thing that I did last year that I started last year was just knowing where the free hitter is every single play like making sure I know where that free hitter is for every run uh for every run run play because it just it just helped my game out so much and and it completely slowed slowed the game down for me because I know every single play where the guy I got to make a miss or the guy I got to break a tackle on, you know, I know where he's at before it even starts. So, that's good. >> A lot of guys say it feels like, you know, they get that first hit, first sack, and then they feel like, "All right, it's good time for you." Like, what is kind of that moment feel like, "All right, like I'm back." >> Um, I think I think it's the first hit, too. Um, or like when a big play happens, you know, I know that, you know, that's that's the start of the season right there. Um, but it's it's either a pass protection or or like like I said, like if that big play happens or just the first tackle. I know that first tackle I'm like, "All right, I'm I'm ready to go." Like, let's let's do this. >> What was your confidence? Um, what's your confidence in Tua as the starting quarterback? Obviously, you know, he >> Yeah. What do you think he can do week one with this team? >> I think he'll he, you know, he has he came from a lot of talent, so, you know, it's it's cool that he has a lot of talent around him. Um, and I think it's going to make him a lot a lot more confident knowing that. And, you know, me and two will talk all the time on the field and we talk about, you know, angles, where to get the ball out, like when to get the ball out. Um, but it's just him having that trust in us that when when he puts the ball in our hands, like that's when we, you know, got to use our God-given talents and and make it happen. Um, because that's that's what we're supposed to do. and you know he he's aware of it and you know we talk but I know he talks to all the receivers you know all the tight ends like so it's it's cool that he can give us the ball at anywhere on the field and and trust us to to make a play um and you know I'm not really big on like catch possession catching like it's you got to you got to try to try to get in the end zone so you know I think he he knows that's where that's what we're about >> says the quarterback's best friend is a great run game so do you take like a little bit of pride of knowing that you can maybe take a little bit of pressure off on him if like you guys are outstanding that game. Like how do you >> Yeah, absolutely. That's that's the standard here. That's the standard that we set here and you know it doesn't matter who's at quarterback, you know, as long as they trust us in that run game and you know with the guys up front. Um you know obviously they they've excelled uh all of them. Um and and with with Chris and you know birds of the guards and then obviously with Jon coming in you know and knowing the standard and where he's came from you know he's he's won the championships. He knows what it looks like. So um it's it's it's a cool thing with and even with news um and then obviously you know the iron man Jake but uh those guys are the guys that make it go and you know I I my job is to make them look good but then to has to know like that's what we're here to do so it can make it easier on him. um in the passing game. >> What's it been like just for this team and for you hearing so much external noise about the quarterback position here because I know you obviously get so much national attention when you do these interviews and it's like one of the first things they kind of ask you. What's it been like for you to kind of navigate that situation? >> Yeah, I just I just make sure I'm here to support them. Um you know, no matter what cuz I know the past like couple years, you know, it was quarterback competition. Um, but I I know for my job is to make sure that they're they're supported whether I talk to other people or talk to other media or stuff like that. Um, so they can so they can just feel confident going into it no matter who's you know who the guy is obviously is to us. So like making sure that he's you know where he needs to be mentally. Um but yeah, I I told them like I'm just here to serve man. um and to make sure that you guys are at your your best your best self and make sure Tua goes out there Sunday, you know, super confident in all of us and just ready to go. >> And is that part of it too? Like having so many position players around Tua that have can kind of help enable that success. Is that something that you guys have taken on like okay we can maybe silence those conversations externally if we are able to do our jobs? >> Absolutely. like you know the the execution is is where the fun's at and when we start executing at a high level and then really nobody can say nothing and all you can do is just watch. Um but that's that's on us to to make sure that whatever play call that they have like we executed at a at a really high level. Um because then then when the noise gets silenced like you know what else what else can you say all all we can do is just put in the work. So it's it's everything's on us. You know we have to go in the game prepare. We have to go in the game ready to uh execute at at all costs, run or pass. Um and then that's that's when everything else takes care of itself. >> Couple more. Along those lines, uh Cam Hayward was on the Rich Eisen show earlier this week and he said, you know, you take John Robinson, you combine with Bill Callahan, the offensive line, and he said, you know, it's going to keep a lot of people up at night. Do you think that's kind of the ceiling for what this group can do? >> Yeah, I mean, there's, you know, obviously we got to go out there and do it. Um, you know, I I felt I felt very confident in this off seasonason and and you know, this this run game, man. Um, you know, obviously Bill is is the legend and, you know, it's it's cool learning from him because, you know, I've I've learned so many things that I haven't even, you know, thought of. Um, but he he's had so many great running backs. He has so many great run games, so many great experiences with with the O line. Um, yeah, I know he's like the best the best that it gets when it comes to, you know, coaching the offensive line, uh, in the run game, but, you know, it's for me it wasn't even about that. Like, I I admire him as a as a coach, as a person, but, you know, just just seeing how smart he is and and learning from a lot of different schemes, a lot of different ways of getting the ball in space, like it's it's really cool. Um, seeing the things that he does for for this offense. >> You some new wrinkles to what you guys are going to be doing in the ground game. What excites you about the prospect of what you guys are going to bring to the table in the ground game this year? >> You know, there's a lot of possibilities of, you know, things that we can do. Um, you know, with Burge, like dude, dude is funny. You know, he he was smiling at me the other day and and we had a we had a run in practice and he was just like he's like, "B like I ain't seen this before." And I was like, "Bro, I I know, man. Like I I'm so excited, too." Um, but I I I could tell like, you know, everybody's so committed to it. Um, you know, and it and it just sets up the pass, sets up everything else, sets up the energy in on the defense, like, you know, that that that's what gets everybody going on the team. Um, and just being physical and and doing it for four quarters. But yeah, I'm like anxious now cuz we we ran it so long in in practice now and I just want to just go out there in the game and, you know, put it, you know, put it to life. Um, all right, Kendall. I I know that we we talked to you periodically on and off throughout training camp just about like, >> you know, really asserting yourself and and really fighting for for a spot. And I know the dev truck came out yesterday and you're you're the guy alongside Divine. What did that mean to you? And and what do you feel like you showed over the course of the last couple of months to to >> um It's very exciting. You know, it was good to see that of I wouldn't say I mean hard work paying off. you know, the the long summer that I had, the injury that I had to go through and and the combine and everything. Seeing the long road it took to get here, you know, it was a long road. The offseason really wasn't offseason, you know, trying to find a job and then you get in here and a whole bunch of older guys and then you you work your tail off and you just put your head down and work and then you're told that you're going to be the starter and then it kind of restarts everything. You know, you don't you're not at the finish line yet. So you still have to have a lot more to go, but it was very exciting. >> How much did I talked to Divine before you came out here, how much did his mentorship, getting to know him and seeing how he plays really help you along in the process? >> Um, it helps me a lot, you know, being out there to be able to talk to somebody that's been able >> to play a long time and play the position and, you know, he helps me a lot and he's able to make the calls and he's the green dot when we're out there. So, helps me calm down and um really just focus in on what I have and he's talking to the defensive lineman and all that. So, it's been good to be able to hear him and how he communicates and how he communicates with the back end. So, um I'm just there to help him and we're there to help each other. >> I would imagine you guys are probably one of the taller and >> yeah, >> linebacker players in the league. How much does that help you guys do you think? Uh, it probably helps us a lot just be able to, you know, move out in space and be able to move all around and get on the line of scrimmage and be able to move around in space and, you know, use our length to our advantage. It's it's good because you can't really target either or or if we're like in a a different package, either of us can go guard the tight end or anything. So, it's it's fun to be able to have somebody like that. >> But, it'll be fun to see how we play through the season. >> In Miami, it looked like you and Harold were kind of playing in playing out a lot. Is that the way you think it'll be in season? You going to play, you know, all three downs? You have >> I don't know. I haven't even I haven't even looked at the the first thing I saw on the dep chart was when y'all saw it. You know, I just out there doing what I'm supposed to do, doing what I'm told and and whatever they asked me to do or ask me and Parker to do, I'm sure that he'll he'll think the same way. Just go out there and and do what we're told to do. >> How do you guys compliment each other, do you think? Uh, >> I feel like we compliment each other a lot, you know, just because we we're entertainable parts and we bring different things to the game and, you know, we're one two punch. So, just being able to um whenever we're out on the field, just be able to bring different things but also the same things because we played the same position in college. So, I feel like that'll help both of us. around the film to watch Pittsburgh. >> What are they what are they shown you and how are they dangerous? >> I mean a guy Aaron Rogers. >> I mean that's that's that there. I mean he's played a long time and he's uh probably one of the smartest guys um in the history of the football game, you know. So, it's crazy that it's my first football uh NFL game, but it's been great to be able to watch him and have an extra week to be able to get to uh watch him and see how he operates and all the checks that he has and all the little things. You know, it's a different I've never had to go up against a quarterback like this just because he's so different. I mean, he controls the whole the tempo of the game. He never lets the game rush him. You know, you just got to go out there and play defense and just really be on top of your game. How impressive it is that he's been able to sustain such a long >> crazy. It's crazy. I couldn't imagine playing. >> How What year is it for him? >> 20 years. >> I couldn't imagine. Yeah. My body will give out ways. >> Maybe 20 years. >> Yeah. It's just crazy to me. Like it's crazy. >> And how old are you? >> 23. >> Yeah. Yeah. >> Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Facts. Um, we were talking to Kevin earlier this week and he was just kind of joking about how he could watch, you could watch so much film on Pittsburgh because of the fact they have a new staff coming in and go back and watch some things that Dallas was doing. Green Bay back in the day with Aaron Rogers and Michael. Um, what were kind of some of the keys that you were honing in on during your film study over the last couple of weeks? probably the same thing as coach just it's a lot you know because you have to go back and watch so many games and it's really hard to because if you pick one game that they did or pick one season and then they don't come out and do that then it's like you wasted time so you have to it's a broad uh bird's eye view of it all but you have to also have to see the same stuff that they did over and over so it's kind of hard to say what I'm looking at you just kind of try to find things that they've done over and over and carried over and try to do those things and coaches do a great job of giving us uh things to look at. So, just taking what they have for us and and not looking at stuff that probably they probably won't run. >> To that point, Brick, I've talked to Brick about this before where he's sometimes like >> they can go out and they can do what they want to. We have to be about us a little bit. Does that kind of when you go into week one and you have a new staff, is that kind of how you're approaching it? Yeah, you have to go out there and if we go out there and try to game plan and scheme up stuff that they do and we forget about our rules ball and just everything that we've been doing, honing in on our defense and, you know, flying around and running around, if we lose sight of what we're good at, then it'll be hard to to play any team. So, you have to be able to uh be where your feet are. Um, control what you can control. And also, you still have to go out there and and scheme against a team, but you also have to look in the mirror. >> I believe this morning, I'd asked Kevin about about you and Harold, Zack, EV, this collection of you guys being able to play early. Yeah. >> Why do you think you are? Like, why as a group do you think you guys are really ready for this? Um, as a group I feel like we came in with the mentality that and when we first got here, Matt Ryan told us like don't come in thinking that you have like a year to to learn the defense. Like you're going to play and you're going to help us win. So he told all of the rookies that and kind of just take that, you don't take that lightly. You know, you have to you have to be ready for the opportunity and just, you know, being mature about it and not being what they call a rookie. you know, you're a rookie, but at the end of the day, you have to play like you're not. So, >> I've long heard the idea that the last year of college and then the whole draft process and then rookie camp and trying to acclimate everything is like the longest, hardest year of a guy's life. Is there a way you can put into words how challenging the last 12 months have been for you? >> Last 12 months, >> going back to like beginning camp, college camp, week one college. >> Yeah, it's been a long Yes, it's been a long time. I try not to think of how long it's been. I try to put in categories and try to put the last season then training and then OTAAS and try not to put in one big call. I've been gone for 12 months but I've been gone for a month. That's how I think about it with training camp. So, and now it restarts cuz we had the weekend off. So, now it's the week one and try not to think of the combine and how long we've been going. I mean, it's football. I mean, if you're tired of playing football, then it probably ain't for you. So just being able to fall in love with the game and just, you know, taking the opportunity that the coach has given you. >> I know I asked you about Kendall, but Perk and kind of the role that he could carve out for himself as well. >> Uh just a young group of fast linebackers. I think uh if we play fast, just get to the ball, that's going to be hard for a lot of offenses. So I'm excited to see them boys fly around. >> I know that today was probably a big day in terms of like getting the cards out at practice and everything like that. What have you kind of learned about this Pittsburgh offense? Obviously Aaron Rogers being who Aaron Rogers is, but what are kind of some of the the notes that you've taken? >> Uh A-Rod's a great quarterback. Uh I think they want to get to their weapons. Uh sometimes quick games, sometimes deep down the field attacking our corners on one-on- ones. So uh we just got to be on it and uh guess we'll see. >> Yeah. Um and then one more question for me. Uh Kevin was talking Kevin Spansky was talking a little bit about how much film you could pull from like all of these new coaches and what the Steelers did last year, what Mike McCarthy's done before. Like >> how did you go into this week in terms of the prep and the film study for for what you're going to potentially see on Sunday? >> Um like you said, uh a lot of film to watch. Uh I went to back when they were together in Green Bay, watched a little film there. um he's been at OC I think at Dallas. So just just watching different teams uh light teams defensively wise. So I like to watch Houston against those teams just to see what you know we would look like against them most likely and certain defenses at least. So uh just watching that film I think we'll be in a good spot. >> What talked about Rogers said they got a pretty potent running game of what you seen from them and how you want to prepare. >> Oh yeah for sure. I feel like they want to run the ball set the tone. Uh hopefully uh we just got to fight back, you know, uh not letting them set that tone, make them one-dimensional hopefully and just go from there. >> Thoughts about your role um and your guys around you, what you want to do. There's some questions about people trying to break in for pass rushing and how important that's going to be against Rogers to set the stage for the guys behind you in the secondary. Talk about more pressure for the guys in the middle. >> Uh I don't think so. I think we're all family out here, so uh we we work together as a team. Uh we support each other. Uh, I know the back end got me, I got the back end. Same with the front. Um, I back them guys up. I let them eat, do what they do, and I told them, "I back you up and go from there." >> Avon, how are you just mentally, physically feeling going into your first week one of the NFL? >> Um, mentally and physically feel good. I'm ready. I'm locked in. >> Does it feel any different like preparing for week one compared to all of training camp? And just how's the energy feel? >> No, it's it's it don't feel different. You know, same mindset. >> It don't feel different. Sorry. >> It looks like you're going to like it. >> Can you ask the question again? >> Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. How does it feel? That's very nice here. How does it feel different just going into week one compared to training camp and everything out? How's the energy feel and everything? >> Yeah. It feel the same. You know, same mindset, same field, study. Um just time to go play now. All the work I put in, just time for it. >> What's the conversation like with your brother? Like, will you guys get ready together? Will you drive in separately? Like what does that Sunday look like? >> Man, we ready. Are you excited to be getting to have like a this first week one experience with him again on the same team? >> Yeah, man. It's it's a blessing. It's a blessing, you know, one of one, but you know, we we talking. We we not with each other outside of here. You know, I go my way, he go his way, but you know, we got the same mindset. We both watch the fan. We both locked in. >> How confident does this defense feel just going into a week one, especially when you're going up against a Hall of Famer like Aaron Roger? >> Yeah, we confident. We confident. We ready. We've been preparing for a long time. It's time to go show it. What was the team's reaction when they found out that uh Tua was going to be starting and what's just the confidence in Tua under center? >> Um just everybody was just excited for Tua >> and it's time for two to go go show the show the world why >> we got him. >> How's the What's more of the challenge opening up week one on the road compared to being able to have that at home? What challenges does that present? >> None for us. Just I I think crowd probably the only difference same mindset with us like we home away same same energy. Go out there and ball. >> Avon talk about Aaron Rogers and going up against week one against Aaron Rogers. One of the the best to do it. We were talking to Kendall and he was joking. He was like I don't remember a time when Aaron Rogers wasn't in the league. Um, when you think about Aaron Rogers, like what what comes to mind and how excited are you that like your first opportunity to play in that game is against some of the best? >> Yeah, Kendall was right. >> He been in the league for 21 years. I'm 21 years old. So, but um you said >> Yeah, just like your your thoughts on being able to to go up against him and what it's been like to really study him this week as your >> Yeah, it's a blessing to go against A-Rod, you know, just somebody I've been watching since I've been growing up. So now I get to go against him. So you know I'm ready. I'm ready for the look at him in his eye and ready to go ball. That's really it. >> You didn't get a lot of preseason reps. So how excited are you just kind of let loose in week one? >> I'm excited. I'm excited. Um been grinding for it, been training, been doing a lot of practice. So it's time for it. You're about to get your first professional stamp. And I know it's been a thousand times, but truly, how crazy like is it that you know your brother is going to be right there on the same field, first professional snap, uh, at home just opening up all this just how how crazy is that? Like do you realize like you you've lived a lot of people's dreams probably? Oh, >> it's crazy. Like it's just crazy just looking to my right or my left and seeing him out there like >> Yeah. you know, just this time last year, we we call each other to talk about football, how I did in college, how he did out here in the league. Now we teammates, so it's a blessing. Um during the game, I'm just I'm just keep my head straight and we just going to ball together. Just something we talked about since we was growing up. If we ever play each other, it's going to be a movie. >> What's uh your pregame like routine? What's kind of is there a certain meal you always have to have or what does it look like getting ready for game day? I don't. It's just whatever they got in the hotel, I eat it. But, you know, put my put my headphones on, listen to my music, and right mindset to go. >> What kind of music? Like, who do you have to listen to? Who >> Little DJ Young Boy, King V. >> Yeah. >> Appreciate it. Thank you. >> You play Nickel in Clemson? >> I did. >> How much versus outside? >> I play I play like every third down in Clemson. >> Okay. So, you're you're pretty comfortable there. Yeah, for sure. >> Um, Billy, tell us a little bit about finally getting the the go-ahad to to come out here in practice. I know you just got it here in the last couple of new weeks, but what was that first day like back? >> Uh, it felt so good back playing football. Um, a lot of people are asking me today how I felt being back out there for the first time. Um, and I feel good healthwise. Um, I just I feel like I haven't took a snap in 9 months. So, um, you know, that stuff normally comes back pretty quick, about a couple practices, but I feel good. >> What's kind of your acclamation period kind of looking like? I know Coach Deansky said did some individual drills last week in terms of what what kind of does your ramp up look like for you? >> Yeah. Um, yeah, obviously it started with um, you know, just being able to get to the point to where I can do DB work. So, a lot of just forward sprinting, straight backward pedaling, then some change of direction stuff, some sled pushes, and then finally getting into where I'm comfortable enough to do DB drills of backpedaling and breaking right back downhill. Um, and you know, uh, it's just been a progressive building block ever since. So, just going from that to, um, hopping in with the DBs and their indie to be back with the group. Um, and then, you know, to today um, taking just reps here and there. And so, um, just a a slow building block, um, but we'll get there eventually. >> Really the process of being patient and having to wait your turn to come back to practice to play football. What did you learn about yourself throughout this whole journey? >> Uh, I learned that there's a lot more to life than football. Um, I'm a guy who ever since I was a young kid, I worked the hardest on every team that I was on. Um, and never took a day off. So, um I kind of look at this injury as giving me a step back from all my hard work, all the things that I've done and u just learning life is more uh than just football. Um so just being able to go on vacation places, see different things, try different foods, all types of things like that. Um but ultimately being back now, I've realized that I've missed it so much. >> You've gotten to watch obviously from the sideline. What makes you so eager aside from just getting out there, but what makes you so eager about joining this particular defense? um just how I how my presence is felt out there. Um obviously, I mean, in my opinion, I haven't done nothing, but um when I'm out there, everybody feels me. Um and so I can't wait to um mesh that in with Jesse Bates X, um you know, Mike Hughes, even Avon Terrell, AJ Terrell, um and the linebackers, too. >> Do you feel like you'll be ready to play >> Uh I'm ready right now, but um still getting there. U still got to build some confidence with it out there. Um, but we'll see where we go. >> Okay. >> What was the hardest, you know, part about the last nine months? >> Um, I'd say the early stages, not even being able to walk. Um, being a pro alete and now I can't even get up in the middle of the night to go to the restroom without using a scooter or being in the shower and I have to sit on the ground. Like, um, those things and never being injured before and seeing what that was like. Uh, it brought me back to ground zero. But, uh, I honestly didn't even know I'd make it to this point to where I'm back practicing and here I am. >> Billy, how proud are you of Kendall Daniels? >> Uh, very proud. You know, I've heard a lot of things about him at Oklahoma. Obviously, we didn't play together, but I wish I played with him watching him. Um, but just another guy who comes in and about his business. Um, take advantage of this opportunity. >> We talked a lot about Go ahead, Alison. What do you feel like you need to see for yourself in order to be ready to go for game action? like what do you feel like is still maybe missing? >> M I just need the live reps. Um just getting going live, you know, versus Drake London, Zack Branch, um OZ, all those guys. Um even coming up and defeating blocks on Charlie and Kyle, uh things like that. Just getting live reps and then I feel I'll be back in the group. We saw you every single day on the sideline during training camp and uh Kevin Space has talked a lot about just like the mental reps and making sure guys who can't really be out there just yet get those. What was kind of your process in in getting those in in in practice and making sure that you're mentally stimulated through it? >> Yeah. Um always just following my position. So just always backing up behind the nickel, knowing the play call, seeing the play, seeing the motions, whatever it is. Uh but also conversations that I've had with Brick um our DC of just you know taking this time to learn the defense as a whole. Uh take this time to learn safety if needed um and things like that.

title: Quarterback Tua Tagovailoa Week 1 Media Availability | Wednesday, September 9th | Press Conference
text: when when and how did you learn about, you know, being that guy >> in QB1? >> Uh, we learned it on Monday. So, Kev just just sat me down, then he had a conversation with everyone else, and then we went into the quarterback room and he had a conversation with all of us. >> How did you react to it? >> I mean, I'm I'm very blessed, very fortunate, obviously. um you know, playing in the NFL, this is this is what you want to do to be able to to to start. Um unfortunately, there's only one person that can do that at our position. Um needless to say, you know, I I I have a great relationship with with MP. Uh I have a great relationship with Coupe. I have a great relationship with Jack. And you know, as I said, that's it's it's just how the position um works in this league. So, um, love love our guys in our quarterback room. Um, and I love the relationships that we've been able to build throughout OTAAS and then throughout training camp going into this first weekend of season. >> What does it mean to you personally in your own personal journey to get back to that KB1 spot? >> Well, I I would say it it's a blessing. Once again, it it's not something that I take for granted. Um, you know, when something gets taken away from you, you start to to process everything and think of all the things that you could have changed. You know, just me sort of looking back with my time in Miami, um, things I could have done better and things like that. So, it it's it's a blessing. >> What do you think you could have done better? >> Oh, there's a lot of things I think I could have done better. Turning the ball over, could have played better. Uh, my decision- making. uh you know from prior years in terms of last year just wasn't good. >> How are you feeling about your kind of command of the offense and and the operation going into this event? [snorts] >> Yeah, it it feels good. Uh, again, just out there in practice, we're we're trying to simulate overly communicating, making sure we're we're knowing where we need to be, communicating, communicating, communicating out there, and um, you making sure we simulate game-like scenarios, game-like feel, game-like situations every time we step out there on the practice field. >> Tua, going off of what you said about, you know, what you could have done better, you get this opportunity now to be QB1. How do you mentally approach Sunday and what are the expectations you put on yourself when entering the game against the Steelers? >> Yeah, the expectations I put on myself every time is to go out there and score one more point than the opposing team. Um, you know, and for me that entails me doing my job, making sure I'm getting into the right looks, if we have run plays, getting into the right looks if we have pass plays and vice versa based off of what the defense is giving us. So that's my expectation to go out there, do exactly what I need to do to help our team win and that's it. >> I'm curious about your philosophy as a quarterback in the league. You know, seventh year for you for Aaron Rogers. You know, he's 42 now and sometimes it's not necessarily about getting there, but longevity. So what's your philosophy as a quarterback and that longevity that you're starting to see with some guys? Well, I think my philosophy, you know, I I would say first off, Aaron Rogers is is just a different type of human being in terms of his longevity. Uh playing at a high level for how long he's he's played um the position. I mean, I I watched him when when I was real young. I mean, elementary school, middle school, high school, and then uh you know, a couple years back being able to play against him and then last year as well. But I I would say my philosophy is is to take it like a year at a time. Not to think of what's going to happen next year or how long I want to play. Longevity uh for me is is is not a thing. I just trying to live right now within the present. >> You started your entire career with the Dolphins and now you're getting a chance with the Falcons. So like how refreshing is it to kind of get this new start, new team, and be able to do it week one? >> Yeah, it it's very refreshing. Again, I as I said, it's it's a blessing. That's that's the best word I could describe uh the scenario and the situation that that I'm in. >> Do you feel like you have something to prove or do you want to prove something to people outside of yourself in this building? >> I would say I I I I don't think I for myself and and what I believe, I don't have anything to prove to anyone outside, but it's to prove to my own self that I can continue to play at a high level. >> Well, you kind of told them, you know, you're going to be starting quarterback. Is it more of a week toeek thing for you or do they say it's your job until further notice? That's how they describe it. >> Yeah, Kev didn't say any of that. Um, how I how I'm taking it is I got to go with this dayto-day and you know that's out of my control. What I can control is how I prepare, how I go out there, how I play, how I perform and that's that's all I can do. Each week in the NFL obviously presents a challenge, but when you look at the Steelers defense, what stands out to you? >> Their front seven. I would say their front seven. Uh not to say that they're they're, you know, they're they're guys that they have at corner and safeties not good, but their front seven I I think really gets those guys going. And then from there, you got really good guys in the back end. Uh and then I got a really good relationship with Jaylen Ramsey. Um, you know, I know a lot of people know Jaylen, but great player, great person, and I'm excited to go back up against them. So, um, in your experience, how often do you see things in week one that are new to the team that that you're playing where, you know, your preparation or and they throw a new wrinkle out there to you, is that more common in week one than any other season? >> I would say yes and and no. uh just depending on on the coordinator. All we can do is look at their preseason games, look at their their past with how they've called games. Outside of that, you got to go out there knowing what what the looks are going to be and reacting to any of the new looks. And if they get us, they get us. You come to the sideline, you adjust, and then you you continue to go from there. Continue playing. So then do you almost like prepare for your reactionary plan anymore going into the week? Like here's how we go about adjusting because we do expect to maybe see some things that we're going to have to adjust to. >> Of course. Of course. That's exactly how how you go about it. Go about the prime the primary looks in which we want certain plays and then reactions off of not getting those primary looks. >> Yeah. Coach Kevin said the quarterback's got an early look at the game plan and he wanted to make sure it was to your strengths. Do you feel that he uh was able to do that? >> Yeah, for sure. Uh it was a collection of all of us being able to sit down and and talk talk through, you know, what we seen within their defense, things that we like, things that we feel comfortable running, things like that. Bjan kind of said he felt like it's part of his job to kind of take a little bit of pressure off of you by giving you a strong run game. So, how nice is it to know the weapons that you have on offense like Bjan and Drake and Kyle and things like that? >> Yeah. Well, I appreciate him saying that because I feel the total opposite like, you know, kind of want to help help get the run game going by allowing our pass game to, you know, get into a rhythm, get into it flow. We were talking to Mike a few weeks ago and he said that in the quarterback room you guys have like a a saying uh something goes wrong just it. Yeah. Can you describe what that means is like pan is kind of like a security valve. >> Yeah that's you you basically said it. He's just the security valve like >> oh these guys aren't open. Where's Ban Bit? >> To uh coach Spans talked a lot about all security and and protecting the football. How do you kind of walk that line between mitigating risk but also then taking the chances when they're available to you? >> Yeah, I would say just preparation. Just that that's all it is at the end of the day. Preparing for for looks if we don't get certain looks, knowing where your checkowns are, your outlets, things like that. Just being able to keep our offense on the field, keep the ball moving. >> You got limited reps in the preseason and now it's like you're full go now in week one. What's kind of like I guess the difference between like going full goal and easing into it like not too hard. I guess >> I would say I would say playing seven years it's never never really put any thought into sort of ramping it up or or just having to now is go time. uh, you know, I think it's more about how comfortable you can feel with the game plan that sort of gives you anxiety or or or kind of stresses you out a little bit. But, you know, as as that gentleman in back there asked the question with with Kev, you know, we we met earlier this week and we got to talk about uh things that we like, things that we didn't like, things that we want to run and and vice versa to that. So, it's just a week of preparation. >> Yeah. >> Anything else? >> All right. Thanks. >> All right. Thanks, guys. >> Thank you. Hey, hey, hey. [music]

title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski Week 1 Media Availability | Wednesday, September 9th | Press Conference
text: All right, good to see everybody. Uh Wednesday, work week. So, a really big day for our football team. As you start the game plan and uh spend a lot of time understanding our opponent, who we have a ton of respect for, uh and we start to introduce the base game plan to our players. Uh Coach McCarthy does a great job. Somebody that I have a insane amount of respect for how he's done it. Um he put together an outstanding staff there in Pittsburgh. I know a bunch of their coaches. I think they're terrific at what they do. So, it's going to be a very well-coached team, a very sound football team. Obviously, offensively, with Aaron Rodgers, who I've seen quite a bit in my my time as a coach and you know, I'm he's he still can make every single throw. He's got as as good an arm as anybody I've ever seen live. Um it's unbelievable. So, noth- none of that has has fallen off at all. He can beat you with his mind. He's just a terrific player. Uh they they have ways they can get the ball on the perimeter to big, physical, fast receivers. Uh a really good run game with some backs that I really think are are excellent. Um defensively, Patrick Graham is a terrific defensive coordinator. I've competed against him quite a bit. Uh you have to be ready really for anything with PG. He he he has a defense that can get in and out of any front, in and out of any coverage, and they're sound and they uh there's really great thought behind what they're doing. And then, special teams, Danny Crossman has done it for a long time in this league. Um does a really, really good job keeping you um making sure that you as as a opponent are on top of everything. Uh and they have excellent special teams players. As you watch the tape, it really jumps out at you. So, uh big day for our football team. What happens is you get a install here for base game plan, offense, defense, special teams. Uh we'll have a walk-through here in a minute. Go out to the practice field. Uh you know, hit all the first and second down type of things on a Wednesday. Work against cards, so it's again the first time not the first time did it in the preseason, but uh one of the first exposures to running practice on cards. So, you'll see the scout team out there looking at the cards, running a play as you prepare your team for your opponent. So, there's there's a way to do that well, and that's going to be important for us to both do that at this walk-through coming up here and then at practice.
