Really to prepare ourselves for this great challenge, and it is a great challenge. Going on the road to a a a great environment. Division reigning division champs. So, we're excited about the opportunity, but we also understand there's a lot of work that needs to go into it. But, with that I'll take any questions. >> You coached against Rodgers, I guess, way back when, right? Like early 2010s, even prior to that, I guess. So, I mean, how much of the guy that he is now is he or how much of the guy was he from that is he still now? And I mean, is there anything you can lean on from however many times you had to coach against him now? >> Well, you know, I wouldn't say as a young offensive coach I wasn't doing much coaching per se against him. I was I was there to, you know, I saw and witnessed some unbelievable things that he's able to do in terms of running right, throwing left, across your body, on the money 40 yards down the field. You know, just somebody that I again I've had a front-row seat. Alex Van Pelt was a coach there in Green Bay as well. So, knows him well, knows the game well. So, just he is I mean, he's a Hall of Famer. I don't you guys don't need to hear it from me. You guys know how great he is, and and we respect him. We respect the the the player that he is and and the ways in which he can beat you. >> Going off of that, Kevin, I'm curious, what is your philosophy on seeing quarterbacks in the league when it comes to longevity? Sometimes with a younger generation it's about getting there, but the reality is sometimes it's about staying there, and Aaron Rodgers is a pretty good example. >> I think you're definitely seeing guys play into their 40s. I think Brady was really the first to do it at such a high level. So, I'm not surprised that that's becoming the norm as players take care of their bodies. and then as anybody as you guys know, any experience you get, any reps you get, you just get better as a thinker, get better as a processor. And I think at this point in his career, you're not going to fool him. You're not going to show him something that he's never seen before. You're you're just going to have to be about your business and and understand that he's a great player. He will make his plays. And and I think that's from his physical ability, but also the amount of reps that he's had at this game just make makes his processing so so elite. >> With Billy Bowman Jr. coming coming back, getting back into the full swing of things, what does kind of his acclimation period look like? Expectations for you guys with him? >> Continuing to progress. He's somebody that I've got gotten to witness first-hand how hard he has worked at this and really excited for Billy to be back practicing, you know, being part of individual periods last week and seeing him move around. And he's feeling really good. He's getting close. We'll continue to bring him along this week and see where we can get to, but that's one that we just need to monitor and see how he feels at practice, how he how he recover from those practices, but doing really really well. >> Does it make it, I guess, a little bit more challenging when you have a guy like Aaron Rodgers who's already so great, but then he's reunited with his former high coach, who we all assume will be there. So, as like a coaching perspective, how much more challenging does that make it? >> Well, I think, you know, coach McCarthy has done it at a really high level offensively at Green Bay, at Dallas. I think he's got a great offensive staff. Brian Angelico is the offensive coordinator, comes from Minnesota and can incorporate some of the things they're doing there. So, it's a really impressive group. Now, it's week one, so there's a lot of guessing in terms of what it will ultimately look like, and that's that's week one for you across the league. But we know how how good this staff is. We know how good the scheme has been in in the past. So, combining all those things, I think a lot of it is just to see what it looks like on Sunday. >> What's kind of the most important thing you want to see from Tua on Sunday? >> Yeah, I think all of our players, you know, in in week one you want to make sure that you execute at a high level and and certainly whether it's the quarterback position or otherwise in week one, what we have to do as coaches is make sure that our guys have a a really good understanding of game plans. I think there's a a uh desire by a lot of coaches to do everything in week one and and show everything you've been working on and it's just there's not enough plays. That's not just not the reality. So, uh for two and all of our players understanding what the game plan entails understanding what we're trying to attack on each play. Uh so much of that, you know, why you guys will hear me harp on Wednesday and why it's so important to work is there we put a lot on our guys' plates on Wednesday and and here's a brand new game plan. You know, fortunately the quarterbacks got a sneak peek of it yesterday and and can can digest a lot of information, but then it's also okay, now you got to take this to the walk-through here and then you got to take it to practice and then you got to put some finishing touches on it today and then oh by the way, we got third down coming tomorrow. So, there's a lot in the process that any player, particularly the quarterback, that we put on their plate. So, um it's their ability in in the week to trust in the routine and and really own the game plan if you will. >> By my count, two is going to be the 14th guy to start at quarterback for you as a head coach. At in all of that transition, do you learn something in how you prep when it's a new guy and he's new to you and you're new to him to get him ready? >> Well, I I think we're, you know, any coach, I don't care what you're coaching, you're you're only worth, you know, you're worth your salt if you're doing what your players do best and if you're leaning into what your players do best and I could tell you with working with all the quarterbacks over my career, whether they started or not, the guys uh are comfortable with certain things and not and they're not comfortable with everything. There's a bunch of concepts that Arch didn't like. Uh but what our job as coaches is to find out, all right, what in this broad uh scheme fits your eye, if you will. Um what what are what are your strengths? What can what can we lean into in your strength? So, sometimes that happens uh in a given season if you play multiple guys, you have to have those small pivots in a season. We've had to do it via injury at times and you do you can't change an offense. You can't go to the Delaware Wing T, but you can lean into certain concepts that guys see better than others. >> Kevin, I don't remember a wide receiver core being as big as this crew is. Is that what obviously challenges the opposition to do? >> Yeah, big, physical, fast. It's an outstanding group and and they're physical as blockers. They're physical with the rack with the ball in their hands. So, there's obviously you know, there's no substitute for size with that position where where guys are so physical and and can you know, be a part of contested catches, one-on-one balls, those type of things. So, it's important to understand what their skill sets are, understand what's what are the routes that you're getting from each guy and then it's a matter of being in position so that you can make a play on the ball. >> Kind of in that spot right now where a lot of you know, really young guys are in line to play a lot. Look at Harold and Kendall and Zachariah. What about this rookie class collectively has kind of prepped them to where if they have to play a lot, you think they can kind of handle it well? >> A lot of work. I mean, a lot of work. I could could count up all the meetings and count up all the walk-throughs and count up all the practices and the lifting and you name it. There's just a lot that goes into getting ready for the season. And also there's growth in the season. I think it's certainly a misnomer to think that a rookie's got it all figured out in week one. And I think all those guys will be better in week four than week one and week eight than week four and so on. I think there's just an amount of growth that can happen in season. We often talk about freshman to sophomore, you know, that jump in year two, but I think you can make strides in year one as well. And I think that's will be a testament to their work, the the work of our player development team here, the work of their coaches, to to understand that there there's a uh there's there's still a ton of work to be done even though we're just getting now into the regular season. >> You've talked about Aaron Rodgers and the level he operates at for Pittsburgh's offense. On the defensive side, there's Cam Heyward who is from down the street, and he's someone that is prone to causing some chaos at the quarterback position. What do you see in just his ability to get after the quarterback? >> Yeah, incredible player. You know, that that defense just in general that's a very good front seven. They're they're terrific players in their own right. Cam Heyward himself, again, I've seen great battles between him and Joel Bitonio. I think two future Hall of Famers. I got to watch that over a bunch of seasons just battling each other, physical. So, he's a terrific player, has not fallen off at all, I mean, at all. I think he's gotten better, which is crazy. But, just how physical he is, how good he is versus the run. Great in the pass game cuz he he can be physical, he can also get on edges, he can bat balls down. So, yeah, a terrific terrific player. >> I know like some of the starters really didn't get like that much game action in the preseason. So, when you're going into week one, like do you kind of not that they're on a rep count, but you kind of monitor them a little bit more in that first game just overall? Like >> I do think it's important as a staff to have a good feel for rotations going into week one. Sometimes you're dealing with weather early in the season as well. I don't think that'll be the case necessarily this week, but there's nerves that come into it. So, definitely being aware of of our rotations and and making sure that guys are fresh for the fourth quarter. I think it's important. >> Your message to the team heading into week one, how do you balance the excitement of a new season with the reality that you got 17 weeks to go? >> It's it's a it's something you we talk about, and and it's not my quote, but I've I've heard this quote that it's it's not a marathon, it's 17 sprints. And and I think there's great validity to that because it's it's something that every single week your best is required. And then that one ends and and you move on to the next one. And we as players and coaches definitely have the blinders on to focus just this week. And and you know, a lot of times I don't know who our opponent is the following week or the week after that. Just you pour everything you have into that opponent. And then realize that the next one's coming. And that's the NFL. That's the beauty of our league and how it's set up is they're amazing challenges every single week. >> Following Bailey's question, what challenges do does T.J. Watt present for your offense and protection? >> Yeah, that's a that's a great defense. Again, I've gotten to to compete against this defense over the years. And and there's no there's no easy out. It's it's a difficult to run. It's difficult to throw. Terrific in in the pass rush game. T.J. Watt obviously somebody that has been able to make so many plays over his career. And he's he's blessed with incredible length and power and and can run sideline to sideline. So he's just a great challenge for a for an offense. It's not it's not something where you say, "Hey, this is one guy is going to take this guy away." Or it's just one match-up. He's somebody that the entire offense has to be aware of. >> Time for a couple more? >> This attack style front that your defense runs, is this the first time you've been associated with that as a head coach? And is it something you have to get comfortable with? >> No, I mean attack front I mean you can get in the weeds a little bit on on what exactly that means. And and and in one the simplest way is you either have two gappers or you have an attack front. An attack front where it's one gappers and you're getting off the ball and and you're trying to be disruptive. Two gapping more you're playing the block and you're looking to get off of the block into either gap. We we have the ability to do both. Certainly an attack style of defense can can show up in different fronts. I was around Jim Schwartz for all these years. Jim runs an attack defense. Joe Woods as well ran an attack defense coming from San Francisco, which is where you'll see that also with coach Washburn influence from that regard. So, I think we have the ability to do both and based on calls and you know, attack while it's a one gap scheme, which is no different than a lot of teams. There's also a mentality that comes with playing that scheme. >> I know Jordan's obviously made plenty of starts before, but how valuable is it to have you know, Bijan Robinson in the solid run game when you have a guy like Tommy making his first start with it? >> I think any quarterback making your first or your hundredth start would like a good run game and I think it's our job as coaches to put together a balanced game plan because you never know what the game is going to call for. It's it's easy to say, hey, we're going to do X, Y, and Z and and but then the game changes and and the the game can change for a bunch of different reasons. So, putting together a well-balanced attack and then Tommy on game day being ready to adjust, but obviously excited about Bijan, excited about the run game. >> Thank you. >> Okay, thanks guys. >> Thanks, coach. Appreciate it.

title: S Budda Baker Press Conference 9.9.26 | AZ Cardinals
text: Buddha, with the beginning of the season, there's been so much said about what you guys are going to be. How do you guys kind of approach what this all is with everything that's said around this team and and that kind of stuff? >> Yeah, you know, I mean, you just ignore the noise. You know, at the end of the day, it's noise. It's just people's opinions. They um you know, they don't know anybody in the building and they don't see the work that any team puts in. So, you know, you got to respect, you know, anyone's opinion because that's her their opinion, but at the end of the day, everyone is, you know, 0 and 0 right now. So, um, new teams, new coaches everywhere. So, it's just a matter of, uh, who who you going to be on week one. And, uh, we're just excited for the opportunity to go play in LA against the Chargers. >> With, uh, it being week one, it always seems like week one is a little bit of a crapshoot in terms of what might happen and all that stuff. Do you find that do you find as a player that you go to week one I mean you have an idea of what might happen but do do you feel like it's it's is a little bit of a wild west in terms of what could happen as as opposed if it was week five? >> Uh I mean yeah you know uh just cuz you know like I said new coaches new coaching staffs new offenses defenses stuff like that. So for example the Chargers they got Mike McDaniel as their OC. Um, you know, there's only little film you can watch of the Chargers is going to be more personnel building, but uh, you know, it's more Miami film that you're watching because of all these different teams and, you know, different, uh, styles of play. So, you know, like you said, it's kind of nobody knows really anything until that week one starts, until teams are um, playing against each other and uh, seeing, you know, what the scores are at the end end of the game. And at the end of the day also, it's only week one. So, uh, you know, we got 17 weeks. So, uh, I I will say we're definitely excited to play week one and, um, you know, looking forward to having a good game. >> Statistically, Justin Herbert is good and accurate when he's under pressure. So, when it sounds simple enough of you rattle him by pressuring him, when a quarterback is still good under pressure, what what can you do to phase him? >> Yeah. Yeah. I mean, he he he's uh a really great quarterback. Um, you know, you you got to get in his face. Uh, he's a six six type of guy. So, not really anything's going to, you know, make him feel like he's going to have to get the ball out until, you know, guys are tackling him. So, and even then, you know, we we played, you know, a few years ago where Dennis Gard had him wrapped around for a sack and he got out of it and just threw the ball. So, he's very strong, a guy who can make all the throws inside the pocket, outside the pocket. Um, you know, a guy I like watching film on, just a ultimate competitor and, uh, definitely excited to go against him. >> You've, uh, you've had a few head coaches here and head coaches that were head coaches for the first time on the NFL level here. >> Do you do you notice that like obviously Mike's going to be the first time head coach in this game? He's coached in this league for a while. >> Yeah. >> But this is the first time he's a head coach. Do you notice those things in that first game? Do you notice the coach that coach being a little nervous that first game or everything or do you never really even >> Yeah, I don't really, you know, I don't really notice um you know, especially with Mike, uh he's he's going to be calling the plays, too. So, um yeah, he's the head coach, but he's also making sure that the offense is, you know, doing their um you know, style of play that we have. And um you know, he does a great job. uh Mike does the floor of just living in the moment, living in the present, never too high, never too low, just, you know, one play at a time of coach and uh just definitely excited for him to be our head coach, but also him to, you know, call his his first game as a head coach. Um but ultimately, we're all just playing ball. We just want to do our job at a high level and uh ultimately get a win. >> You mentioned watching some Miami video. How do you kind of strike the balance of maybe not going too far down that rabbit hole since there's different players now obviously since coach McDaniel moved, but also maybe still want to pick up on some tendencies. >> Exactly what you're saying. You know, you can't go too far down the rabbit hole because Miamiy's personnel is, you know, different from the Chargers personnel. You know, for example, Tyreek Hills lining in a running back stance and motioning out and running nine balls overs and yeah, we might have that. The Chargers might have that. Um, but you know, Miami was, you know, the running back was 4-3 guy. Tyreek 4-3, Wadd 43. So those guy and they were shorter guys, you know, so compared to an offense with, um, you know, you got Quinton who's a taller guy, you got, you know, Lad who can do all the, you know, the option routes and stuff like that. And, you know, they have great running backs as well. But like you said, just trying to kind of see their personnel on watching film, but also kind of seeing the play concepts that um Miami has done, you know, in order to, you know, try to connect it with the Chargers personnel. >> Not a few preseason snaps in the joint practice, but when it's first game, even when you're as a longtime yourself, does it still take a few snaps to kind of maybe knock any rust off the court? >> Uh, you know, I don't know. Well, that's that's a hard question. You know, everyone's different. I feel like uh you know, me personally, I don't think so. Just because, you know, I try to treat practice and everything like a game, but in a sense of Yeah. I haven't tackled anyone yet personally. You know, I didn't I wasn't able to play versus the Raiders in the in the in our, you know, um in our game where you're able to go full speed. Even the Packers, it's like Yeah. And dur during the joint practice, it's like, you know, you can't really go full speed. you can't really, you know, smack a running back coming in on a blitz or, you know, uh, you know, try to sack the quarterback. So, it's all, uh, being a pros pro. And, uh, you know, this is the first time I'm able to, you know, hit someone and not have any repercussions about it. So, I'm definitely excited uh to to do that. >> Running back Hampton, I mean, the handful of games he played last year, a lot of yards after contact, a lot of broken tackles. What do you see from him from last year's game? Yeah, more like a shorter, stalkier guy. Very fast, has the speed. I think he's a 4-3, 44 guy. A guy who can get in and out of his breaks. Um, catch the ball. You know, we're going to need all all heads around the ball with him and, uh, tackling and wrapping up. You know, the biggest thing that you see in week one is tackling. Um, you know, most teams miss a lot of tackles in week one because we're not as tackling, you know, in the in the offseason. So, that's the biggest thing, wrapping up, tackling. if you if you can get your arms around, you know, the guys to wrap up and have the camaraderie help you out on the tackles. So, just uh having that ability to to understand that, yeah, it's the first week and yeah, there's a big emphasis emphasis on tackling. >> I know you don't go directly against them, but the Chargers safeties, you know, Derwin James and then Tony J, who you got here, I think when he left, so you got to respect their game, right? >> Yeah. Is Tony still there? >> Yeah. Yeah, man. I respect their game. Of course, Derwin, we got the same agent, so I'm able to uh you know, kind of train with him a couple days in the off season. Just a ultimate uh uh competitor. Um you know, his game reminds me a lot of myself. He's just a 6'4 two 220 safety, you know. So, um you know, they do a great job. A Tony, of course, haven't had the ability to meet him when he here, but um when he was at other places, just meeting him, getting to know him. uh guy who's very smart. Um been playing in the league a very long time because of how smart he is and taking care of his body. So definitely uh respect those type of players. Um me going into year 10, that's another thing for me is taking care of my body and continuing to to uh you know try to get better in my craft. So Tony's doing a great job. Um you know, got all the love for him, just not not this week. Buuna, going into year 10, has your perspective on success in the NFL changed at all over your experience and the circumstances? Obviously, it's to win and get a championship, but just personally year to year, has that evolved for you at all? >> Uh, for me personally, from year to year, you know, everyone's happier when you win, you know, that's that's the biggest thing. So, uh, just winning and um, you know, for me personally, that's just what it's all about. Um, it's all about getting better, taking it one play at a time, but ultimately, you know, you get known for winning. So, uh, that's what I've noticed and that's what, you know, I've been here 10 years and I'm trying to do consistently and have us as a whole team, um, um, definitely try to win. So that's our main goal each and every day whether it's practice, wait room, meetings, just winning, having that winners mentality and just um trying to get better and on Sundays having fun. >> What do you want the first impression of your defense to be for the rest of the league come week one? >> Yeah, my first impression I just want, you know, I want teams to look at our film and just be like, "Wow, these guys are running to the ball." You see 11 guys running to the hat each and every play. These guys know what they're doing. They know their job. They do it at a high level. They play very fast and they create turnovers and sacks. Um that's the biggest thing, you know, um taking them one play at a time, but having those turnovers, getting those sacks, getting the ball to our offense who I think is going to be, you know, a very good offense. And um you know, our job is to get the ball back to those guys. So that's the number one mentality for the defense.

title: WR Marvin Harrison Jr. Media Availability 9.9.26 | AZ Cardinals
text: Training camp, seems to take forever with even just with that extra week. How how excited are you to get out there for real now? It's got to be >> It's been a long time coming, obviously. Especially when you miss time last year and don't get to finish the season really on a healthy note. So, I'm excited to go back out there this year and have some fun. >> What do you like about this offense with the with Coach Schwartz? >> Simple but complicated. Like, I mean, it's simple for us cuz we know what we're doing and I mean, it's pretty deep to the standpoint everything kind of looks the same, but I mean, it's just it's just simple. Like, it's not like we're trying to do a thousand things. We're just trying to do one thing a thousand times. Kind of, you know, that that saying. So, it's really exciting to be in the offense. >> With that simple but complicated mindset, how does Jacoby fit into that? And how does his skill set kind of fit with this offense? >> Yeah, I mean, his just ability to process things, especially when we're under center and play action. And a lot of times quarterbacks have to turn their back to the defense and I mean, for some quarterbacks don't like to do that. So, I think I think that's what one of his strong suits is, him being able to do that. And obviously, the run game's going to be important for us. So, when we have those play actions and and be able to process and just his you know, his routine throughout the whole week studying defense, I think that all kind of helps us to perform at a high level. >> Why is that ability to process at a high level even more important in this offense? >> Like I said, you turn your back to the defense a lot more than probably someone who's just in the gun. I mean, you're just in the gun, you keep your eyes on defense the whole time. You get to see the rotations, but you know, as a quarterback when you turn your back to the defense, you don't know where the safety's going to be. You know, everybody in the league does a good job disguising you know, at this point. So, being able to turn your back to defense and still process things at a you know, quick pace, I think that's very important as a quarterback level. >> How do you view this season for you after coming off of last >> Yeah, I mean, I just want to stay healthy. I think if I stay healthy this year, everything else is going to take care of itself. And I know the kind of player that I am and what I can do. So, I don't mean go out there and play football. I mean, I've been doing it my whole life. So, yeah. >> Do you feel like you are bound to break out into kind of who you want to be? >> I mean, break out, I don't know if say the term that you know everybody likes to use, but I'm just going to go out there and play football. Um do what I can, do what I know I can do. Um like I said, I know what I'm capable of. I have confidence in myself to go out there. Um it might be breakout to you know other people, but I think I know what I can do. Uh I think just having Jacoby, like I said, being able to process things quickly. Um being able to push the ball down the field uh for me. And then uh just like having pieces around me, having Mike, having Trey, J Love, KB. Um just having a bunch of other weapons around me. They all is going to help help everybody in the long run. I know, right? It is a lot of we- a lot of weapons, one ball. And I think just everybody is so unselfish. I think that's probably the biggest thing. I know, man. I'm just so proud of Mike cuz I mean, I see the work that he puts in day in and day out since I first got here. I think Mike was one of the first guys to text me congratulations when I got drafted. Me and Mike have kind of had that bond throughout. And I'm just so proud of him cuz I just know what the work that he puts in and know what uh the game means to him and all that he dedicates to it. So, uh no one's more proud of him on this team than I am because I just know how much he has earned it and he deserves it so much. Um so, yeah. >> You mentioned Kendrick Bourne earlier. Does Does he keep your group on on their collective toes with his energy and >> Just bringing in just bringing energy day in and day out. Whether he's having a good practice, bad practice, it doesn't matter. I think that's what we definitely need cuz me and Mike are kind of a little serious. When we're in a serious setting, you kind of take things right, you know. Um tough sometimes when things don't go well, but having KB around us definitely helps. >> Do you ever Do you ever say Do you ever shout at >> No, not at all. We need that. We need that energy day in and day out for sure. >> Do you get nervous or butterflies still on game day? >> Absolutely. I mean, I think everybody is different. I always I always ask people like for me like when you care about something so much, I think it's only normal to get nervous and maybe a little anxious for it. I think that's what it is for me. I think for me it's just channeling those emotions more than anything, but um when you care about something like you know, football as much as I do, I think it's just a normal reaction. >> So, specifically what are the days that you feel them? Like morning or right before kickoff? >> Uh I don't know. I just think about football everyday, so kind of all all the time like you could really say, but I think just training and preparing for myself for game days uh is the best I can do. >> What is the balance for you of wanting to be kind of a cerebral like player thinking about things a lot on the field, but also not thinking too much and being able to play carefree in your own >> I mean the best thing is to think less. The less as possible. I mean the more you thinking the more bad things usually happen, but for me I think think less as possible. Trust in preparation. Uh it's probably the biggest thing I can you know kind of tell anybody is trust in the preparation you put in throughout the week and whatever happens on game day happens on game day, but all the thing that you can really keep control of what happens Monday through Saturday. So, that's kind of my mindset. >> Tell us about the Chargers D a little bit. Like what what what's that like preparing for a new coordinator? You know some of the personnel, but but the does that heighten the importance of making in-game adjustments? >> Uh definitely. You got to be able to adjust on the fly if you have a new coordinator. I mean obviously he was there I think 2 years ago when we played them. Uh but anything like week one is always the week where you kind of have to adjust on the fly cuz there's no game film on anybody yet. I mean preseason's preseason. Uh very vanilla, but I think that's one thing that Mike kind of talked about is being able to adjust on the fly when we need to. Definitely. I think we're all very confident individuals. I think we're confident in ourselves and also confident as a group and as a unit. I think it starts with Mike and still in that confidence and confidence in us. I think we have to play with that a little bit too. We have to show that on Sunday. No. Ping pong, yes. Ping pong, yes. Not I'm not there yet. I think I wouldn't say I'm A tier. Trying to work my way into B tier group, but um I definitely got to get some ping pong. >> Have you gotten custom paddles yet? >> No, exactly. I didn't get that far. You got to be good to get custom powder, so. We'll see.

text: Kobe, uh, at one point during training camp, you were talking about the the currency of your teammates respect and how that was important to you. It just seems like it just seems like uh for everything that ended up swirling around you in the offseason and they talk about the contract, the one constant was that whatever teammate was talking about it, it was pretty clear they wanted you to be in this position that you're going to be starting week one. I know you talked about it before, but just was that something I I don't want to say that kept you going because that's kind of a little overblown, but something that meant something to you a lot as we kind of went through these months. Um I I I think you can ask any player in a locker room is you know you want that sea on your chest because you know how much um you know it means to the people around if they were captains. Um you know and it's and it's voted on by the players. It's not some like fan favorite or or like who's the highest paid or things like that. It's based on on our players and we got a lot of guys that deserve that seat. You know what I mean? And uh I'm fortunate to have it but we got a lot of guys that deserve that. >> Were you expecting it? >> Uh you know I don't expect anything in this league. text: I mean, I think any signs of comfort for him is significant. However, I haven't I It's not like I could be wrong, but I didn't see him wear the neck roll every day. I think it was during either mandatory mini camp or it was in training camp and you were talking about the struggle that you would face because you were injured and you were banged up, but you also still wanted to be available for your team because your team needs you, but then at the same time not being able to perform to the level that you know you're capable of performing. Should you have played football last year? Like looking back on it, do you think it did more harm than good? And like how mentally challenging was all of that? I I definitely don't think it helped. Um I don't think it helped. I know I know the injuries that I sustained uh um continuing to play football didn't help it at all. If anything, it just got worse. And um but you know as a competitor I guess how I was raised, how I played growing up with a lot of my friends that are now playing professionally. If we could go we went. Um and you know sometimes your body may not be able to perform like your mind might be able to. And unless you can't walk, you were going to go out there and you were going to play and you were going to perform cuz it made you tougher, you know, it made you um stronger mentally knowing that I can like the confidence it gives you when you're still able to get open or when you're still able to run fast and you're on one leg, you know, it gives you a different amount of confidence because you think, damn, if I can do this on one leg, just wait till I have two, you know. >> Um that's that's that's what that does. But I think playing last year during those injuries, I think it definitely did more harm. But did it make me stronger mentally? I think so. >> And now obviously you are healthy and you're ready to start another season. The Bills take on the Houston Texans week one. You have a couple additions to the wide receiver room. DJ Moore and Skyler Bell. Uh from your perspective as a teammate, you get a veteran in DJ Moore that comes in. You get a rookie and Skyler Bell. What have you seen from your two new teammates this off seasonason, this uh camp and preseason? >> Uh they're doing very well. You know, DJ started off really strong making a lot of plays in camp, which I'm pretty sure everyone saw. Um Skyler was hurt for a portion of the camp um or sidelined him, but you know, he did well in the game um in the preseason game where he played the entire the entire thing. So, uh I think he's he's growing, he's learning. Um you know, he he he watches, he applies. DJ is just that vet in the room that, you know, keeps everybody keeps everybody on their toes because, you know, vets vets are not scared to say anything, you know. So, uh um but we have we have a good relationship, DJ and I and Skyler learning and coming along. >> What does DJ do for you, right? Like I understand what DJ does for the offense, but what does his addition do for you and for the other wide receivers? I've talked to Khalil about this a little bit and you know he's had some really interesting insight of like how it could potentially open things up or how it could give you guys more favorable matchups. You know, it does feel like it really benefits everybody, but what does it do for you specifically? >> Uh, you know, I think Khalil was right in what he in what he's saying. I think from a I think it it I think it will breed um a competitive spirit in the room. You know, I feel like, you know, when you like I was talking to somebody today, you know, I went to St. St. Thomas Aquinus High School. And when you're there with guys that can play, it forces you to be like, "Okay, I need to be on my game, you know, because I don't want to stand out for the wrong reasons." So, you you start to you start to have a healthy uh relationship with competing against your teammates and it brings the best out of you. Um, I think from a mental from from a mental standpoint, you know, having him in the room definitely elevates a lot of guys games. You know, it's it's been elevating my game. You know, you you learn a lot. You see what they're good at. You're like, "Okay, maybe I should uh maybe I should try that move or apply that." Um, but it's it's good to be able to to compete with and you know, at times it's like almost against, you know, but it's not it's not against as in, oh, I got to do better than him for this reason. It's it's not it's not that. It's like uh he's he's forcing me to be better. You know, when I was playing with Keenan and Mike, you know, >> Kenan would tell me that Kenan would would tell me that I pushed him to to be to be on his game every day, you know, even with Mike Williams and all these guys. So, I think just having having really really talented guys in the room just elevates your game. >> You're speaking my language, by the way. I know all about St. Thomas Aquinus and living in Florida myself for 16 years. Holy cow, Matt. I mean, there's a there's a high school that produced has produced many, many great NFL players. Michael Irvin, Joey Bosa, Nick Bosa, Gino Atkins. Crazy. I mean, you're right. Asante Samuel. >> Nick Nick Bonito. >> Nick Bonito. >> That's pretty amazing. >> In one high school. >> I mean, what when you were growing up and you were going and playing football at a high school like that, what was it like every day kind of going out there and competing with these guys and against these guys and going through a season like that? >> It was hard. Um and that's that's just what I'm what I'm used to. And you know I I'mma go if I'm going to go I'm going to go hard every single time. >> What was your and understanding there were so many different hurdles that came up along the way. What was your first season with Josh Allen like? And what does he do that maybe people don't appreciate enough? Like I understand this is the number two player on the NFL top 100. This is a guy who has won an MVP. I think everybody understands how good Josh Allen is. But is there anything that people don't understand that makes him that good? Uh he plays the game like it's high school football. Like it's literally um yeah, he's a professional quarterback in the NFL, the best in the game, but he plays it like he's just out with his boys having fun. Um, you know, and I think it takes a lot of stress off of off of guys, you know, when they see the the guy who's stereotypically supposed to be the one that's stuck up and all in a ball and has to get everybody on track and you do that, you do that, you do this, as you know, as a quarterback. He's not. Um, he plays very free. He laughs. He jokes. Um, quite the opposite of me. I quite quite the opposite. I'm more quiet. I'm more reserved. I'm more just just analyzing. You know, some people might mistake it as um me either being distant or not having fun or um not enjoying the moment. But, you know, it's it's not it's none of those things. I just I feel like when I'm when I'm doing something that I'm very very passionate about, I give it all of my attention and I get quiet to give it the respect that it deserves. And that's just how that's just what I do. So the moment I walk into work, I'm usually just quiet, just trying to get right, you know, and be ready to put everything into it. Um, everyone has their own things, but for Josh, that's I think that's what helps him and also helps his team. >> Yeah, it takes all all different kinds of personalities in a locker room, especially football locker room with, you know, 53 70 people, uh, whatever it is. What about your head coach now who was the offensive coordinator? Um, Joe Brady, what about the transition and the change for him? Anything that's different about him, how he goes about his business every day with you guys and his transition from offensive coordinator to head coach. What have you seen? >> Uh, he needs to learn how to coach defense. >> I think I think I think I think that's I think that's the only uh I think that's the only thing that I've seen different, you know. I think his approach to the to to to work is the same. His approach to the offense is the same. Um, his approach to his players is the same. It's just now he needs to learn defensive calls. >> Joshua, this is the last question for me. It's a question that I've asked a lot of your peers. It's a question I've asked a lot of your teammates. And that was a bit surprising because admittedly I kind of thought he would stick with somebody on defense. But I also remember, you know, I asked that question to David Edwards and to Conor McGuffin last year and they like immediately got to Deion Walker. They were like, I don't know. This was the fourth round pick. This guy is really, really good. And over the years it's been, you know, a lot of different answers and a lot of but sometimes it surprises me. Like when Shaq Thompson said Jackson Haw, I was like, "Wow, that's like a little random." He's going to let you know that he's that he's there with his physicality. Um he's fast. He's he's quick. He's smart. Um he can play the ball in the air. Um, so I think Cole Bishop is is a sleeper. >> We can't let you go without asking about this weekend's game. Uh, the Houston Texans, obviously, it's been a struggle for the Bills the last couple of years down there. I know you weren't on the team a couple of years ago, but last year, um, you know, obviously Josh got sacked several times. It came down to the very end. You guys weren't on the result that you wanted to at the end of the game. What makes their defense so special? And just talk about maybe the challenge ahead on Sunday against this Texans team. >> Uh, they're they're very fast. They play fast. Um, you know, they send everybody they send everybody a lot all the time. Um, they have a talented group inside and out. Um, but you know, honestly, I'm not even thinking about the Texans to be honest. I think I think as a competitor you Yeah. you study your opponent, but I think sometimes people can get too caught up in their opponent and they lose themselves in the process. Um, I'm more focused on what I need to do. Um, how I need to go out there and do what I know how to do, what I need to do to help my team, what this offense needs to do to win the game. Um, to make it easier on the defense. Um, I think it's all about all about the Bills, you know. Yeah, you of course you respect you respect your your opponents and your competitors, but I think I like to put more focus on what I have to do. I think I think as a as a team, we put more focus on what we have to do and let them stop us, >> you know, let let them stop our best. H >> how do you get ready? What what's on what's on the playlist? How do you get ready? How do you get in that mindset? What's on the pregame playlist for Joshua Palmer? >> Pregame playlist. Honestly, a lot of Michael Jackson. >> Oh, yeah. I love that. Oh, love that. >> I have a Walkman um that I got during training camp. And it's been my best friend. I I bring it almost everywhere. Um you know, it gives you gets you away from your phone, able to enjoy the music. Uh teaches you patience. You can't just skip skip, search for what you want. You just got to listen to what you have and work with it. Um so I've just been buying a lot of Michael Jackson CDs. Uh the current one that's in there right now is bad. >> Yes. >> I was just gonna ask you like off-the-wall bad. I mean, listen, I am mad now we went this long without knowing this because >> I'm a big Michael Jackson fan. title: Exclusive Interview with Denzel Ward
text: Welcome back to Cleveland Browns Daily, brought to you by Bally Bet, official sports betting partner of your Cleveland Browns. And we are happy to be joined by the Warden, your five-time Pro Bowl cornerback of your Cleveland Browns, Denzel Ward. And Denzel, it feels like we have been waiting forever to get to play a game. You finally get that opportunity going down to Jacksonville. How excited are you to just finally play some football? >> Yeah, excited, man. Like you said, finally play some football. The season is here. Uh this is what we all work for and uh look forward to. And so, you know, it's time to go down there and and the goal is to get a win. >> Get a win as we did last time we were in Jacksonville, by the way. And also make them know your name, as we have on the T-shirt here. What do you kind of when you set your goals every year, given all that you've accomplished in this league, what do you set the goals for? Team, obviously, win win the division, all that. But personally, what are your personal goals this season? >> Uh for me, personal goals is definitely to start off with interceptions. You know, I want to up my interceptions this year. And uh just definitely be in that shut-down corner uh going into every game. So, not allowing my guy to catch the ball. And uh just doing what I have to do in each game to make plays and uh do what we can to win. >> How do you balance the fact that they don't want to throw the ball in your direction? So, it's not you're not going to get as many opportunities to get interceptions. >> Well, I'm I'm talking it up. So, I think they going to they going to attack me more uh this year and throw the ball at me. So, I'm looking forward to it. >> Last year, we kind of came out and we said, "Here's what we're going to play on defense." And that's what you got and we were just really, really good at it. This year, we're going to do some of that, but there's going to be a little bit more disguise, a little more movement post-snap. Do you think that'll help kind of give some more opportunities where the ball might be coming in in your direction? >> For sure. That's why I say I'm looking forward to playing in uh Coach Woods' defense cuz like you said, there's a lot of different moving parts and opportunities to get interceptions and make plays on the ball. So, I'm looking forward to putting it out there on tape uh this week. >> How's the communication? Cuz I know that's so important in this defense. And the good news is in your room, there's a lot of new faces. But the three guys that are most likely going to be out there, yourself, Tyson, Miles, you've been together this whole off season. And then the safeties have been out there with you guys as well. How's that communication, and are you guys do you feel like you're you're ready to go out there and roll week one? >> Definitely. I think we're in a great spot, you know, communication's been great, and we just have we have constant communication every play, you know, and on the field, off the field. So, just really just getting on the same page. You got to be on the same page in this defense, and that's the biggest thing. >> What challenges do Trevor Lawrence and obviously this Liam Cohen-led offense, it was very productive last year. They've got a bunch of different receivers, they've got tight ends, they've got running backs who can catch it. What what kind of challenges do they present? And then when you're facing a guy like Trevor Lawrence? >> Yeah. Yeah, Trevor Lawrence is a great quarterback, and able to extend plays, and great at making second-chance plays, just rolling around and being able to get the ball to his playmakers. And so, we got to have to cover twice, and be tight in coverage. And yeah, just looking forward to the opportunity. >> What's like the biggest difference between you getting ready to have your NFL debut, which by the way featured many interceptions, to to today getting ready to play in week one? >> Yeah, hopefully I could replay that and have a couple interceptions in this game. You know, I'll take two interceptions this game. Well, man, just just focus on my assignment, my job, and going out there having fun, and making plays. I said the main goal is to win, and going out there do whatever I can to help us win. >> How good can you and Tyson be as a duo? >> I feel we could be the best. You know, that's the goal, but I feel we could really be the best dual tandem in this league. >> I think so, too. I'm actually very excited to see a full season of this together, to see you guys out there. All right, you made some news, obviously not football-related, as now a part owner of the Cleveland Guardians. How did that come about, and you're already smiling. Why was that so important to you? By the way, how cool is that? >> Yeah, it's pretty cool. Yeah, it's pretty cool. Just constant communication with the Guardians, and you know, seeing that it was becoming more real. I'm grateful that they gave me an opportunity to be a part of what they got going on, and as I like I said, it's pretty special. I always watched them as a kid growing up, and just another chance to be a part of the Cleveland community, and yeah, it's fun, it's enjoyable, and I'm looking forward to it. >> Like when you think about the fact that you obviously grew up in the area, you've been watching these at the Guardians, the Cavs, you're a fixture at, you know, Cavs games here to be and you played for the Browns. Do you sometimes feel like this is a little surreal? >> Yeah, it is. It is. I do sometimes like, man, this is real like I'm a Cleveland kid, born in Cleveland. Like this is the teams I grew up watching and then like I'm a part I'm really a part of the organizations playing and and just being part owner everything. So it's it's definitely a surreal feeling. >> You're on the all-time Cleveland Browns team as a cornerback. You're go to all of your front row all the time at the Cavs and the big games and now you're a part owner of the Guardians. I mean >> It's it's special. I'm grateful, man. I'm grateful. Still a lot more to accomplish and do, but definitely grateful. >> Oh, we're going to start that again at Win down in Jackson this weekend. Denzel, thank you so much. We're grateful to have you and the leadership that you've kind of taken on with this team and obviously the great play on the field. So let's go, baby. >> Thank you, man. Let's go. >> All right.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference | September 9th, 2026
text: time healthwise, just how do you feel like you guys are? Sounds like everybody's going to practice today. How do you feel like confident that, you know, at least knock? >> I feel like we're in a good place, you know, outside of losing Alex, you know, a few weeks ago. I mean, we've been we've been relatively healthy. Some uh nicks and bruises here or there, but feel good about where we're at. time to really hone in on on Desawn and deise a game plan that you think will maximize his strengths and abilities. How do you feel? How excited are you about what you're putting in place for him? And how do you how confident do you think he feels in it? >> Uh I can't speak for him. Um we certainly are going to try to build it as best we can around the things that we've seen in the months that we've been around him. What we think uh gives us all offensively uh chance to operate at a really high level And uh so I'm excited for him. I've said that all along for all the work he's put in. Again, you'll have to ask him, but I I'm assuming that he's super excited about the opportunity to get back on the field and uh continue to play at a high level >> to get this far without any soft tissue injuries. What do you attribute that to? >> Well, I think our training staff does an outstanding job in terms of getting our players ready. our assistant coaches have done a great job in terms of the rotations that we have during practice. I would also say that it's it's been a relatively cool, you know, training camp. I mean, we've last week, luckily, we got a little bit of uh we got a little bit of uh weather, a little bit of heat, but uh I think it's it's a combination. I think the guys have done a great job taking care of their bodies and uh people within the building have done a great job >> and their defense. Sean today talked about that front and how aggressive it is. Just what have you seen, you know, in getting ready for this week from them in that regard? >> Well, again, it all starts, it's the same with us. I mean, we talk about it being the engine of the defense and it starts up front and and they've got those guys. I mean, Armstead and Hines and and Walker and and Hamilton, the guys up front, I mean, they they really make it go. I mean, and uh it'll be a great challenge for us and it'll be great to see where we're at. I mean, that's really where you're at at that moment is the excitement about Sunday is you get to see where you're at. There's nothing to fear. There's nothing, you know, to be worried about. The bottom line is is after the after week one, we'll be where where we're at individually and then where we are where we're at that point as a team. Look at Trevor Lawrence. How have you seen him kind of develop throughout his career and where he stands now leading that offensive one game? >> Well, I mean, first of all, he's a tremendous football player and has been for a long time. Liam and Grant have done a great job with him and Liam's done a great job wherever he's been maximizing quarterback play. uh when he got his opportunity as far as when when I got to know him was at Kentucky and they were scoring at Kentucky when Kentucky wasn't scoring. I mean, they were playing great defense. That'll tell you a lot about uh what I think of Liam and then obviously uh his background with with Shawn McVey and then and then doing it with Baker at the at the Bucks. I got a ton of respect for them and their offensive staff and obviously um Trevor has thrived under that. I know it's only a one-year sample size, but uh really thrived under under that system. >> Kind of following up on that, Liam was talking earlier today about he spoke to you before you got the he jumped from Rams to Kentucky. Just what was sort of your piece of advice? What what was sort of the advice you gave him in those conversations as he was making that move? >> Well, it really wasn't there wasn't any advice. He wasn't calling me for advice. He was calling me to talk football. So all we did was talk football. I mean, we were probably on the phone for 45 minutes just talking football thoughts, you know, just when I was at Georgia and that he had been at Kentucky and had left and had come back. That was when he came back to Kentucky a second time. And I've always enjoyed talking football with Liam. I think he's really bright. He's passionate. Um, he says what he mean, he means what he says. I like guys like that. And uh, that's fun to be around and it's fun to talk to. and I've really enjoyed uh getting to know him and got a lot of respect for him. >> You know, week one game predictions are coming out. A lot of NFL analysts have the Jaguars. Um in fact, NFL Network, I think all the analysts picked the Jaguars win. What is kind of your message to the guys? Do you use that as bulletin board material for them? Do you even acknowledge it? >> Well, I don't really acknowledge it because I don't I don't make predictions, you know. All I try to figure out as figure out is how we're going to be our best today. That's all we've done since we've been here is how we're going to be the best we can be individually and collectively as a team today. That's really all we can control. Um so I I really I did not know that. I did not know who's predicting what. I really really don't care. Uh what I care about is how we practice today, how we prep, how we take care of our bodies. That allows us to put our best foot forward Sunday. Um, you've been at it since January, been in camp for six weeks, but is there a different energy this week? Do you feel that at all? >> I felt that on Monday. I thought that with a few days off, I thought it might be a little bit sluggish and it was not. We'll see today. Um, it should feel that way. It should feel like it's different. It's everything we work for. It's why we get paid, we get paid, right? It should feel different. uh to put our best foot forward today and then tomorrow and then Friday, wrap it up Saturday and then go play our best football on Sunday. >> In some ways, how you know your journey to this point in your career, you know, you know, has has been long and there's a little bit of a freedom in that for you that you're not focused on the future. You can just do it your way today. Um, how do how do you plan on balancing that? Because it's easy to talk about that, but when you're in the moment in the game, your call plays and things like that, how how do you balance the the freedom of just kind of doing it your way and letting the results be what they are versus some of the conservative nature that sometimes comes with being a a head coach? >> Uh, I won't know that till we play. I mean, I don't anticipate that. I think that helps being the age that I am. I mean, over the course of time, you go through the ups and downs of an individual practice, a week, a month, a season. So, I think I'm pretty well prepared for the ups and downs that are coming. Uh, they come every day that comes with life. So, I don't see it that way. Um, I anticipate call it the way I see it. uh offense, defense, special teams, and and I again I won't know till we get there, but I don't I don't anticipate it being any different than it's been over the last however many years I've been coaching. >> You and Deshan are kind of speaking the same football language and that you probably when you first started to get to know him here, maybe you realize that you guys have a lot in common, you know, just from a football standpoint. So, what has that been like sort of sympatico between you two just talking ball and and getting him ready to get back out there and play? >> Well, it's been great. Uh, he has really embraced what we do offensively. I think for him it's been, you know, breath of fresh air, new life, new opportunity. Now, now we've all got to take advantage of it. The same with myself. I mean, so it's I'm excited for him. I would hope that all of our players, including Deshawn, that we're speaking the same language, offense, defense, special teams, and speaking the same language terms of our expectations on a daily basis, a weekly basis, and how we're going to play on Sunday. >> Um, you spent the last the offseason, the last summer months getting to know your team, figuring out what you guys do well, as you talked about. when you picture what the identity of this team is on offense and just as a team as a whole, what does that kind of look like in your eyes going into? >> Well, I've always said it is, and I've heard a lot of coaches say it, but our identity is how we play and there's scheme elements of that, but how are we going to play as a team? I mean, when someone watches us play, like whether it's our operation, whether it's how physical we play, whether it's how connected we are, whether it's how we chase the football and convoy downfield or how our defense uh runs to that smoke. I mean, to me, that's what you want your identity to be. And then you figure out the other part of it systemwise, offense, defense, special teams. But my identity wants to be what I what I just talked about. >> Travis uh collaborate to to do uh perform a game plan. >> Well, it's been a we do it collectively. Travis isn't the only piece of that. He's a big part of the run game and has been when we were at Baltimore, but every one of our coaches has a piece of the game plan and we as we get together at the beginning of the week, everybody has a chance to present of how they see their given area and we try to be able to pull from that. Obviously within our system, uh you can't create a new offense every week and I love guys having ideas because I think the best way to get to an elite idea is having lots of ideas. Uh that never ends. Uh you're always chasing edges. You're chasing uh better ways of doing it. So, but ultimately um Trav wouldn't be here if I didn't trust him completely with what we do offensively and within the run game. And um there's a lot of times when I'm not in those meetings, Travis runs them.
