What have you seen from him in the leadup to his first start in whatever? >> Yeah, just been growing every day, getting better every day and um that's all we could expect from each player on this team and um just looking forward to seeing him go out there compete and you know um we all the goal is to get a win so that's that's the goal for everybody. >> Prediction for Saturday, >> Buckeyes, man. Buckeyes win always. >> Thank you guys. >> Not going to make any headlines. Huh? I'm not You stop and start my day. I appreciate it. identify why you might have a 7 and0 record against the Jaguars and sort of what how that has transpired over the years. >> Um I guess a majority of it was you know that was one of our big rival teams um been in that same division when I played for Houston. So, it was, you know, mandatory to try to get those games. Um, they were very, very, it was very close, intense games and, um, you know, we found ways to win. That's pretty much all I can really say about that. >> Deshawn, how how much more just comfortable, you know, connected do you feel like you you've gotten over the last couple of weeks with guys like Casey and Denzel and and the like? >> Uh, yeah, we just continue to just build that trust each and every day. Um, the more reps, the more opportunities that we get out there on the field. um especially live in practice, but also in the film room, off the field, being able to communicate, talking, seeing different things that coaches really trying to explain what I'm what I'm seeing and what he's seeing as he run the routes and um you know, just trying to be in the right place at the right time so I can put the ball, you know, get the ball to them and get them in their hands so they can make plays. >> Michelle, we've asked you along the way, what's it going to be like if you started when you're start now or days away. What do you think, what are those emotions that you're feeling now and what do you think they're going to be outside? Um, I mean, that's one thing you got to control. I think, uh, I'm super excited. I'm super happy. I'm super, you know, blessed for the opportunity, um, that this organization gave me. And, uh, I just want to be able to capitalize on it. So, really, right now, I'm just present in this moment talking with you guys, you know, getting ready for practice and just letting, uh, you know, the days come to me. I don't want to rush it. Um, and I don't want it to, um, you know, try to drag it on, you know, I just kind of, again, enjoy each moment because I know how fast it can be taken away. So, um, you know, I just continue to just focus on my present. >> In terms of, uh, career accomplishments, how does it where do you rank just being able to start a game? >> Um, I mean, it's it's definitely good. I mean, I don't know if I can rank rank it anywhere, but I mean, like I said before, it's it's a blessing. It's a great opportunity to have this um, you know, this chance this year, and um, you know, I want to take full advantage of it. when we talked to you last week, you said that um you haven't yet showcased what you can do in Todd Mon's offense. So, what can we expect to see? So, >> um yeah, uh I guess we'll just have to wait and see pretty much. And I don't want to get too much in what we trying to do getting ready for the game plan. So, uh we'll just have to wait and see. Do you feel like, you know, there's any pressure on you to get this offense going right away given how stick to get it off right? >> Um, yeah. I mean, that's the goal is to just be able to get off and and be explosive, put up points, help our defense out, and be able to capitalize and get the win. Um, but you got to be able to take the what the defense give us. You know, this is a very, very good team. Uh, this defense is very strong. I think they won the last eight out of the nine games last year. um they were pretty much close to winning that wild card game against Buffalo. So, you know, this is a really good team and you got to, you know, be able to see what they're trying to do defenders and try to find the the weaknesses in their defense so we can try to move the ball and get points. >> It's been a while since that Buffalo game is out of your mind. >> Which Buffalo game, >> preseason game? >> Oh, yeah. I mean, yeah, that's I'm not worried about that. You know, we focus on now, you know, it's about what we got what we can do now. So, uh, it's not about what we woring about in the future or in the past, excuse me. You know, we're not worried about 24. We're not worrying about last year me not playing. We're not worried about the preseason right now. We got to focus on Jacksonville. Sean, >> how do you prepare for a a team where there's, you know, not a lot of tape to look at as far as like current tape? Because preseason is just so benile. I'm sure Jacksonville really hasn't shown a lot. just, you know, as a quarterback, how do you prepare for this week, uh, as far, you know, matchups and, you know, what they do defensively without having a lot of that visual elements? >> Yeah, you just try to watch, you know, the games from last year. Um, you try to catch a little bit of the preseason, like you said, is, you know, pretty vanilla. And then you just take what the coaches and the and the scouts and everyone that put the data in this week, you know, and try to, you know, game plan on how we want to try to attack them. And uh you kind of execute your master your game plan and then you kind of have the base of what they kind of ran last year, what they were really good at and and then on Sunday you kind of gota, you know, react and adjust on how they, you know, playing different week differently from last year. >> Deshawn, what have you seen from the Jacksonville defense just as you've started to really dive into the week now? >> Uh very very aggressive up front, you know, and um that front four is very very uh talented and very good. And then you have the linebacker group that is very active, instinctive, and very smart. And then you have a secondary that has some young, talented, fast, uh, instinctive players, too. So, um, yeah, it's a very good defense that that plays sound. Um, they understand what they want to do as a defense and, um, and what they're trying to take away from us. >> So much of a quarterback being out there playing has to do with confidence. How confident do you feel in the game plan that you and and Todd have kind of put together with each other? How do you feel like the synergy is between you guys and how confident are you in this game plan in general? >> Uh, it's going well. You know, me and Tide, me and Trav, um, the whole offensive staff is just communicating what I like, what he likes, what what I see, what he see, and then we got to meet, you know, meet in the middle and then we got to, you know, be able to trust the game plan that he wants to call and I got to be able to execute that. So, uh, each and every day is a step of building that confidence and that trust leading to Sunday. And, you know, by Saturday night going into Sunday morning, uh, we want to be fully confident and go out there and let it loose. >> Todd's talked a lot about just figuring out what you guys do well throughout training camp and preseason. >> As you get closer and closer to people here, just what do you kind of feel the identity is for you guys on offense? >> Um, I feel like we can be multiple. I mean, we can do a lot of different things. cuz we have a lot of different guys that are very talented and um that can, you know, get the ball in their hands. So, you know, I think we just want to be multiple and and try to spread the ball around. >> You feel like you have to talk about he mentioned now he's 60 years old. He's waiting a long time to get in this position and he's not worried about the next job. Um, you know, and somewhat liberating. He can do things the way he wants them done and not worry about things like that. for you not after going through everything you've been through physically, you know, is is there maybe something a little bit liberating for you as a player just to go out there and just be yourself and and let it all hang out there and the results will be what the results will be and not maybe worried about the future so much. >> Yeah, I mean I can't focus on the future. I got to focus on now. You know, if I try to look ahead and I get distracted on not focusing on what I need to do now, then you know, who knows what the future might hold. So, uh, all I can do is control these moments now, these opportunities I have now. And I want to be just like Monk Ty Mon said, like, you know, he he's 60, he feels like this is his shot. So, you know, me being on my last year of my deal. And, you know, uh, being year 10, I feel like this is my opportunity to be up to go and showcase that I can still play in this league. And I can I want to continue to play in this league. So, um, this is my opportunity to do that. You know, you don't want to talk about the past, but it's 7 and0 and never losing to that team. Give you any comfort? >> Nah. Nah. I don't I don't get too comfortable, man. This is this is a different team. This is 20 20 20 26 man. So, you know, I'm not going into this game looking at the 7-0 record at all. You know, this is a good Jacksonville team that, you know, we got to go out there and we got to earn it. So, uh I'm not looking at that at all. >> Excited about this game. It's the last one >> about this particular game plan and what you're going to be able to do on Sunday that maybe you have in a very long time that maybe we didn't ever have here. >> Uh yeah, I'm I'm super excited. I think I'm super excited for the opportunity. I'm super excited for the game plan and and and the players we have in this locker room that we can go out there and uh be very explosive and um put up a lot of points that the Cleveland Browns fans want to see. >> Thank you. >> Thank you. Thank you. Let's go. Okay. >> Yeah. Carol, just uh how do you feel now that you feel you completely caught back up and that you're physically 100% and back in the flow of everything after your after your surgery and stuff? >> Yeah. Yeah, I feel great. Uh you know, obviously a lot of rehab, you know, a lot of uh extra time went into it. So, you know, everything's been feeling good. You know, I'm ready. I'm ready to Connor has talked about a lot how you improved your blocking >> from a year ago. So what did you do to get better at? >> Uh I mean I I can't really like pin it on to something but uh obviously you know blocking is just a want to. So uh you know just showing everybody every day that you know I want to you know I want us to win and things like that. >> How do you feel like it's been going developing chemistry with Deshawn? I mean just it's crazy to think like you probably didn't throw any ball at all before this like offseason/s summer. So how has that process been? >> Yeah, it's it's been really nice. You know, obviously been practicing every day, you know, just building that chemistry. So obviously it's really nice, you know. Uh it's crazy to think about like I used to actually watch him on TV when I was younger and next I'm here. So it's pretty dope. >> Like what's the process of developing that chemistry like for you as a pass catcher? Is it just repping it over and over and over again or is there more to it? Yeah, it's just like you just said, just repping it. Uh, you know, talking through things, you know, you know, seeing how he see things and how he want me to adjust, you know, things like that. >> You were such a focus of the offense last year. How do you think your role would even grow more? >> Uh, I mean, I don't really think about it that much, you know. I just whatever the coach, you know, give me, I just go out there and, you know, do at my best of my abilities, you know. Have you put on any like upper body like that? I I'll say I'm the same. I'm the same size. Yeah. >> With with new coaching staff, new playbook and system. Does your I know you're real multiple last year. Does does that carry over? Does it feel any different what they're asking you to do this year as opposed to last year? >> No, I feel about the same. You know, uh like I said this before, like everybody know my abilities. So, you know, you know, Todd, you know, we just like to uh work off of our strengths and things like that. So, same. Appreciate it.

title: Joe Burrow Press Conference - September 9
text: [music] Heat. >> [music] >> How does it feel for it to finally be game? >> Yeah, we're ready to go. We feel good. You know, we we put in a great week work last week. Got another couple days here, but we're itching to get get at it. >> First impression types defense. >> Yeah, they throw a lot of a lot of things at you. Um, you know, you have to handle your protections really well. You got to know your hot answers really well. You got to know where your quick answers are if it's not hot. Um, you got to know your plan inside and out. You got to know what coverages they play behind it. They make it tough for you. A lot of prep, but uh, we'll be ready. >> Joe, I know you talked about pretty much the whole offseason. This is the year, you know, you guys got the group to hopefully make a deep run. How important is it, even though it's just game one to have that Super Bowl mentality each week going into every week, zero and zero mindset, trying to get that win? >> Yeah. Not just each week, but every day. Every day at practice, every day in meetings, every day in the weight room, every time you step foot in the building, trying to bring that mindset and Sunday is just um a result of what you do in the offseason, but mainly, you know, that week of work. So, you got to bring it every day. Now that you have a whole training camp going against this defense under your belt, what are your full um like just ideas and thoughts about the defense going into the uh the year? >> Yeah, I'm just excited to excited to watch it. You know, I have my thoughts and and impressions about our entire team, but you know, we got to go out and prove it. We got to go out and and execute on Sundays and prove prove ourselves right. So, that's what's great about football. you have every Sunday you get to a chance to make an impression on your teammates, your coaches, the world and um doesn't really matter about anything else. You can block everything out. You can be be terrible for for several weeks, but you know, every Sunday is a new opportunity. >> You had a great interview with Jeff Hobson, Bengals.com, and you wanted to kind of >> shout out Hobs. Shout out [laughter] shout out Butchie. Uh, you wanted to staple down the fact that you are committed, Joe. Why was that important for you? >> Um, I I don't necessarily Yeah, it was never a question in my mind. I didn't necessarily think about, you know, stamping that in that in that moment. That's just uh that's how I feel. I don't uh you know I am where my feet are and I try to attack every day with championship [clears throat] mindset like I said before and you know I love it here. I love everything about this place. So you know we're going to make it work. >> How does all the moves in the offseason kind of reinforce your belief here? >> I think it's obvious that everybody in the organization wants to win and is willing to do whatever it takes to to make that happen from the top down. And um you know I just try to attack every day with the same mindset that you know everybody upstairs does. That's with the fact that they just want to win. >> When Dan Pictur tells us I want this team to be what our where I want the offense to be what the offense needs to be to win week to week and that can change. When he says that to you, what does that mean? >> You got to be adaptable. You got to be able to adapt on the fly to a lot of different things that are thrown at you, both from the defense and from yourselves. Uh, you know, it's no secret we're going to face unscouted looks every week because of the weapons that we have on the outside [snorts] and the style of offense that we've played in the past. And we have to be able to see those looks and interpret out the looks that we're going to see based on the looks we see early in the game and be able to adapt to that. And I think we've done really well at that in the past, but you know, we just have to continue to build on that. >> You had the toe injury last year with a full off season. How much more do you feel like you'll be able to use your legs and scramble this year? >> Yeah, it's going to be I'm excited to to break that back out again. you know, last season I I certainly couldn't when I came back and uh you know, that's a that's a big part of my game. Um, you know, was a good experience last year figuring out how to play without that. [snorts] Um, and so I can pull that out if I need to, and I'm sure I will at some point in the future. You know, football's a physical game, but [clears throat] um, my legs are a big part of my game. >> Are you just pleased with where your speed's at overall during the season? Yeah, right now I'm pleased with how I feel, how I'm operating, how I'm lifting, my strength and conditioning. I'm pleased with it all. >> Over the course of a season, how long does it take to for you to get acclimated to game speed and really get a good game feel as the season goes on? How long does it usually take for you? How many weeks? >> Well, it depends. It depends. You know, early in my career, a little more than than now, I hope. Hopefully, seven years in, it's it's pretty pretty instant. >> Is it you talk about being a reps guy over the years? Is it hard to go for for several months without playing and getting out there first week, especially for how little you play season? How much is that like try to get a feel for that that especially week one maybe two? >> Yeah, for sure. But, you know, everybody's in the same spot. Uh I think early in the season, there's just a lot of [snorts] everybody's getting their feet under him. the timing with the receivers, um the contested catches on the outside, the tackling from the defense, the the speed of the game up front, offense and defensive lines, and so, you know, the first couple weeks it's whoever can adjust to that more quickly. >> I know in the past you've talked about not really being on social media much, especially during the season, but you know, you are human. You see TVs, you I'm sure hear from your friends and family things that are being said. Because of your stature in the league, it's felt like everything you say when you come on this podium, it's dissected on TV in articles for the next week. Has there been anything in in the last year, maybe the last six months that you know you've seen or heard that you just thought was completely taken out of context that that bothered you in particular? Do you just not even pay it any any close attention? Um, no, no, there's nothing that that I've taken particular offense to. Um, that's the life that we that we live. You know, it's not uh thing things that that we say are going to be interpreted in a lot of different ways. And, you know, Hobs and I talked about this the other day. I'm very efficient with my words and so that leaves a lot of room for interpretation sometimes. And um that's fine. That's fine. That's uh number one, it brings attention to the league. That's a big reason we get paid so much money is because people care about it. People want to watch it and people watch these shows and want to watch us on Sundays and love us and hate us and everything in between. That's what's so great about the game. And so, um people have a right to say and write whatever they want. And then I you know when you're younger you maybe take a little offense to it but you know it's like that's just what happens. >> Was there a certain point in your life where you became less bothered or unbothered by people hating you in your in your world? >> No that when I when I established myself in in the league I would say it was a turning [clears throat] point for that. You know, when you're younger, you're emotional and intense and you know, you especially the way my college career played out, you take any motivation anywhere you can get it. Um, but now I'm intrinsically motiv motivated. I'm not externally motivated. So, uh, you know, as you get older, that's kind of a switch you got to make. >> Anything make you laugh? >> It all makes me laugh, man. It's all It all makes me laugh. It all makes me laugh. But it's all good. You feel like the biggest key is for y'all to start quickly, especially with the opponents you have. You have Tampa one of the best runs in the league. What's the biggest thing to make sure you start quickly to give you all a shot at going two and0 through week two weeks? [clears throat] >> We you got to play fundamentally sound football early in the season. You know, your your tempo in and out of the huddle, your substitutions, um your play calls have to be correct. You got to line up correctly. You got to be dialed in on the snap count. No pre- snap penalties, you know, that's early in the season. and that gets you so far. Um, and then just put the ball in play, make them tackle. You know, no defenses have really tackled for however many months since last season. Uh, you know, a lot of these starting defenses either had a couple series in the preseason or or none at all. So, just try to get the get the ball to your playmakers in space and let them go to work. >> Now or never mentality that you've had at least this offseason and spoken about it. Was there a switch where this happened? Were you rehabbing last year and realize this is the mentality you had if you had it and now you're just speaking about it? >> I don't know. That's just uh just how how I felt lately. I just want to try to bring urgency and intensity to every situation that I come into uh interact with. >> So much talk, Joe, about under center where you guys were at the beginning of camp in spring. How do you feel about where you are now under center and your comfort level with it? Your confidence in your teammates to run it as opposed to where you were at the start of camp. >> Yeah, I feel great about our our whole offense right now. You know, I think we can do a lot of different things. We're going to be multiple in our formations and and our looks and our play calls as well. Uh and we can go and execute any way that we need to to to go and get the job done. When you look around the league, are there any quarterbacks you're looking forward to watching this season and seeing how they do? >> And there's so many great great guys across the league right now. I think the the league is in a great spot. Um, I think it's being played at a at a high level in in a lot of places. Certain places not so much, but you know, there's there's a lot of guys that are making great plays. And I think the the position is being played differently than it has for a long time, too. And I think that's good for the game. It allows it the barrier to entry at the quarterback position is as low as it's ever been. You know, you see small guys, tall guys, big guys, skinny guys, fast guys, slow guys, a lot of different ways to play the game right now. >> I'm not sure it was Sorry. >> I'm not sure it was unexpected, but uh Zach confirmed today that T and Jamar are on track to play Sunday. How do those guys look right now? And how big is that for you knowing that they're on track? >> Yeah, they look great. He look great today. He look great. Um, you know, those those are guys that Yeah. Yeah. You're going to be better if you get reps during practice, but guys that have seen a lot of football, played a lot of football. Um, a lot of times it's just about feeling good, getting to Sunday, and going out and executing. >> One of the top three favorites to win the NFL MVP this year. I know that winning the Super Bowl and the team success is the most important thing, too. Is that something that you're hoping could happen this year? >> You never know. You never know. You know, the thing about early season predictions is you can predict just about anything you want. And you never know if it's going to be true or not. We're My brother and I were talking the other day and he said, you know, I saw an article so so and so could have the best defense in the league. again. I'm like, "Yeah, everybody could have the best defense in the league before they play any snaps." So, they make a lot of predictions right now. None of it really matters until about week 9 or 10. >> Guys were saying that this is quite a lot. Camp is very sound defensively. What do they do best in your opinion? >> I think our Dline I'm excited to watch them. I'm excited to watch them. Those guys are going to get after it. Um, big emphasis in stopping the run, but those guys are going to be able to get after the passer. We got a lot of depth at that position as well. So, I'm really excited for it. >> The guys were saying that this is the most you've worked on situations, I guess, on both sides of the ball since Zach's been here. [snorts] I'm sure you like that. What do you think was, you know, spurred that and how do you think it's maybe helped you guys going into the season, that concentration? >> Yeah, we've talked about it a lot in the past and focused on it, but it certainly has been forefront of everybody's mind this year. I think just looking back at, you know, a lot of the situations that we found ourselves in over the last couple years and really across the entire NFL, every game is going to be a one-sore game halfway through the fourth quarter pretty much. And it's about what you do when you have the ball or when you're on defense in those spots. And so we've talked about that a lot. >> Across the game, it sticks in my view last couple. >> A lot of them. A lot of them. >> Across the board, your efficiency numbers get better as the season goes on. Um, do you have any reason why that might be? >> Oh, I don't. If you're not getting better throughout the season, what are you doing? You know, you get more reps, you're practicing more, you have more game reps to learn from, you know, you're practicing. You're in the building every day. So, if you're not growing and learning from day to day, what are you doing? >> Baker all day. >> Sorry. It's all good. Uh Baker got his contract done right around the same time frame that you did a few years ago right at the start of the season. Is there anything that did for you mentally going into the season that year having that done? >> Not really. You know, once training camp starts that's kind of behind you behind you and you know way in the back of your mind. So it's certainly a great feeling when you know you sign that contract. But um at least for me, can't speak for Baker, but you know, when when you're in football, you're in football. >> What does it say about DJ Dax, the other guys in contract years, entering contract years that they've been, you know, in football and not let it distract them, not pop off to us and make you laugh, anything like that? >> Yeah, I mean, those guys are those guys are all ball. Those guys are all ball. DJ has done nothing but work his ass off every day to try to be the best player that he can be. uh you know, all he does is talk about ball, think about ball, ask questions about certain looks, try to get better. And Dax is the same way. Um I'm so excited to watch those guys. Those guys have been really good players for several years now. It hasn't really got the recognition that they deserve in my opinion for for being good corners like that, but >> they're topn. >> What's your What's DJ? he can be as good as he wants to be. Um, you know, he he always is just talking about trying to take the next step. He's already, you know, he's already so good, but that's what the great players do. They they're never good enough. They just keep trying to work to get better. >> You and Baker have uh, you know, have had all kinds of games, shootouts, bound runners. I mean, uh, what do you like about his game and what do you expect on Sunday with you and him going at it? >> Yeah, I love watching Baker. I've been watching Baker for a long time. He uh he's going to go make plays. He's going to make plays with his legs. You got to be aware of that. Um he can make every throw on the field. He's probably has the strongest arm in the league. He can laser some in there. He's fun to watch. >> Joe, the book on you has always kind of been not to blitz you. Do Do you think going under center more this year will invite more of that? especially this week with the Bulls defense. >> Yeah, I don't know. I don't know. We'll see. Um I think it depends on how effective you are at at what you're doing. You know, if we're getting under center and ripping ripping the run game, you know, we'll probably get some more run stop run stopping blitzes than than in the past. Um but, you know, if we're dicing them up in quick game and and throwing the ball down the field, you probably won't. And so I think it's just going to depend on the game, depend on the coordinator, and depend on how we're playing. >> There's been a lot also to that point about your supposed comfort seeing the field, reading the defense from shotgun as center as you've grown in the league, you can you feel yourself getting more comfortable under center and reading the same way or can is it a totally different read under center? >> Well, it's different. you have a different mindset really when you're when you're under center versus in the gun and different concepts that you can run. Um, so you're really you're kind of playing a different game and yeah, I'm very comfortable with with reading what I need to read when I'm when I'm under center. You know, you take a quick snapshot when you get the ball and then your back turns and you have to find your picture again very quickly. Um, that's something I've been working on. >> Did you watch any tape of other center quarterbacks or guy specific quarterbacks when they go into center? to watch any tape anyway? >> No, I got two two old guys in the locker room that have been doing it for a long time that that I get to talk to every day about that. >> How helpful have they been both of them now that you have Josh as well? >> Yeah, constantly learning the game and those two are a great resource. Um, you know, try to take anything from that you can. You know, you you're always looking to get better, looking to improve. And those guys have seen a lot of football and been coached a lot of different ways in a lot of different systems. So when you have a wealth of knowledge like that, you'd be a f fool not to take advantage of it. >> Josh has probably been in every office. >> He probably has a I bet he's played under just about uh half the coordinators over the last 25 years probably. >> Oh, sorry. Go ahead. You talked about not getting frustrated when people say things, not getting caught up in your emotional response and things like that. >> Is your excitement the same as it always was going into the season? Like, do you still get as excited as you as you always did? >> I would say I would say I'm more excited this year than I've been in in in a long time. I think uh I I've always been excited to play, but this year I'm excited to watch, too. I'm really just really excited to see our guys go make it happen. >> Thanks, Joe. >> Thank you, Jeff. >> Thanks, Jeremy.

title: Zac Taylor Press Conference - September 9
text: [music] Go ahead, >> coach. As you get ready to face a Todd Bulls team, talk about his defense, maybe the things that are his staples that you have to prepare for. >> Well, I mean, Todd's been doing it for a long time. I mean, he's got a lot of respect for the pressure they put on you defensively. He's been a coordinator since the late 90s, you know, really is when he started and he's been doing it 15 years in this league calling defenses and so, um, he's fine-tuned exactly how he wants it. He's got the pieces he likes and makes it challenging for an offense. Um, the last time we played him really was 2022, you know, a long time ago. So, again, it's your works cut out for you whenever you're preparing for it. He gets those guys to play violent. They give you a lot of different looks. they do a good job rushing the passer. Um they try to knock out the run game. So, um he's got a lot of guys on staff that he's been with for a long time dating back 10, 15 years probably. And you know, so again, it's um they've got our respect and our attention and we got to have a great plan for him. >> On track to play something? >> Yes, they they'll continue to do more and more every day, but I like the pace that they're on right now. >> Will go forward. >> Shamar will keep working towards that. Yeah. So, I won't um make any predictions how it's going to end up this week for him, but um I think he's feeling a lot better every single day. Monday felt good and we'll just progress him this week and see where it ends up. >> Before you got hurt, what did it look like with him? All the new additions there to have him in the mix there. >> He played two plays in training camp. >> OTA when you kind of saw him like what? >> That's good. I think we have good depth there and and [clears throat] he's a a guy we view as an ascending player, you know, in year two and so just the more work he can be, I'm I'm up on his future and now I just got to get him back in the mix and get him in pass and get him all the work he can get to catch up. A lot of respect for Dax and so I'm I'm excited that we've got him back in the mix here. >> Is it realistic for Shamar to be ready for for Sunday? Can he >> It's a possibility. It's a possibility. Zack, the whole offseason, Joe Burrow was talking about just how different this team is and obviously all the offseason optimism level is at a high team. Can you talk about what you've seen just so far in the preseason? What makes this team different from years past? >> We got great leadership on our team. What what makes a difference is hard to say necessarily, but I just think we got a lot of high level players that believe in what we're doing. They've put in the work number one. So, it's one thing just to talk and declare expectations. It's another thing for the work ethic to match that conversation and I've seen that work ethic match the conversation for our guys. They have a lot of confidence. A lot of guys have been there, done that, know what it's supposed to look like to be on a championship caliber team, know the work that's got to be put in and the standard that's got to be shown at every position. I feel really good at every position on our team that we have the leaders who have shown the way of what it's supposed to look like. Um it doesn't have to come from the coaches every day. We've got it coming from the players and we'll continue to challenge them that way. Um, but I like what I've seen so far. >> What made you uh you went heavy in situations. The guys said it was the most situations they've ever worked in the match. >> What uh what uh made you do that? >> Well, we were in we've been in so many of those situations in years past. And I think um when you have a staff, that's the benefit of the staff returning. And we've gone through the installs, especially on offense and special teams a million times over the years. Al and his group two years now feel really good about a lot of guys returning and so now you get a chance to spend not just time on scheme all the time in your area but situationally as a team we were able to dedicate I mean I'm talking five minutes extra a day you know it's not like anything earthshattering but you just get a chance to really show our players the video of the situations we've been in last year that have decided games last two years get a chance to just do them in practice and really focus on them and so not just get up there with the video and give the speech and Hey, we got to be better in this situation to end the game or be a situational master in this situation that comes up with 11 seconds left in the half once a year. We've really put the work in on the practice field and made our players go through those exercises and coaches go through those exercises and um you learn something new every year. Like I've been here, this is my eighth season and there's still situations that came up um week one Atlanta Tampa Bay last year at the end of the game. Atlanta's got the ball twice, down three, balls on the 30, 16 seconds left, no timeouts. You know, what's your mindset there? What are you What are you trying to put yourself through? He's trying to go to score a touchdown. If you throw it in bounds or take a sack, the game's over and you're down three. And so there there's still situations that you put yourself through the exercise every day and and uh our players and coaches have all been involved in that. >> Did you put the did you use real concrete examples from the last two years? >> Absolutely. Yeah. Us or them? us or other teams that sometimes, you know, a situation you've talked about a lot, but you've just never actually had to do it. We haven't been in a ton of like down clock situations where you got to complete the ball, get down, spike it with one second left like Chicago had in the preseason against us. We've we've repped it a billion times, but it's maybe happened once or twice in in the last seven years here, one of them being 2019 in Miami. So, um you know, those are things that sometimes you just have to show other teams doing it because it just hasn't happened to you yet. pitch told us um Zach that the first thing he put up on the board this morning was our offense is going to be what it has to be to win the game. But how do you think you guys are suited better this year to be that kind of team? >> Experienced. I think our guys um can handle the amount of scheme that we put on them because most of them have been here a long time. There's other guys we're trying to get up to speed as quickly as possible, but I just think we've >> [snorts] >> um played games a lot of different ways over the years and we have the ability to be who we need to be to win that game and and pitch has been he said that in the springtime really is when he first said it and um I feel good about that. I I feel some of our best years were exactly that if you go game by game on how it looked for us um we were able to evolve to being an attack mindset for the defense we're playing against. Um, but be also sometimes if a team's trying to dictate, we're comfortable, you know, living in a world where where we can we can do a lot of different things to to affect you. And that's that's our plan on offense right now. >> How much is critical to Joe being on board really with that? >> Joe's been on board every step of the way. I mean, we that that's part of just the relationship over seven years is this isn't like a once a month conversation. You feel good about this. It's an hourly conversation. Um it's a Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday conversations, Saturday morning. Um where are we at for the week? And so it's not this blindsided by, you know, we repped this play 3 weeks ago and I really don't like it. You know, we're going to have that conversation right then. And so I think that we're all on the same page and um feel really good about the communication process for all of us. >> For the majority of Burough's career, he's made some huge plays plays with his legs on third down. Last year, he was coming off a toe injury. Mhm. >> With a full year, a full off seasonason, how how much can that be that that mobility be a part of his game? >> It's a weapon. I think every great quarterback in the league makes plays with their feet, you know, and they makes they make plays when there's not a play to be made. Um they make plays when you have that gut in your stomach saying, "Get rid of the ball. Just let's punt it." Um and those guys go make a play for you and extend the drive or score touchdown, win the game for you. And it's any team that's got high aspirations, their quarterback usually is able to do that. And there's a balance. There's there's times in the game where you don't need that play all the time. And I think he's continued to learn that over the years with experience of when that time comes and when it isn't. Um you get a feel for how your defense is playing, how your special teams is playing, and okay, it's not that game where I need to do this. I just got to manage the game. And so I think that's just part of playing quarterback and calling the game as well and communicating throughout that game kind of what what type of game this is evolving to. >> Years that he's a big rep's guy. Are there things that you can do as a play caller or schematically to help get settled in early in the season, weeks one and two when he hasn't really had a lot of games? >> Yeah, it's it's hard. I mean, you got to feel feel out the game a little bit from their standpoint. I mean, last year we had three possessions in the first half against Cleveland. Three. Scored on two of them. We had eight or nine normal down plays in the second half. So there was no rhythm, you know, it just that was just the way the game played out. So it's impossible to predict if we're going to get 45 plays in the first half or we're going to get 12. And um we'll have a plan for how we plan on starting the game. And and you got to be willing to adapt, especially in September to something they're doing that's different on defense than you prepared for or something maybe you've you've found a rhythm with that you want to stick with. Um, so it's not possible to predict how the first half is going to shake out to be able to get him in rhythm, but we'll have a plan in place that we feel good about. >> Baker Mayfield signed his contract this week. Uh, that's different. So, I I think that was just a unique situation kind of how I wouldn't compare um compare those two situations. >> Talking about Baker, uh how is his game evolved in that? >> I got a lot of respect for Baker. Um I'm from Norman, so I got a lot of friends and family that have been Baker fans for a long time. And he's one of those guys that they they cheer for endlessly. Like, he's really impacted their life. and and um I don't even know they won they didn't win a national championship or anything but just the way he played he really impacts people. So that's what you see from him um especially at Tampa and just the way people talk about people when he was in LA just the effect he has on them and his teammates and so he's an elevator. You see somebody that elevates those around him and he's a playmaker. He's a fierce competitor. Um got a lot of we've seen him on this field many times. um he's played well on this field and so our defense has got to come ready um because he always does and you know we got to get the best of him. >> Speaking of effect u the effect of the fan base here team has done a great job with the strategy open in orange the white just talk about opening day open in orange and how the fans really inspire this team. It >> they really do. I mean, the the our stadium environment is is tops in the league and uh I get that feedback from opposing teams a lot that maybe haven't been there. It's a new coach on a new staff and they come in here and um after game it's they're really impressed by it and I just think it's it's really grown over the years especially and I'm excited. I mean my family's excited. They're all I got to make sure they all got their orange jerseys and orange shirts and whatever they're going to wear to the game and um because they got to do their part and we got to do our part and so we got to give them a reason to be loud. Our defense has got to play well out the gate so that on third down as soon as the second down play ends and the 40 second clock starts our fans are allowed as they're as Zach Robinson's trying to call the play to Baker in the headset at 36 35 seconds. That's when you got to be at your loudest. So he's got to repeat it. So then when Baker gets in the huddle, he's got to repeat it again because the tight end on the other side can't hear it. And then when he gets to the line of scrimmage with hopefully six, five, and he's got to make an adjustment, they can't hear him and they got to take a timeout. So that's that's what home field advantage does for you. Um, we got a really smart fan base that has always given us that advantage. And so we just got to have an environment that's unmatched. We're capable of that. I've seen it happen a million times. I'm really excited. I'm glad we're opening at home. We give ourselves that opportunity. That is an advantage in week one. and we got to take full advantage of it. >> Your starting linebackers have openly talked about wanting to prove what they're about and how much they've improved. >> Ours are yours. >> Ours. Okay. >> When you're looking at year two of a young player, what what's a sign of growth and improvement for Demetrius and Barrett starting on Sunday? >> Reaction. I think reaction time, pre- snap communication, postnap reaction, those are things that have just continued to slow down as they felt more comfortable. They were thrown into the fire last year. Demetrius week one. uh Barrett, whatever it was, weeks six, seven, eight, and you had to learn on the fly. And so now there's just that confidence of them and everybody around them. They know what to do. They know how to communicate. They know where to be. There will be things that get thrown at us that we maybe didn't get chance to prepare for because it's some new wrinkle they got this year. And I I trust that they'll be able to solve those problems on the field. >> Does week one feel like a normal game week to you like compared to the other 16 or is it different because of what it is? >> Yeah, there's so much buildup to it. you know, it's just the first game of the season and it's a fresh start for everybody. So, I I can't say it feels the same as other weeks. There's a lot of buildup to it. Um, but that's why we just try to keep our process as similar as possible to stay in our routine, get used to our routine again that we have from season to season and um just be ready to go on Sunday. >> How much more of a challenge is it mentally for you, Zach, to take chances in week one if you see the opportunity? Are you more conservative? Do you have any kind of sense for that? >> No, you just you got your plan of of where you want that and then you got to feel out the game as it goes to. And so I I think that's most games. Um to say week one is a different mindset. I wouldn't say that. Um I think it's once that first ball's kicked off, you get back into the game and you get into the flow of things. >> What does it say about your culture and your team that you have guys like DJ Dax and others in contract years? Yeah. And they've been around. It doesn't feel like a distraction. It feels like they're they're all in on the season. >> I'm proud of those guys. You know, it's I haven't felt it for one second from any of them. >> Um they've all come to work every single day. They've had a great mindset, great attitude. They've affected others the right way. Really proud of of that collection of guys that you're talking about. Um that have just been about winning and and they know winning helps them. you know, it's I think um Pitch said that this morning or Sulcen Jordan Sulcen actually got up there this morning and said, you know, it's it's part of this team having success is going to help everybody in this room. And so those guys have really taken on that mindset and embraced that. Knowing you're not gonna share a lot of what to expect on Sunday, but is Cashes far enough along as far as like what you guys have seen from him in practice and in meetings where you would feel comfortable putting a rookie like that out to have a significant role on in the play? >> Yeah, I won't speak to what his role is going to be, but he he to my recollection hasn't missed a day since he's been here. um been a part of every meeting, every practice, and gotten exponentially better and more comfortable with every rep. He's really attacked it. He has met extra. Um feel really good about where he's at right now. Now, how we decide to use all those guys remains to be seen, but um he's done everything he can to put himself in a position to be used at the maximum volume. >> How much did you watch Bane [snorts] uh draft? >> Yeah, a lot. >> Yeah. What did you what was your uh impression of [clears throat] him and how daunting is it with a guy that hasn't been deployed before having to prepare for how everything >> affects the game? I mean that that's the takeaway you had was um affects the game and you know he was paired with Mezador. Um now he's paired with Dyabi. I mean it's another great pairing with with great players in between. Um so definitely a force. He's going to be a great player at this level. He's already shown it. I mean, he played what, seven snaps against Kansas City and had a great rush that affected the down. And so, you've seen that um from him in college. You've seen it sparingly on NFL tape so far. And I expect him to have a great season. >> Thank you. Thanks, >> [music]

title: Dallas Cowboys Talk Week 1 vs Giants | Player Interviews
text: I mean, week one, just talk about your excitement to to get on the field and play. >> Uh, super excited. text: Yeah, he has, but I'm not going I ain't going to display what he's told us. Um, but we got major respect for him. He has major respect for uh Kyler and what he's been able to do in this league. title: Jordan Love: 'I want to go out there and be the best offense we can be'
text: How is US Bank Stadium as a as a road venue to play in? >> Man, it's a it's a it's a good stadium. Um, it's definitely a loud environment. Uh, you know, their fans do a good job. So um you just got to up your your volume in away games, but Sean does a great job. I think he knows the offense inside and out what he needs to call. Um and he's done a great job all camp with it. Um so this will really be our you know our first test to be in a real away environment and see >> Jordan, you've known all along you guys working to have Micah on defense start of the year. What do you guys have to do on offense to help those guys? Man, I think always uh the goal of the offense is put up as many points as you can. Um you know, I think that's our goal no matter who's out there on defense with with Micah, without Micah. Um you know, I want to go out there and be the best offense we can be. I want to put up touchdown every time we touch the field. Um so it's just about us going out there having our process, sticking to our rules, trusting what we see. Um you know, whatever they hit us with from a defensive perspective, just being ready and uh obviously having in game adjustments, but you know, I just want to be able to move the ball consistently down the field and put up points. Um and just you know obviously I think uh third down is that's that's the big one. That's the test always is can you convert third downs and stay on the field. So um for us it's just stick to our game plan to try and be as explosive as possible. >> With the uncertainty surrounding Josh the running game just how much responsibility does that put [clears throat] on you and just the passing game in general? >> Yeah, we'll see. Um you know I think for me no matter who's out there similar you know I want to be the best. I want to I want to go out there and execute my job at a high level and on every play. Um and so I think for the everybody, you know, the receivers, um you don't got to go out there and do anything fancy or or try and, you know, do anything more. It's just go out there and do your job, um and make plays. >> Matt's talked about your ability at the line of scrimmage every snap. Just over the years, how have you been able to elevate your your team in that regard? Um, I think it's just every year for me is understanding the offense a little bit more, understanding the protections a little bit more. Um, what calls I need to get to and being able to process everything a little bit faster. So, I think year after year, uh, you know, obviously you see more looks from defenses and, you know, as we go back, watch film, break stuff down, you figure out the answers, and then, you know, it just starts clicking when you're at the line of scrimmage. But obviously, you know, you get up there, you're up against the clock, stuff happens so fast, so you got to make some really quick decisions. Um, but I think it's just reps, reps after reps, and just understand what I need to do. >> Following that, where have you grown the most as a player in your years as a starter in your mind? >> Uh, where have I grown the most? I mean, I think uh that area is definitely [snorts] where I've grown the most since I've got here is just understanding protections, how to protect myself, how to make certain calls to be able to pick stuff up. um knowing when I'm hot and how to get the ball in my hands and so um you know never trying to I'm always trying to avoid the negative plays which is you know sacks not maybe not seeing a a blitz and getting hit in the back so things like that. So um I think that's where I've elevated my game the most and you know since I got here that's where you know I've put the most time in. I feel like just trying to understand this stuff and um something that when I got here I didn't do a whole lot of that in college. So uh definitely an area of my game that's improved. You guys have been working a month and a half, but what do you learn about your offense and your team in an open when you finally play four quarters together [clears throat] against another foe? >> Yeah, I mean that's when it's when it's real, right? You know, practice we we put ourselves through all these different situations and um things, but you know, when you get to a real game, that's when it's real. And we got to go out there execute um play at a high level. Obviously, um it's us versus them. you know, it's it's it's who's going to go out there and be the best team, who's going to execute the most plays, who's going to be the toughest on the field. So, um, everything's real. So, I want guys to go out there, play free, play fast.
