If something happens, you know, we'll talk about it later in the film room, but just go out there, play fast, be physical, um, and execute a high level. >> It's more this defense about the toughest, uh, read and diagnosed pre- snap that that there is. Yeah, he's I think he's got one of the best uh you know trickiest schemes I think you know at the line with everybody up at the line of scrimmage, all the different pressures they bring. So there's a lot of stuff you know for a quarterback to be able to see. It's definitely tough. Um and I I I think not too many other defenses are as exotic as they are. Um so yeah, >> what distinctively makes it difficult to diagnose? >> Just the different looks. You know, you'll get looks where everybody is at the line of scrimmage. They're blitzing. They're bluffing. uh guys dropping out. Um you know, I think they do a good job in a lot of their coverages. Um you know, being pretty sticky in coverages, but you know, I think it's just a lot, you know, a lot of different stuff to game plan for. Um a lot of different pressure packages. >> Is what Ganon showed you guys in training [clears throat] camp with all his stuff, is that at all like this or are they totally different? >> It's similar. You know, I think a lot of teams will do some similar stuff, a lot of stuff on third downs for sure. Um but you know, with a team like the Vikings, you can get that first, second down, you can get it whenever. So, um, you know, they're very exotic, but yeah, there's a lot of teams that do, you know, eight up at the line of scrimmage on on third down, seven up. So, uh, you know, JG going against our defense, they do some similar stuff, but there's always a couple little wrinkles that are different. >> Are you hoping Harrison Smith retired? >> I thought he was retired. Thought he was. Um, you know, uh, him coming out of retirement, you know, good for him. That's cool. Um, we'll see. You know, we we'll plan for him being out there and, um, adjust whatever the case may be. But, yeah, he's a very good player. So, got a lot of respect for him. >> Getting back to the call, Jordan, I recall something that you talked about with maybe it was Fox or something that you just basically just threw it hot at Utah State. Is that a fair assessment? >> Okay. So, what was a what was the rookie training camp like having to learn all this? And then B, how much do you relish that now? The cat and mouse, I know Erin was like with lock and stuff like that. How much you relish [clears throat] the cat and mouse at the line of scrimmage of I know what you're doing. I can make the get in the right spot. >> Yeah. Um, first part of the question was, uh, what was the first part of the question? >> Just how hard was your rookie training camp having to learn? >> Oh, yeah. Yeah. Um, yeah. I mean, like you said, in college, we didn't do really any protection adjustments as a quarterback. So, um, you know, I knew that coming in. All my draft prep was a lot of understanding protections and, uh, trying to break some stuff down, learn this stuff, and to be able to get on the boards and talk to the coaches. And then obviously, you get here, learning is just it's a lot. It's a lot to take in and and be able to digest and to go out there on the field and try and, you know, emulate the things you see on film and stuff like that. So, it's a lot. It takes time for me. It took a couple years to be able to fully grasp uh some of the protection adjustments and uh some of the looks I need to do stuff on. And I think just the confidence of in practice being able to try things and understand, you know, where you might be hot in pressures and and some of the adjustments you make. So, uh it's just a learning game. But, yeah. Do you like the mental challenge of that at the line of scrimmage having to deal with this? >> Yeah, it definitely is a a challenge like you said. Um, but I like it. You know, I like it. It's definitely rewarding when you make the right call and and it's picked up perfectly and you're able to uh, you know, put up an explosive play against the defense. So, that part is definitely fulfilling. >> Hey Jordan, I don't know anything about college football. Is what you did at Utah State with not having to decrease that responsibility for protection. Is that pretty common just when you talk with other quarterbacks or is that kind of Utah State thing? No, it just I think it depends where you're at. Um, you know, we are more of a no huddle fast offense where we're just getting on the ball and rolling. Um, so, you know, there's coaches really didn't want us thinking and making protection adjustments, just go as fast as possible. So, I think a lot of the offenses that are similar to that might be similar, but I've definitely talked to some guys that, you know, did some different protection stuff, ran more NFL type offenses. Um, so I think it just depends where you're at. >> Last week, Tucker was telling us that hopefully with fewer miles to feed that, that he doesn't have to share the ball as much. in past has talked about how the offense runs its best when he touches it at least once a drive. Do you agree with that assessment? And what's it like to have a player that wants the ball that much? >> Yeah, I love, you know, guys that want the ball and, uh, do good things when they get the ball. And I think Tug, uh, you know, that's what he does every time he touches the ball. So, um, he's definitely a guy you want to feed as much as you can, um, and try to find ways to get him the ball. Are there any of these guys that you're around now that you're throwing to having several years with him now where you look at it and like this guy's got to get this many targets a game like just to feed the offense, he's got to be able to hit this threshold. >> No, no. I mean, I think I I still look at it as, you know, I'm going to go through my progressions of what the play is called and try and get to the best option uh that's out there. You know, I never want to lock in on, oh, I got to I got to go to this guy every time. Um I just try and stay true to my reads and my progressions. Jordan, you said uh you said you like you [clears throat] really like being able to make that right call at the line of scrimmage, hit them with an explosive and you know, maybe they're coming after you. >> What's the flip side of that? Like I mean, how how frustrating is it when maybe it doesn't work out or you misdiagnose it and then how do you like bounce back from that? >> Yeah, I mean it happens. You might make a wrong call and all of a sudden there's nobody blocking, you know, somebody running right at you. So, it's like, oh, oh, you got to find ways to get the ball out or uh, you know, it's going to be a really bad play. So, you know, that happens a lot. And I think that's just you got to understand, you know, when you do make adjustments, things like that. All right, where are the weaknesses now? If if I'm wrong and I'm hot, where do I go to get the ball out? So, it's just understanding that part of the game, too, because that happens all the time. You know, you might make an adjustment, the defense gets you, they're disguising, showing one way, come the other way. So, that stuff happens all the time. It's just having answers. Um, so yeah. Jordan, what's it been like for you working with Janu Smith and just having a vet in the locker room and who likes to sit beside you in meetings? What's it like just kind of working with him, especially his familiarity with the floor in this offense? >> No, John has been great. Um, like you said, I mean, just he brings a different presence, you know, being a vet, being around the league. Um, he's played a lot of ball. So, um, I think for him coming in, like you said, he's been in some systems that are similar. Um, I think he's picked the offense up pretty quickly and he's obviously still learning every day, but um, you could just see how how quickly like he understands what he needs to work on and and learn and grow to be able to be ready for week one. Um, so just someone that he's a pro, you know, he knows what he needs to do and what he needs to work on and he's going to make sure he's ready for week one um, to handle whatever's thrown his way. >> Matt said he looked at the first team meeting, looked out for Jonno and he was he was sitting right next to you like the offset. Did that surprise you and whose seat did he take? >> Nah, nobody's seat. Um, and it's it's open seat right there. And no, it's it's it's a it's a free-for-all when you go into the team meeting, sit wherever. Um, but no, I'm glad he sat next to me. >> What's it like to not be the youngest team in the league for the first time as a starter? >> Uh, I mean, it's a Yeah, I mean, like, like you mentioned, I have vets um that have been around, been some other places. Uh, they just bring a different, you know, perspective um and and some some cool ideas for a lot of things. But, um, [snorts] I think to that point, too, it's one of those things you don't really think about. You know, it's just obviously I think the first year we had a lot of young guys, but after that, uh, you don't think about it, you know, especially on offense when you've been with some guys for a couple years and, you know, we have some chemistry built. Um, you know, I don't really look at it as we're the youngest, even though we were for a couple years, but, um, I think it's cool that, you know, we're not labeled as the youngest team now. Um, but it's not not anything that is a big focus for us. >> How do you how do you feel just going into week one? Do you feel anxious, excited? Did you lose sleep? What's this week like for you? No, I'm excited. Um I'm excited for week one and just get this season started. You know, I think training camp and preseason, uh it's just a very long grind. Um and so whenever you're get ready to go play some real ball week one, uh everybody in the locker room is excited. >> Do you think you have a new appreciation for how quick these seasons go, having been through a few now as opposed to three? >> Definitely. Um you know, I think everybody knows your rookie season is the one that's the longest. you know, that season feels even though I didn't play, it feels just endless. And then after that, the years just go by very fast. So, definitely gives you an appreciation to, you know, you got to can't take any day for granted when you're here in the building. Um, every week you got to attack it with the same mindset, trying to find ways to get better. Um, and try and go one and0 every week. But, um, you definitely see, you know, the more you're in it, how fast these things go by and how important every game is every week is, especially the later you get in the season. >> Per season as a father, too. How does that change things if at all in terms of routine and everything? >> No, it, you know, doesn't change much. Um, I think the the cool part about, you know, for me going on year seven is I've definitely found a routine, found things that work for me to be able to get my mind, uh, my body right heading into a week of game prep. So, um, I know what I need. I know what I need to look at to be able to get ready for the game and and how to get my body right. So, um, you know, I think everything makes that a little bit easier, but um, it doesn't change very much.

title: Head Coach Matt LaFleur Press Conference
text: Hey, hey, hey. sound. I don't Heat up. Hey. Heat. Hey, Heat. Oh yeah. Heat. Heat. Perfect. Number Hey, hey, hey. Hey, hey, It's ready to work. obviously Aaron Jones probably isn't maybe quite the guy you had back here a few years ago, but what you know what's the expectation and challenge facing a guy like that? >> I think he's still quite the guy. Um, yes, he's got more wear and tear, but um the guy's a dynamic player, dynamic person, and he can he can really hurt you. You talked about Harrison Smith the other day as kind of the straw discourage the drink for them. Just in what specific ways do you does a guy have having a guy with that veteran knowledge just impact the rest of a defense and does it make any difference for a guy like that that he's just arriving this week? Well, we we'll find out what type of a difference it makes, but I think, you know, he's been in the system for many years, so I I think it's going to be a pretty quick learning curve for him, and it's just going to be where he's at physically, which from what I've been told is this guy is crazy about taking good care of his body. So, I just think, you know, it it's another smart football player out there that's got a ton of experience and knows the system inside and out and it it definitely helps with their communication. >> Even before this year, Christian has been a leader for you guys in the receiver. He's obviously been healthy. He's put a big production with the arrangements that you made this offseason at that position. What how's his role changed? How have you seen him kind of elevated to the moment? Well, I think all those guys I I think really what what it's going to be is going to be more opportunity for for everybody in that room. Um or I should say for our three main guys. Um and we need them out there for as many plays as humanly possible. We we know that this guy, speaking of Christian, I mean I think all three of those guys are difference makers, but um you know, we need him out on the field for as many snaps as possible. Does >> that mean a lot of >> We'll see. Do you want me to give the game plan? >> Caleb Johnson. >> Yes, he's done a nice job. And I think it it does help. I would say that there was some carryover, not only from when he was at Iowa with Tim Lester, but also with Arthur Smith, who I've worked with before, and then he had Aaron there. So, some of the terminology is the same. >> You've obviously faced players you've coached before. or what sort of advantage do you think maybe you guys have that JG spent the last couple years with Kyler? >> Well, I'd say he he knows exactly probably what he likes and doesn't like. So, but again, it's it's a different scheme, a different system. There's 10 other guys out there and I think that's a pretty pretty good supporting cast he's got around him. There's a lot of playmakers out there. I think their O line is one of the better OS in the league. So, they've got a lot of talent around him. How confident are you that Banks and Zack will be able to go and go full? >> Well, I think we just we're going to take it one day at a time and see where they're at and they'll be out there in a limited basis today and hopefully we can build up upon that throughout the course of the week. >> Are you hopeful that tomorrow's um initial court appearance provides any clarity on Josh's status moving forward? >> Yeah, we I mean the the more clarity the better, but um yeah, it's just wait and see. Eric Wilson had a really good year last year. Um, I think four forced fumbles, which is I want to ask about. How worried you have to be of of guys like him and maybe some of the other guys too as far as >> Well, yeah, I think I mean I think they forced 21 takeaways as a defense last year, which I mean that's pretty solid. Um, they do a great job of attacking the football certainly punching at it, raking at it. Um, but also just the pressure that they put on and they get a lot of strip sacks on the quarterback or they make make the quarterback make a rush decision. And I think you can tell the whole defense is tied together in terms of the the rush and the coverage. And sometimes on the back end, those guys will play a little bit more flatfooted and and being able to anticipate that the ball's got to come out. >> Matt, you might not care for this question, but where would you rank? >> Why would you ask it then? asking anyways. Rank US Bank Stadium in terms of the toughest places you've had to play. >> It's up there. It's definitely one of the toughest, especially you talk about week one. Um I think we all feel week one, the excitement around it. You know, it's got a playoff type feel to it. So, it's that'll be a challenge. >> You feel like you've handled Noise though pretty well over the years, not just at Minnesota, but obviously for field and so on. >> Depends on the game. How' we do? >> Okay. communication. >> Yeah, I think for the most part I think we we got smart guys that and it's not like we're reinventing the wheel and and throwing a lot of new stuff at them all the time. Um but that can get a little dicey and I think it's a combination obviously the environment for them and then just all the different looks that they present from a defensive standpoint. You've been very complimentary throughout the offseason of just the progress Jordan's made over the years, but I'm just wondering what's the next step he can take in his game to get to kind of that elite level where >> I I I get so confused by that question every time because I think he's an elite player. So, I don't know. I'll let you guys figure that out what what the next step is. I think a lot of times it's it's due to team success and the more success we have, the more people will view him in that light. And so >> that how does uh when you're uh incorporating Jonno Smith, so he he has some background with you. You think he knows everything at this point? You could use him any way or do you have to, you know, limit some of the ways you can use him? >> Well, I think the advantage of when you have a game plan, you kind of pair things down. So, I think absolutely he's 100% locked in, dialed in to what we're asking him to do. Um, and a lot of it's just going to be where he's at physically to see how much how many reps he gets. >> What have you thought about his condition? >> I thought I mean it's looked great. I mean, he's a guy that takes care of himself, his body. He looks great. Um, I haven't heard any complaints from him, but certainly there's a lot of familiarity with with where he's been in the past and what we do. It's kind of hard to believe that with a way that you know this guy is >> um well I would say the confidence in him really grew I would say about midway through that first year. You know I think early on we I'm talking about me. it was trying to uh protect the quarterback a little bit more and then when we kind of just let him let him go. Um I mean he did it. So I think the first year but you know obviously you guys may think different. >> Matt, if you guys go more of a by committee at running back, what what have you seen Chris Brooks be able to do when he's carrying the ball as opposed to just pass blocking? >> Yeah, I think he's done a nice job. I think you saw it last year. He he got a lot of ops versus them. um in that week 17 game and I I know he was out there and um but all their their starters were out there. So um yeah, I've got a lot of confidence in Chris. >> How important is it to get off on the right foot and finish for this game for some of the games you guys didn't do that last year? >> That's important. I mean, this is week one NFC North rival. Um, I think I think every game's incredibly important, but I mean this is the one staring us right in the face. So, it it's absolutely important that we get off on the right foot. >> Banks has missed a lot of time at camp obviously. If he is able to go, is he your starting left guard or do you have to be careful with what you do there? >> Well, we'll work through that. I think yes, the to answer the question, if he's able to go, he he's the starting left guard. Um, and then we always we have contingency plans after that. >> As Cincinnati gets ready to make his debut, just what stood out about his progress during the training camp in terms of learning as he went along? >> Well, he's hyper competitive. You can see that with every with every rep. Um, I think this guy, he he lives and dies football. He's constantly I mean, I'll get a random text from him asking me who are the top corners in the league that we've gone against since my time in the league. So, um, and he's he always wants to meet with with Bobby and and DB and JG. So, I I just think he's a he's a football junkie, and I the the progress is just come through the reps, the repetition uh, and the experience that he's gained through those reps. >> Is there an identity with the team right now or is that something that you guys just kind of build whether that's week four or week five, week 12? Do you kind of build that identity now or is it kind of a work in progress kind of thing? >> It it better be on display week one. So that I mean that's that's obviously the emphasis. >> Man, I don't know if you remember last year's game here. There were a couple times that you know there were some free runners right at Jordan. Um he made a couple really nice throws off of that too. Uh in general when you're playing a floor >> Spoon I do remember those plays. They are I've seen them too many times this week. >> When there is a free runner like that, is that generally a missed assignment or are there just going to be times because of the defense that they run that there's going to be a free runner? >> Well, there there could potentially if they got more than you can block with, then they're going to get a free runner and the ball's got to go and you got to have a hot throw or an answer for that. But I would say in that game specifically, there were a few times where, you know, we didn't have everybody on the same page. And I I quite frankly, I showed some of those looks today to to show them that, yeah, we got we got lucky in some of these instances where it didn't really bite us in the butt. So, um, yeah, we've got to we've got to be on it. Matt, how much growth have you seen from Anthony [clears throat] Belton as he's been spending time at swing tackle and just what he's, you know, how much progression he's been? think it's just again, it's it's always hard for a younger player. I mean, we've had him at guard, tackle, moving him all over the place. Um, but kind of letting him settle in and um I'm happy with his progress. >> Last one. >> Do you get more amped up, Matt, for week ones? Obviously, it's not your first rodeo, but do you get more fired up as as your as your coaching career goes along? >> I get amped up for every game. So, I'm going to try to be calm, cool, and collected this year. >> Thank you guys. >> See you.

title: Trevor Lawrence Speaks to the Media | Sept. 9, 2026
text: You guys sound pretty excited. >> It's week one. Come on now. >> Oh yeah. >> Good. I love it. >> Are you excited to see us, too? >> I am excited to see you guys. >> This is a better setting than sweaty after Bryce on the field. So, >> yeah. Air conditioning is nice. >> Yeah. >> Oh, what's up, guys? >> Did you still get uh Butterflies nerves going into week one? >> Yeah. Yeah, I mean I wouldn't say the nerves kind of in the tunnel right before the game is usually more so that. But I think just like I've talked to a couple guys this week about it just feels good to be at week one and game planning and prepping for an opponent. like you go in the training camp grind just every day installing kind of every play that you have in your offense and then you get to the end and you know you've just been doing the same stuff against your defense and um I think having the direction now of of preparing for an opponent and you got something to game plan for like that's the fun part and the puzzle you put together throughout the week and you're mastering your plan and getting ready like as a quarterback you love that because you know what you're doing and what you're trying to get get to every day. Um, so that's that's been fun and I think guys are really excited to be at week one. >> Trevor, one thing Le has talked about is challenging defenses outside the numbers and down the field. Do you feel like you and Brian made a lot of strides in that area? >> No doubt. You know, I think the um challenge really for all of us in our offense is how can every every part of the field be a threat? And I think that the guys have taken ownership of that. I think the some of the different plays that we've been able to put in and different route combinations and the way guys have ran them and got open all spring in training camp have shown um that they can do all that that you know we can make also I can make the throws and that every part of the field is a threat and I think that that's important for your offense to stay balanced and to um stay really effective in the passing game. So, I think where we're at as an offense in that department has been good and we got to continue to get better and now we get a chance to go showcase it on Sunday. Uh, but yeah, I think we got a good plan and just got to keep dialing in the details. >> I think Liam mentioned something about the standard being more player driven this year as opposed to last year. Coaches were kind of carrying that flag. Have you noticed that with the team? >> Yeah, I think so. Especially as we've all gotten more comfortable together and we kind of know what to expect. Like last year when there's so much new, you got a new staff, some new players, you're all coming together for the first time. Some of us have played together before, but you got a new system and there's so many different moving parts that you're trying to get used to and learn. Um, you're learning personalities and I think now there is that, you know, familiarity with each other and, you know, we can step up and we know, we know the standard. We've talked with our coaches a ton and I've talked to Liam, I've talked to Grant, I've talked to Spence, we've all talked about kind of what the expectations are, what the standards are. And so I think that's the cool thing about as a player and a leader on the team, you know, not just myself, other guys. Like you can feel when that standard might dip a little bit and like, hey, we need to pick it up. You know, it's not really up to our standard today. And I think there's been multiple times in training camp where that's happened and guys have had to, you know, grab the offense or grab the defense or grab your position group and say, "All right, guys. Let's let's lock in. Let's get going here." You know, it's not been it's not been, you know, what we want to put out there on the field so far today. So, I think that's been noticeable and we got to continue to do that, especially in the season because it can't just be on the coaches to to push that every day. It's got to be a player, player driven thing. >> The way you've uh cut down your turnovers significantly from earlier in your career, especially the fumbles, is that just part of the maturation process that you've gone through as a quarterback or was there I know you obviously did some things to try and fix that, but they like just >> plummeted way down. >> I think it's a lot of things. I think it's a lot of practice, a lot of drill work, a lot of, you know, work in practice and individual of working taking care of the ball, securing it at all times when I'm moving, having two hands on it, knowing when to tuck it, knowing when to um, you know, knowing when to call it quits in the pocket sometimes and and to not try to be a hero all the time. So, I think there's a mix of all those things. The more you play, the more you realize when is the time to try to make a play and when is it not the time. I think that's just as important and that takes some time to learn and you know I think that's part of playing quarterback is you touch the ball every play and we we talk in our room a lot is we always talk about taking care of the football with all the other position groups and especially how we carry it, tuck it, you know, not get the ball punched out, but the reality is quarterbacks lead the league in turnovers every year because we touch it every single play. So how important it is to be detailed and to take care of it and that includes decision- making. So that's another part of it too, just to continuing to get better and better. And if you don't turn the ball over a lot, you're you're going to win a lot more games, and that's that's the reality. So just trying to do my part and get better at that every day. >> Liam said with regards to Tom Lun, of course, first time head coach, first time we're seeing this Browns offense, but same for the defense. Sounds like they have some of the same principles from when Jim Schwarz was a defense coordinator. How do you approach a first time DC and what you could see presented to you on Sunday? Yeah, it's always interesting playing a a team week one that's a new defensive coordinator and um I'm sure there's going to be some wrinkles, some things that um maybe are different that show up that we're going to have to adjust to on the fly. That's that's playing football. That happens a lot of games, even if it's teams that uh have had their D coordinator a long time. So, that's part of football, but I think just understanding the basics of what they want to do. I think we have a feel for that and um and and know what to expect. Now, there could be, like I said, something that's different on Sunday, but being able to react and not being so rigid in our plan and in our rules where we're not able to adjust on the fly. I think that's the biggest thing. And we've had conversations of of that and and knowing what we can do to adjust as we go. So, um yeah, I mean, they've been a really good defense even though it wasn't, you know, Rutenberg before, this defense has been really good for a while. So, I would I would imagine that some of the there's some similarities because they want to keep some consistency, but I also think that they could have some really good new wrinkles on whether it's third down, red zone, passing situations. You know, that's where it'll be interesting to see exactly what they want to do and I know um they're going to have a good plan and we're going to have to adjust accordingly. >> You feel like you've got enough more answers this year, year two with Liam, than you had in any previous year. >> Usually offensively in general. >> Yeah, you answering to whatever the defense does. Yeah, I think there there's just that now having a full year of doing it and we've seen all the stuff that we did throughout the season last year when you're when you're game planning, you can go back and pull from those things and say, "All right, we we did this last year. This is our check if the defense did this." And so, it's just easier because last year it was the first time you're learning a lot of these things. So, you're um trying to get it down going into that week. Uh and now we've done it before. So, you can look back on tape and say, "Okay, yeah, I remember this. You know, I got it." It's it's not having to really necessarily put as much thought into just learning what you're doing now. It's adjusting the defensive look and talking to to my guys about how to play off of that instead of just trying to figure out what to do. >> When you're going against a corner like Denzel Ward, what's the balance between respecting his game and, you know, what he offers and then still playing your guys offense and know you have a pretty good player match up? Yeah, that's all that's all every week when you play good good DBs in this league, that's a that's a battle of a lot of respect for those guys in Tyson as well. You know, I've played with him uh for for a few years here and so those guys are good players. We got good players, too. I mean, they know that they're going to we're going to throw at them that we're going to get opportunities to go at them and we got to make them count. You know, I got to put the ball um in places where only our guys can get it. Guys got to go and and make those plays whether it's down the field um or or wherever. guys got to go and and and go take it from them. So, I think that that's a real thing is knowing um where are our favorable matchups and that's something that you look at all week as you go into the to the game, but you also never want to let a guy take away one whole side of the field. So, you got to keep them honest and you got to be able to go win on on everybody. So, I think those our guys are ready to do that and we'll just see how it plays out Sunday. >> Lady Camp able to start connecting with March more often in that 12 personnel. What kind of weapon can he be when his range is out there with his under? >> Yeah, I think he's gotten more and more comfortable in the system and I think he started to play a lot faster as he's gotten more comfortable and knows what he's doing and I think you're seeing our chemistry come along as as camp's gone on and going into week one. So, I feel great about our tight end room. I've said it a few times during camp and I think he's going to be able to do some great things for us. I think it all starts up front like we talked about with the O line. Same thing with the tight end room of the willingness to block and he has that and I think that's going to serve us well and it's going to help him a lot. One because we're going to be able to run the ball but also he's going to get opportunities in the pass game because of being on the field because he can he can block. So I think that that all plays together. >> You went through the process of season ending injury having a rehab in the offseason and then making your debut. I think he's a great player, a great person, you know, does things the right way. So, he's always a guy that I'm going to root for uh besides Sunday for a couple hours, but he's he's the he's the real deal. Love that guy and always hoping for the best for him. >> Thank you guys.

title: Klint Kubiak and Kirk Cousins Presser - 9.9.26
text: Yes. >> Bobby once told me about developing young quarterbacks. He would set aside a series once a game predetermined like second series of the third quarter where that backup would play. Do you have in your mind, I'm sure you won't tell us when, but do you have in your mind like I want to get Fernando reps every game or no or do you have any or maybe not decided? Um, yeah. I think with that I probably wouldn't do the Bobby Bowen go in game one. We're gonna let our let Kirk go. But, you know, everybody's got to be ready. You know, the back if you're not if you're not starting, you got to be ready to go in at any given moment. That's whether you know it's whether an injury, whether performance, whether who knows, you know, the backup's got to be ready. So, that's that's no no position's any different. >> Fernando was listed number two on the depth chart. What what was it that you saw from him that made you comfortable for him to be the backup? >> Well, him and Aiden still got a lot of practice this week, so we could change our mind, too. They just let him keep practicing and getting better. >> Where have you seen the most growth in your offensive training camp now? >> Uh, we're still growing offensively and defensively. Special teams, we're we're a growing team and you find out about yourself in games. So, you know, that's we're going to find out a lot about ourselves on Sunday. Clint, uh, you got a couple players, Max Crosby and Brock Powers that were dealing with injuries last year coming off injuries. We didn't see Max during the preseason. Just a little bit of Brock Powers. Are both of those guys cleared to play and are they ready to go on Sunday? >> Yeah, we're expecting to have all our guys ready for Sunday. >> Follow up on Q's question. Undecided right now on quarterback two for Sunday. >> Yeah, but Scott Fernando on as number two on the depth chart. We want our guys to compete throughout the week at all positions. coaches. Week one, game one. How much of a tone setter can this be um leading up towards the rest of the season? >> Yeah, we know it's it's a long season. You just want to put your best foot forward at 17 sprints in a row. So, we got our first opportunity on Sunday. >> What are you looking for as far as, you know, Max and Brock getting back out there because we didn't see much in the preseason. How excited are you to get those kind of guys back for your team? Yeah, obviously it it'll be great, you know, um just all all 22 playing together, you know, all four quarters. It's going to be a four-court game. >> It has been a same story around here a long time where teams are doubling into triple max because there is no threat on the other side. How critical for your team success is to someone else emerge as a pass rush threat? >> Yeah, we have the guys that that can do that. You know, we got great compliments to Max and that's not just a defensive line. our linebackers, our our DBs. So, uh you know, we're just worried about ourselves and getting better today, getting better in this next practice and preparing ourselves for for Sunday. >> Have you guys decided on team captains yet or when you'll decide on that? >> We do it every week. >> Yeah. >> Have you allowed yourself to kind of take in this being what you've been wanting to head coach first NFL game and what what do you think it might be for you on Sunday from emotional standpoint? >> Uh no, it's it's a game. It's it's not my first NFL game, you know. It's It's our first game as a staff, our first game as a as a team. Um, that's what I'm excited about, the us part of it. >> On the other side, Miami, new head coach, new quarterback. How do you prepare for a team like that being in a similar situation? >> Well, it's game one for everybody. There's there's unscouted looks, there's unknowns. Um, so you worry about yourself, focus on yourself, and being the best version of ourselves. >> With the speed of Devon Aan, how much are you guys focusing on limiting explosive runs in going into Sunday? He's an elite player. He's he's going to demand all of our attention. >> And at this point in his career, what do you see from Kurt Cousins from a physical standpoint? >> Oh, he's playing he's playing good ball. You guys you guys saw him in the spring. You know, he's ready to play. He's starting for a reason. >> To follow on Sam's question, 15 years at the quarterback position, like what traits are required to be able to have the kind of career that Kirk has had sustained what he sustained? >> I think the number one thing is thick skin. you know, you better, you know, you you've been through a lot, wins and losses, success, failure. Um, anybody that's played that that much football has had a lot of failure and has failed forward. I see Kirk in that in that light. >> What is the day each week where the captains are decided and what are the kind of the qualifications each week that that decide who the captains are each week? >> Yeah, you know, we we let them know we we let them know early in the week and it's it's, you know, coach's decisions. It's who we feel who we feel is is our leaders for that game, who's had a really good week of practice, who's someone that we want to reward for having a great training camp. Uh it's never one thing, but it's uh it's three guys, OD and special teams uh that we want going out in front of our team before kickoff. >> You talked about Kurt's urgency changing since you last saw him in Minnesota. How specifically have you seen that evolve? >> He's always been urgent. I think he's he's just he's got he's a better leader and he's more urgent than ever. When you when you play a lot of football, um you realize that, you know, sometimes what's said in the meeting on Wednesday, hey, this is what we think they're going to do on on third and 10, they don't do that. You know, you have to adjust. So, you're ve he's very um very confident in what he wants what he wants it to look like. Uh where he wants the receivers to be at uh where where the hots are, how we want to adjust protection. He's just extremely extremely confident right now in being just overcommunicating how it's got to be on Sunday and that helps that helps the whole team. >> What is wants to work on the culture for this organization and this team? >> Where is it at in your mind? And are you satisfied with the amount of foundation you've been able to build over a time? >> Yeah, we'll never be satisfied. We're always trying to get better. The culture is about the people in the building. You know, obviously it can start with us as coaches, but ultimately the culture is set by the the players on the field, and we're going to find out Sunday what we're all about. I really like the guys that we have. Um, but the players set the culture. >> Can you tell me about Cody White? What does he lend to this team? You guys were able to pick him up, add him to the practice squad, but what does he lend to this team and what does he need to do to make that step up to the 53? >> Uh, yeah, he's he's a very intelligent player, physical, reliable, obviously spent a year with him. Uh, a guy that's played really good football last year in Seattle and guy that we're excited to have on our team. >> You see Traden Stuks grow throughout the course of training camp in the preseason. >> Yeah, see his confidence grow every day. uh you you see his football IQ show up every day. Um it's his first game. Really excited about him going out and playing, putting his best foot forward, and it's going to be him and a lot of other young guys that that we're counting on. >> That's his leadership and his confidence. What's the best thing that Kirk brings to this offense? >> Leadership. Sorry. That's the best that's most important thing for a quarterback. >> Clint, are you expecting well Ash practice with limitations today or like how do you expect the practice to be for him? Uh, we'll give the designation after practice. He's going to practice. >> Max talked about one of the things that has changed for the better, his team dinners now on Saturday before the game. What was the idea behind that? >> Uh, in all facets, we just want to connect, find any reason we can to connect, players and coaches. >> You guys have worked hard all offseason to put together a team. Now it's week one at home, the home opener. How excited are you to put this team, this product out in front of the fans? >> I'm excited about practice today. That's how that's how we get that's how we get to Sunday. You can't get to Sunday by just showing up. We have to put the work in. As far as the fans, uh that will be something that's something I've been looking forward to for a long time. Our whole coaching staff, all of our players playing at home in front of the silver and black is a privilege. >> Who are the captains for week one? >> I'll let you know. >> Is obviously going to have a role in the passing week, but what do we other receivers have to do to gain their share of targets in your opinion? >> What you say one more time? uh whatever of a receiver >> I'm gonna go back to last I'm not trying to keep it a secret. Uh Kirk is a captain. We have Shaun. He is a captain. And we have Quay Walker. >> Uh what are the other receivers outside of Brock Bowers going to have to do to gain their share of targets in this offense? >> Uh everyone's going to get targets. You know, we got to spread the ball around to be successful. It's going to take a contribution from the whole roster, running backs, tight ends, receivers. What are some of the challenges of going up against Jeff Hafley as a defensive play caller? >> Uh, have a ton of respect for for coach's scheme and the how hard their guys play on defense. >> Good. >> Thanks, coach. >> Thanks, guys. >> And then it's like, oh my. >> Did you throw something in the TV? >> I didn't throw anything in the TV. No, but my friend sent me a t-shirt. It was brown with gold font. It just said Western One. So, [laughter] >> yeah. Yeah. yet. >> Uh have not have not. So, >> but um yeah, looking forward to uh getting this thing going. It's interesting how OTAAS is nine weeks, preseason, training camp is something like five or six weeks. So, uh there's just so much time that goes into building the foundation, but it's all for these next, you know, 17 weeks and hopefully more. So, um you know, you're kind of excited to turn the page from all that prep to to doing the real thing. and um you kind of feel that going into this week and be a great challenge for us. Excited to get in front of our fans and and um put our put our best on tape. So, take any questions you have. >> What you went through in 2023 then the last couple years in Atlanta, were there ever any doubts that you'd be a week one starter again? And how did you if so, how did you kind of quell those and get to this point? >> Well, I think you just never know what the next snap is going to bring, what the next week is going to bring, what the next year is going to bring. And I've I have learned in this league that anything can happen. So you keep an open mind in both ways. You don't assume anything and you just try to have great habits and um trust that if you do that that good things will happen. It may not happen as fast as you want, but um just try to have good habits and let the let the process go where it goes. >> What is being a week one starter in year 15 mean to you? >> Well, I think it's it's less important to me than you know what you do after that first snap. I think it's all about this entire season and winning the long game and not just about um the start of the season. So, wanna want to start fast, want to finish strong and and um you know, that's what all this preparation through the spring, summer, and and and August has been about. >> How are you feeling physically going into the season? >> Feel good. Feel good. And uh you know, the body work here is second to none. And so, we've got a great team of people here to to you know, make sure that that can continue. You >> mentioned all the words that put in. How much do you think you've grown with this offense over that time? >> Yeah, it's uh uh some is familiar to when I was with Clint and Andrew Janoko and Rick Dennis in the past, but there's plenty that that wasn't when I arrived and plenty that I needed to learn. And so that's what it's been about is trying to get that to be total ownership. And um now getting game plans, individual game plans, having total ownership because training camp is is more just installing your systems. And so now it's about game planning and um uh and just continuing to build on the foundation we've laid. >> Talked about how much you've grown since the last time he has coached you. In particular, you mentioned your sense of urgency going into this season, brand new team. Does this feel any different for you in terms of how big of an opportunity you want to take this year? >> I I don't know about different. I think every year one has a similar feel uh no matter where you're playing, no matter who you're playing with or for. Um, but certainly in a new place, you know, there's some differences where you you kind of have to say, "Okay, what is it like here? What's our daily rhythm here?" Um, and you kind of learn your team as you go. I think even though we've had so much time together through practices and meetings in the spring and summer, I think you still learn a lot about your football team early in the season. >> Going back to Holland and at Michigan State, you've always in the 20 plus years I've known you approached football with the same love. It's the same thing you had in in high school. How have you been able to now that it has become a business? Just sustain that love, pure love for the game. >> Yeah, I think um there is a passion for the sport that never leaves you. I think it is true that you know when you get to college and there's a scholarship and there's people's jobs in the line probably more than there was in high school or when you get to the pros and it truly is a business. Um it it has a different weight or a different feel than it did in high school or or recess in elementary school, but there's a purity to the game that you still love the blocking, the tackling, the making, you know, throws, standing in the pocket, um competing, you know, getting out of the huddle, just the challenge that that that is the game of football. Um there's there's a there I enjoy that challenge and that's never left. Kirk, the Dolphins don't necessarily have a lot of big names on their defense, but how do you assess them and do you think there's any underrated players on that side of the ball? >> There definitely are. Um, you know, Brooks, I believe, led the NFL in tackles last year. So, that's quite a statistic and says a lot about him as a football player. I played against him several times. He's had a great career. Um, played Miami last year, played several of those guys last year. They did a great job against against us in the game we were playing. So, um, yeah, they they do have a lot of good players. the the NFL, you know, they host that NFL throwback channel and they had their 100 greatest quarterbacks. You came in on that list. Is that a feather in your cap at all? You think >> this is the first time hearing of that? Uh the throwback channel though sounds right up my alley. I didn't know about it, but I've been known to to my wife's chagrin, watch some old games on TV late at night just because I I I'm I'm a sick puppy for it. So, uh uh I'd probably enjoy seeing the rest of that list maybe more than just seeing, you know, myself. But um uh it'd be fun too to debate with some people as well, you know, because you got your opinions on who you think the top guys are of all time and and why and uh um so it's fun. >> What do you what do you feel like you need to do to best provide success for this offense? >> Yeah, it's a great question. You know, I think it's always going to be about some of the same things no matter what time of the year it is or who you're playing. You know, you got to lead well. You got to elevate the other 10 guys in the huddle and the rest of the locker room with with the way you lead and your presence. Uh you got to be tough, you know, physically, mentally, emotionally. You got to protect the football. Um and you just have to run the operation well. Um and I think if you do that, you know, the plays will come to you. Um but uh this game is played one play at a time and that's the mindset I've always felt helps me best is to just take that that one play at a time approach. Spitech and Clint have really accumulated a lot of young players with high football IQs. You can tell they focused on that. As a leader with so many young guys, but that have that football IQ. How how much does it help you as a leader? >> Yeah, I would say it's not a difficult group to lead. I don't feel like teammates are obstinate or checked out. Uh you they have done a great job of getting uh mature people, people who football matters to them. uh guys you can trust and will be accountable and are coachable. Um so, you know, the key from there is because we're young, we got to raise up leaders. You know, we've got to say, "Hey, it's no longer time to just be a follower. Now we need you to really bring others along, too." And I think that's what some of this year will be about is is making sure that um you know, we we develop some some real leaders on this football team to impact this locker room and help us win a lot of games. Following that a little bit, Kirk, uh, a lot of your younger teammates have talked about just kind of your sense of humor and your dad jokes and whatnot. How does humor help you build relationships with guys, especially maybe when there's generational >> gap? Yeah, I think it's important to have fun, to let your guard down. Um, there's a time for being urgent. There's a time for showing how serious this is and how much football matters to you. And there's also a time to crack a joke, to have fun, to um, you know, be tongue and cheek. And so whether it's the cafeteria or whether it's in between snaps at practice, you know, you try to have fun, too. And I think it's important that that shows up on Sunday as well and that guys don't just feel the the stress of game day, but they also feel the joy of and the fun of playing football. So, um, you try to bring that, especially as an older player who guys are looking to and and, uh, you want to set a good example for them. >> Does leadership feel any different for you the past few years as opposed to maybe it did when you were in your 20s or early 30s? Yeah, I think when I was in year four, five, six, just starting out uh as a starting quarterback, I I think it would have been, you know, you're still a leader by nature of the position, but you just don't have enough experience up on the wall to really be able to uh take ownership. And I think uh the older you get, the more you can kind of say, "No, I I I like it done this way, or I need you to do this." And you can speak with a little more conviction. >> Your who has inspired your leadership style? Um, you know, I think it goes back to my faith and I I I look to, you know, Jesus is the ultimate leader. Um, my dad, you know, has been a guy I bounce a lot of stuff off of and I like to read books and kind of learn what great leaders have done. Uh, whether it's, uh, you know, Maxwell's books or Jack Welch's books. So, I enjoy studying it. Um, you know, everything rises and falls on leadership and so if you get great leaders, uh, that can really help any organization and so, uh, it is an important trait and that's why there's a lot of material on the topic. to that point. Um, you mentioned how vital Tom Brady's input has been, you know, a couple weeks ago. Has anything when you discussed with him changed your approach at all to how you're doing things in year 15? >> It's a great question. I I I've really enjoyed having him as a resource. I mean, I when I first got here, I was like, "Wait, so like I can just text him and he'll give me, you know, 23 years of pro football experience, you know, he'll text me back and they're like, yeah." So, and he made himself very available. It's been unbelievable to be sitting a meeting with Fernando and Aiden and say why don't we just ask Tom what he would do and you know sometimes you're like is he going to get back to us in a day or two and many times it's you know two minutes and we've got a response. So, um, that's been a a joy to have as a resource. And if anything, and certainly you can learn a lot from him that's new to you. But there's also sometimes some affirmation where you say, "Okay, I'm not crazy. This was what my gut told me was the way to do it." But the fact that he's saying that's the way he did it. Now I have a little bit more conviction and confidence in in what felt right. Now I know it's right because I know that it worked for him, too. So, um, I think that helps as well. >> With Ash having a minor step back, obviously him working off to the side and things on his own right. Anytime a player goes through that, especially a player as young as he is, it can be a tough road back mentally. What is your advice to him as somebody who's been around this league to really make sure that he can get back to full strength as soon as he can? >> I think it's one day at a time. And I think it's trust the um you know, the staff here and what they're telling him to do, trust them. And if you if you do that, take it one day at a time, trust what they're telling you to do, I think um you know, we'll he'll be right where we want him. >> What does a successful season ahead look like for you? Yeah, I think it's it's really one day at a time, one week at a time. I think it starts with trying to get a win week one and uh just kind of focus on the here and now, stay in the present. You know, I even get kind of like, let's just have a great Wednesday practice and let's just stay right here on Wednesday, doing the best we can. Um can't win the game today, but we can have a great Wednesday that gives us a better chance to win the game. So, that's kind of where my focus is and um I think that's helped me as a player to kind of stay in the present. you allow yourself to think about how long you want to keep doing this or >> um you know I think your mind goes there more in the offseason. I think once you get into it, you put blinders on and you're just going to work every day trying to be the best you can be and um you know and you have to earn the right to be in this league. You know, nobody's giving you anything. So um you know go play at a level that that says you should still be in the league and and and then let those conversations happen later. You >> obviously have a convers or relationship with Clint that goes back ways. What is it about him that really makes him an effective coaching team? >> I think Clint is uh committed to continuous improvement. I don't think he's ever felt like he's arrived or that he can just put it to bed and just let the system be what it is. I think he's always trying to evolve it. I think he's a great listener. Um I think he can adapt. I think he's uh details matter to him. You know, situations and there's urgency with Clint. So, there's a lot of traits that you want to feel and see from your head coach and from your coaching staff. And I think Clint has so many of them in spades and I think it helps him um you know lead lead us as a team. >> How much does that help him relating to players? He's not insincere. >> He isn't going to bloate. He's not going to he's going to tell you the truth, >> but he's also going to tell you if he doesn't know, how much does that help win a locker room? >> Yeah, Clint Clint is humble. He's hardworking and you can't be fake in this league. Players see right through it. And so when you realize, you know, after a few OTAAS, like teammates, you know, you start to see what Clint is like, I think they they picked up on what I've known for years that he's going to give you everything he has. Uh he doesn't make it about him. Um he cares about you as a player and as a person, probably more than many people in this business do. And so, uh he's going to do right by you and be honest with you. And those are things that you don't take for granted. And um and so it's it's one of the big reasons why I wanted to be a Raider. you have a little bit of a taste of it playing in front of the Raiders fans during the preseason. How excited are you to lead this offense? Put the product that you guys have been working so hard offseason and preseason this Sunday. >> It's a great opportunity for us. I think if you were at the game against the Niners, you could see the noise they brought at one point in the game when um you know there was some exciting moments down in the red zone and you could feel the noise and the energy and you and you know it was gave you the thought of you know what could be down the road here. So um that's what we want to want to do. But they're dying to cheer for us and we got to, you know, give them something to cheer about. >> Okay. Thanks, coach. Appreciate it.

title: Week 1 Will Anderson Jr. media availability | Full Q&A
text: You know. What's up? What's up? What's up? >> You know, a lot of people outside the organization are saying the Texans defense is probably going to be the best in the league. What do you guys think about that and how can you be better than you guys were last year? >> Yeah, I think first is ignoring the noise. Um keeping everything internally. Um I think that's a goal of ours, of course, but it's about how we show up every day if we want to do something like that. Are we going through our process? Are we having fun? Everybody executing. And when you execute, you win and you have fun. So, for us that's most definitely is a goal for us, but I think for us it's just, man, keeping the main thing the main thing and that's winning games and being the best defense. And to do that, you have to go out and execute every uh game. >> There's certain games in the year where they hold implications for come playoff time. This is one of those games depending on who can play at home in the playoffs. Is that something you address head-on and like make it a big thing or just like whatever, you ignore it? >> Yeah, I mean that's a good question. I think for us is we already said like this is a AFC Championship matchup. Two really good teams. We have a ton of respect for them. Josh Allen leading the way. Really great offensive line. Um uh James Cook, man, the best running back in the league, one of the best running backs in the league. So, um it's going to be a great matchup for us, but the type of atmosphere that I'm feeling like it's going to be on Sunday is going to be that AFC Championship type feel. Like I said, two really great teams battling out. They've been battling these last uh 2 years since I've been here. It's going to be a good matchup for us. >> You know, when it comes to the whole chasing and catching up with Josh Allen, what's involved in that? What does it take? >> Relentless effort, man. Relentless effort. Everybody swarming. Like we need all 11 hats to the ball. Plaster in the back end, swarming up front. The rush has to be on point. And I think this is what I love about this defense is everybody unselfish and I say it all the time and coach was showing clips today of just how it looks when everybody is on their job. When the back end is plastering, the defensive line is going to hunt. We all being relentless. So, to be the team like this to get to Josh Allen, it just takes relentless. Like you may not get him the first one, but man, pop back up and go get him again. So, for us it's just um four equals one. No independent contractors. Everybody doing their job up front and just giving the time giving the guys in the back end of op. >> What is that? When he was in Georgia and you were in Alabama, but what do you remember about James Cook and especially last year's game where he had that very big run to very kind of kind of start things out. What do you remember about him? >> Yeah, much hasn't changed. He's still explosive running back, man. He had some big games on against us. A lot of uh great runs against us in uh Alabama. He was on our um our scout report all the time. He's a really tough running back and he's so patient. He'll wait. He'll wait. He'll wait and he'll just explode to the outside and take off. But that's what makes him so great, man. He's not like a just a I'm going to go right now. He just tries to see and feel everything out. So for us it's going to be holding gaps. Everybody staying where they need to be, getting extension, playing with great eyes, great feet, and being in position to go make the play. >> Well, what's the benefit in having a group that is as confident as you all and not only confident in their abilities, but also confident in each other? >> Yeah, um it it it it's it's it's very important, I think. You look at it in all like phases of every position that we have. Um everybody shows up to work with the right mentality. And I think we don't gain that confidence um just by our natural athletic ability. I think it's the preparation that we put in week in and week out and how we watching film like today for instance. Coach had JP come up and be the coach and man, he killed it and we received that cuz it's like, "Bro, if JP can get up here and tell him tell us what his job it is what everybody else doing, that feeds the room." Cuz that's like, "If he can do it, why everybody else isn't doing that?" Like I should be able to tell you what the D-tackle next to me is doing. He should be able to tell you what I'm doing. And so that's how you get a great defense. When you know what everybody else is doing on the field and you can receive that, you go out there and play fast and have fun doing it. >> Along the same lines as well, does that help you as far as when you're playing that defensive line knowing that you have such great you know, defensive backs behind you? >> Oh, yeah, all the time. All the time. It's like we going to the game and it's a certain call or whatever. Be like you like, "We got Staine Kamari back there. We got JP back there. We got Reed back there. We got Caylin going sideline to sideline back there." So for us it was like, "Man, we just got to get home." Even if we just get a pressure or something to affect him, it's like, bro, like they throw that ball up in the air, one of our guys coming down with it because they all have elite ball skills, and I think that's what makes them so special. >> We're talking about how you guys were in training camp. DeMeco had you sit with some offensive guys. Vice versa, mix it all up. Is there a teammate that you sat with that some stuck with you and some either funny or unique or anything like that? >> Yeah, um I would say really listen to Dalton Schultz. Schultz has been a a guy that, you know, me and him actually have gotten a little closer, and I've learned a lot about him but to hear how he goes through his process and, you know, not to put everything out there but just his mentality of how he approaches practice, how he approaches his his real life, um just taking it one day at a time but, you know, having that balance of being able to be with his family and then be up here. I think that's something as a young player that you kind of, you know, you look at it like, how do I juggle all those things? But, you know, he's been great with helping with things like that. So, he's one player that I really looked up to, you know, during that time, really listening to him, how he balances his football life and his family life. >> What we got to How much does the success you guys had against Josh the past couple times, you know, obviously still same play caller and I use the head head coach. How much does that factor into how you guys approach this week um going into the season opener? >> Yeah, we always say last year is last year, and it's like, what we going to do this year? You know, they're going to come out with something that we've never seen before. They're going to have a play drawn up that we never seen before. But, how are we attacking our game plan? How are we going out there and executing it? For us, we've seen the success. Like I said, this is a really great team. So, there's no mistake about that. So, for us, we have to go out there and be on 10. You know what I'm saying? We have to go play our our brand of football. And so, last year, like I said, is last year. It's like, what are we going to do this year? Are we going to swarm this year? Are we going to get to the ball this year? Are we going to take the ball? And I think that's one of the biggest things, like, how many times can we take the ball? How many times can we attack the ball? And so, I think that's the growth from last year to this year, man. Let's take the ball from these guys. >> What would be your first time for C.J. Stroud? >> I'm sorry, can't hear you. [clears throat] >> you have for C.J. as he works through the same negotiating process that you went through? >> Yeah, I mean, at the end of the day, um it's all in God's hand and CJ knows that. Um we've talked, but you know, I think both of us right now, we're head-on going into the Bills game. You know, I think that's the biggest focus right now is man, we want to win these ball games and whatever happens after that happens after that, but man, CJ is locked in. He's been coming to work every single day. He's been bringing the guys along with him. The offense is looking really great and I can't wait to go I can't wait to go watch him spin on Sunday. >> Will you be playing on Sunday when we get CJ in here? >> Will this be your first time playing in front of, you know, the home crowd to open up >> Yes. >> the season? I mean, um on yesterday I got an opportunity to watch your mom, you know, in an interview with Hannah and she was talking about how excited you were when you first when you took your visit here. This is before you knew you were going to be a Houston Texan. What was it about this Houston Texans organization? What was it about [snorts] this city? What was it about DeMeco that made you so adamant in wanting to play here? >> Yeah, I would say man, it's the energy that I felt in the building from everybody. And then I had previously like I didn't know much about DeMeco until like the draft process came and then like obviously watching the Super Bowl and everything like that and like all those good things, but I seen the energy that he had and I seen and then I found out he went to Alabama and I kept following even more and then I seen that he was a defensive coach and he was a D-coordinator at the at the 49ers. And so when I got here, I could just feel the energy when I first met him. I mean, he was excited. I could tell like he's we shared the same mentality like man, whatever it takes mentality and then it bled through the whole organization. I met with Coach Ryans. Coach Ryans was the assistant D-line coach and he had energy from the get-go and that's just when he was the assistant D-line coach. And so for me like that's what I wanted to surround myself with when I came into the league. I wanted to be somewhere where I actually felt like I was wanted. You know what I'm saying? And that was always my biggest prayer is like God, I want to be somewhere where they actually want me. And I left that feeling like, yeah, I feel like this place is the one. title: Week 1 DeMeco Ryans media availability | Full Q&A
text: Hey, coach. >> What's up? Full house, let's go. >> When you go when you play a team that you faced last year, but might show different looks or might look a little bit different, like what's the challenge and what does the coach >> With this being our first game, anything goes, any looks, any type of schemes, anything can come up, so for that reason, I don't put any, you know, I don't put a lot of weight into the games that we played prior. But, hey, we got to go play good football. And we're excited to be in front of our home fans for the first time opening up for our 2026 Texans to showcase what we're all about against a really good opponent. It's going to be a great match up. I see Guys, get ready for a really good football game. They're really good team, they're coached well, they'll be prepared. Our team's good team, we're prepared. So, I mean, you you got to love it. NFL is back. We got a great match up to start the year. Man, let's get it. >> How do you How do you grade the margin of error coming into the first game? >> With the first game, you just have to be dialed in on the fundamentals, right? Protecting the football. That's the main thing for me. We have to make sure we protect the football really well. Tackling is always issue. Can't be an issue the first game. You just got to make sure, you know, you're putting guys on the ground, finishing. Some of our guys haven't had live tackling reps. So, we just have to make sure we're securing our tackling, make sure it's not just one guy trying to make it, but we're all running to the football. But, it's just you got to make sure you play clean in that first game, right? The team that plays the cleanest, right? The team that doesn't make stuff makes the most mistakes, you don't beat yourself, right? This when you have opportunity to win this game. >> What do you What do you consider the biggest difference you've seen [clears throat] from Calen Bullock from now to when y'all first brought him in? >> Calen has really grown from a communication standpoint. Like, I mean, his he does a great job of talking, getting everybody on the same page in the back end. So, we ask a lot of those guys and Calen has, you know, taken it by the horn, done a really good job of making sure everybody's dialed in together and it's just his confidence is at all-time high. We know the ball hawk that he is and I'm excited to see this kid go and have a great year. >> How does your defensive philosophy, how important is it to you not overcomplicate things and so you guys can play fast and not be thinking out there? >> It's football, baby. You don't over complicate it. You put the ball down. You make sure our guys are confident. All right, we again, we we tell our defensive guys, we got a lot of film that we've watched, but they can do anything. All right, but we just just trust each other. Go out there, play fast. It doesn't You know, for us, we don't have to do a ton. We just have to do what we do and do it well. And that's my philosophy. That's what I believe in and just making sure our guys are on the detail, eliminating the explosive plays. Buffalo was I think top two in explosive plays last year. So, for them adding D.J. Moore, getting that explosive threat down field, we know that's going to be a emphasis of theirs this year. We just got to make a play when the ball is up in the air. We got to find a way to make a play and we got to as we all know, get after, you know, the quarterback as best we can. He's a great player. We have great rushers. It's going to be a really good match-up. >> What have you seen from Jaylon Knowles since he's been able to get back on the field and how much growth in that? >> Yeah, from Jaylon, I've seen that confidence start to continue to build. Just him getting out there. He's had He's missed some time unfortunately with injury, but just seeing him be out there, stay out there, that's allowed him to just gain, you know, some better confidence with the offense. So, he's looking good. He's looking good as a returner for us as well. Expecting him to do big things for us as a returner. So, I'm just excited to see him out there, staying out there and that's what we have to try to keep him there all year. >> Jadeveon's back at practice. Do you expect him to be full go and then just for his return to Houston [snorts] for the first time since 2019, how excited are you for that? >> Yeah, Jadeveon is back at practice. All of our guys are out there working, which is a is a great thing to start the season having all the guys available and ready to go. And Jadeveon's done a good job. He's worked himself back. He'll be ready to go. >> From your perspective, obviously, you know, Josh is one of the best players at creating out of structure and making explosive plays. Like you >> [snorts] >> point to, you know, top two in that particular the but from your perspective, you guys have been able to kind of contain that the past couple of times you guys have played him. So, what's kind of that balance of, you know, in a sense, forcing him into creation mode, but also knowing that you've had success, but also knowing that that's also his strength, too. What's kind of that balance um that you kind of think about going into the game? >> And for us, the balance starts with we can't hang our hat on past success. All right, past success is not going to, you know, automatically guarantee you future success. So, we got to go out and we have to earn it. You know, and that's one thing that Josh and his offense is going to make you do. They're going to make you earn every play that you make. And that's how we like it. That's how it should be. And our guys are up for that challenge. We know we have to cover longer than we than you do versus other quarterbacks. All right, you have to rush a little bit longer just knowing it's not it's not going to happen as quick as other teams. It's just got to take time. Guys have to be patient. You have to make sure you're plastering in coverage, being responsible, being where you're supposed to be. When you do that, you have opportunities to make plays. So, Josh is a good player. He's going to make some plays, but we have to just find a way to make more than he makes. >> You guys have been very complimentary of CJ. He's been consistent. He's continued to grow. Just seeing him grow as a leader, seeing the way he's operating in the offense. Like, man, I'm I'm fired up to see him just go play. You know, there's a lot been said about CJ. Man, he's done a great job the past 3 years. We've made the playoffs every year because we've had a talented young quarterback who's led us to the playoffs. All right, and I'm I'm thankful to have him as our quarterback. He's done a great job for him. He's taken a huge step this year in growth. And now it's time to go show it. >> You have potentially have two young guys that could be starting for you on on offensive line. The lights won't be too big for them. They're going to go out and do what they've done all training camp, be consistent, play physical, and finish the right way. >> The other day, Riyan talked about that one of the main things that him and Keelan discussed is just going out and hitting somebody, that physicality part. >> I love it. That's one thing I hang my hat on. We're going to play with physicality. That's one thing I believe in, and that's what football is about. You got to play physical. It's a physical game, tough game for tough people. If you're not tough, then it's not the place for you. >> Because you guys added Keanu Neal in the second round, that helped you all improve the run defense. And let's get rolling. >> You were in the Manning Cast promo that you were in. When did you shoot that? [laughter] How many takes did it take for you to get that? >> I'm a one-take guy. >> No, that was that was a fun fun opportunity for me to shoot the Manning Cast.
