So, you know, they're very talented and now it's just, you know, finding the rhythm and, you know, it's not overnight, but, you know, I think those guys, you know, definitely had, you know, great challenges in camp, you know, going against our defense. Um, so I think, you know, it'll be, you know, every game is, you know, you playing against great players. So, I think, you know, those guys, you know, they're they're two dogs, so I'm excited to see them go. >> How eager are you to get back on the the field, especially to start the season at home when you haven't done that in a few years? >> Yeah, I'm excited. you know, it's our first one, your first game being at home. So, be it'll be fun. >> You remember your first opportunities of playing here at home and your first game what that was like. If you've given any advice to, you know, your guys like like Kaitlin about what the atmosphere is like and just kind of helping them through that process of these >> We're fine. I think I think football is football at the end of the day, you know, like you can't really focus on the crowd or like what's going on more. So, you know, just try to do your job every play and that's my advice. You know, just be yourself. You know, find your rhythm and then roll. So, I think those guys have to be good at that. >> Relationship with Nick Kaylee. How has that grown specifically? What are some things that you and Nick now understand about each other as you can work better together? >> Uh, we've been able to communicate better. Um, and then just showing what I like, what I don't like, you know, and he's does the same thing. Um, and I think, you know, we just getting better, you know, I'm understanding where he's coming from more and he's doing the same for me. you were just saying earlier about you guys as an offense being on the same page more consistently, less penalties, just playing cleaner football. Taking that into account, what do you see as the ceiling for you guys, you know, for this offense? How, you know, how high can you guys go? >> Uh, we'll see, man. You know, it's um I think we put a lot of good things on on tape during camp and in our joint practices and, you know, in preseason. Um, now it's time to go out there and do it. I I can't give you a firm answer on that, but I think it's one play at a time for us. Jaylen null missed a good amount of training camp, but what does he bring to the offense now that you guys have him back? >> Uh, he brings, you know, just explosiveness, you know, being able to be a, you know, I think he's polished his his intermediate to short short game routes. Um, you know, I think his his growth has been amazing just to see him, you know, grow smarter, be smarter with leverages and, you know, winning against tough leverages and, uh, coverages that aren't ideal in in the short to intermediate area. So, um, he's grown a lot. that our competitive training camp was for you all. How much of you being second year in this system help for you helped you all to win some of those battles against that defense? >> Yeah, it's huge. You know, um it's it's not easy first year in any system in any, you know, predicament. You're you're just, you know, every game finding new things, every practice finding new things and working things out. I think now we kind of got a a good grip on what we want to do, what our identity is going to be, and that'll change. you know, uh, it's not always going to be exactly what you want, but I think, um, you know, the foundation we built, um, with this second year in the system has been really good. >> Compartmentalizing football and the business of football, contracts, that kind of thing. How are you heading into the season if they don't do the deal, if they do it later? Uh, and how do you kind of approach that just with the focus, main focus being on Sunday? >> Yeah, you said it. I mean, it's focus on football. let let you know my team and my agent handle that. But you know, my my job is to play football and that's what I'll do. >> Was talking about placing you guys with like defensive guys, etc. during training camp at lunch and getting to know your teammates that you wouldn't normally sit with. Did you sit with anybody that kind of stood out, unique stories or anything that stuck with you by any chance? >> Uh, not anything specific, but I I think, you know, everybody's different. That's what I think is beautiful about this sport. You got a lot of different people, different backgrounds, different areas, all coming together for a common goal. So, I'm very grateful, you know, to be able to every team is different every year. So, I'm grateful to have you all the teammates I do have. And I I was able to make some great connections with some guys that obviously every single year a team will change. Just because you saw looks from the Buffalo Bills last year, that that doesn't necessarily mean it's going to be similar to this year. Is there anything that you've seen that you know, okay, this is something that we could attack on their defensive side or something you're excited to to attack in any way? >> Are you smiling? [laughter] >> I'm not going to do that. But they're they're good, man. They're they have really good players all around. Um I think they look like they're healthy. You know, they um you know, got some some guys on the back end they brought in. Um, so I think they're very talented and, you know, got a new head coach, but I think, you know, their defense is really solid, you know. Um, so can't really, you don't really know exactly what they're going to do, but you know, um, you got to just be prepared as best you can for whatever it's going to look like. But, you know, I think they're more than anything, they're very talented. >> From competitive standpoint, from a competitive standpoint, is there any extra excitement going against Josh and Burrow to start the season? >> Uh, no. I mean, my my my focus is on, you know, my team and then, you know, their defenses. Um, so, you know, I I definitely, you know, um, just focus on that and try my best, you know, stay focused on my job. >> Talk about chemistry a lot through this press conference. Can you talk about the the chemistry that you and Nico have developed throughout the time that you all played together? >> Yeah, it's been great. You know, I've been working with him, talking to him, trying to get him to grow. He's trying to get me to grow. So, just every day pushing each other to be better. >> Thank you, guys.

title: LIVE: HC DeMeco Ryans, C.J. Stroud and Will Anderson Jr. address the media
text: Full house. Let's go. when you play that facility with this being our first game, anything goes. Any looks, any type of schemes, anything can come up. So, for that reason, I don't put any, you know, I don't put a lot of weight into the games that we played prior. also with this team, new head coach, right? New defensive coordinator, new special teams coordinator. There there will be a ton of different looks than we've had than the past two years. So, just to say, oh, what we did the past two years is what's worked, rinse, and repeat. That's not it, right? We got to be prepared and ready for anything. We got to trust our rules, trust what we've done during training camp, trust our training, and put the ball down. Let's go to work. >> What does Ann Oliver bring to their defense? He [clears throat] hasn't played the previous two times you guys matched up. Ed's a man really disruptive player, right? He's done it for a while. Very disruptive. He will he can wreck a game by playing, you know, violent in the back field, making plays sideline to sidelines. Ed is a really good player. He's been a good player for a long time. So, a guy we have to put a hat on every single time. >> You had a lot of good things to say about Montgomery in training camp. How eager are you to see him play for your team in a real game? >> I'm very eager to see Montgomery, you know, get out there for the first time, you know, behind his offensive line. He's done a great job of of leading, you know, inspiring guys and just the way he works, the way he carries himself. Uh it's it's been a pleasure to work with him. So, I'm excited to see him finally get in some real action with our guys and I know he'll be fun to watch. >> How different has been for you and your staff preparing to start the season at home instead of going in a row like it has happened the last couple of days? >> Preparation is preparation. And so whether we're home or away, it's it's good to have a home game to start the season. First time for me being here starting the season at home. But hey, we got to go play good football and we're excited to be in front of our home fans for the first time. Opening up for our 2026 Texans to showcase what we're all about against a really good opponent. It's going to be a great matchup. I've guys get ready for a really good football game. They're really good team. They're coached well. They'll be prepared. Our team's good team. We're prepared. So, I mean, you you got to love it. The NFL is back. We got a great match up to start the year, man. Let's get it. >> How do you How do you rate the margin of error coming into the first game? >> With the first game, you just have to be dialed in on the fundamentals, right? Protecting the football. That's the main thing for me. We have to make sure we protect the football really well. Tackling is always an issue. Can be an issue the first game. You got to make sure you're putting guys on the ground finishing. Some of our guys haven't had live tackling reps, so we just got to make sure we're secure in our tackling, make sure it's not just one guy trying to make it, but we're all running to the football. But it's just you got to make sure you play clean in that first game, right? The team that plays the cleanest, right? The team that doesn't makes the makes the most mistakes, you don't beat yourself, right? That's when you have opportunity to win this game. What goes to your defensive loss that you've [clears throat] seen from Kaylin Bolock from now to when y'all first brought them in? >> Kaylin has really grown from a communication standpoint. Like I mean his he does a great job of talking, getting everybody on the same page in the back end because we ask a lot of those guys and Kaylin has, you know, taken that by the horn, done a really good job of making sure everybody's dialed in together and just his confidence is at an all-time high and I'm excited to see him go play. Right. is everybody knows his range has been great. He's improved every year, improved his tackling from year one to year two. We know the ball hawk that he is and I'm excited to see this kid go and have a great year. >> Talk to your defensive philosophy. How important is it to you not over complicate things and so you guys can play fast and not be thinking out there? >> It's football, baby. You don't over complicate it. You put the ball down. You make sure our guys are confident, right? We again we we tell our defensive guys we got a lot of film that we've watched but they can do anything right but we just just trust each other go out there play fast it doesn't you know for us we don't have to do a ton we just have to do what we do and do it well and that's my philosophy that's what I believe in and just making sure our guys are on the detail eliminating the explosive plays Buffalo was I think top two in explosive plays last year so for them adding DJ Moore getting that explosive threat downfield we know that's going to be an emphasis of theirs this year. We just got to make a play when the ball is up in the air. We got to find a way to make a play and we got to, as we all know, get after, you know, the quarterback as best we can. He's a great player. We have great rushers. It's going to be a really good matchup. >> What have you seen from Jaylen Nol since he's been able to get back on the field and how much growth in that >> from Jaylen? I've seen that confidence start to continue to build. Just him getting out there. He's had he's missed some time unfortunately with injury, but just seeing him be out there, stay out there, that's allowed him to just gain, you know, some better confidence with the offense. So, he's looking good. It's looking good as a returner for us as well. Expecting him to do big things for us as a returner. So, I'm just excited to see him out there, staying out there, and that's why we have to try to keep him there all year. >> Back in practice, do you expect him to be full go? just for his return to Houston for the first time since 2019. How excited are you for that? >> Javian is back at practice. All of our guys are out there working, which is is a great thing to start the season having all the guys available and ready to go. And Javian's done a good job. He's worked himself back. He'll be ready to go. >> Perspective, obviously, you know, Josh is one of the best players at creating out of structure and making explosive plays. >> [snorts] >> pointed to, you know, top two in that particular thing, but from your perspective, you guys have been able to kind of contain that the past couple times you guys have played him. So, what's kind of that balance of, you know, in a sense forcing him into creation mode, but also knowing that you've had success, but also knowing that that's also his strength, too. What's kind of that balance um that you kind of think about going into the game? >> And for us, the balance starts with we can't hang our hat on past success, right? past success is not going to, you know, automatically guarantee you future success. So, we got to go out and we have to earn it. And that's one thing that Josh and his offense is going to make you do. They're going to make you earn every play that you make. And that's how we like it. That's how it should be. And our guys are up for that challenge. We know we have to cover longer than we than you do versus other quarterbacks, right? You have to rush a little bit longer. Just knowing it's not it's not going to happen as quick as other teams. It just got to take time. Some guys have to be patient. You have to make sure you're plastering in coverage, being responsible, being where you're supposed to be. When you do that, you have opportunities to make plays. So Josh is a good player. He's going to make some plays. We have to just find a way to make more than he makes. >> You've been very complimentary of CJ. Is it something spectacular that you've seen from him in training camp and the buildup [snorts] or is it just steady dayby day? What I love about CJ's growth and his his progress, just he's been steady. He's been consistent. He's continued to grow. Just seeing him grow as a leader, seeing the way he's operating in the offense, like, man, I'm I'm fired up to see him just go play. You know, there's a lot being said about CJ, man, he's done a great job the past three years. We've made the playoffs every year because we've had a talented young quarterback who's led us to the playoffs, right? And I'm I'm thankful to have him as our quarterback. He's done a great job for him. He's taken a huge step this year in growth and now it's time to go show up. >> Yeah, potentially have two young guys that could be starting for you on that offensive line. What is that uh learning curve for both of those guys in Ruters? >> Don't over complicate it. [laughter] Block the man in front of you. Be be sound in your assignments. Communicate the right way and play physical and aggressive as those guys play. That's it. We got those are two good young football players that we're we're thankful to have on our team. They've done a good job all training camp and I know that's what they'll do. The lights won't be too big for him. They're going to go out and do what they've done all training camp. Be consistent, play physical, and finish the right way. >> The other day said that one of the main things that him and Keyn discuss is just going out hitting somebody. That's the physicality part. >> I love it. That's one thing I hang my hat on. We're going to play with physicality. That's one thing I believe in and that's what football is about. You got to play physical. It's a physical game. Tough game for tough people. If you're not tough, then this is not the place for you. >> Help you all improve the run defense. [clears throat] How do you feel like he's uh coming along? >> Kaden's come along. He's come along really good. He's improved each week. He's gotten better with what we've asked him to do. and you know, still a young ascending player, but he's done a good job of what we've asked him to do. And, you know, he's he has more to him than just being a run player, but we have a feel like we have a really good rotation with our defensive tackles. We have some depth there that uh probably the best depth that we've had since I've been here. So, just excited with that group with that different amount of guys we can mix in, have different combinations out there. I think it'll be a really uh strong part of our defense this year. Not trying to call you old, >> but you just did. [laughter] >> You've been around this game for a long time as a player and as a coach, and the season starts today. Is that kind of weird for you? >> No, man. I'm Let's go. Like, it's here. I can't wait to watch it and see what's what's happening, man. I'm Wow. I think this I don't know. Is this year 20 for me in the NFL? But man, it it never gets old. The excitement, the buildup of the season openers, it never gets old. I'm as fired up as all of our fans are fired up about the season opening up on a Wednesday and let's get rolling. >> Promo that you were in, when did you shoot that? [laughter] And how many how many takes did it take for you to get >> I'm a one take guy. [laughter] >> No, that was that was a fun uh fun opportunity for me to shoot the Manning cast. I'm thankful for those guys allowing me to be a part of that and you know the other coaches I was able to work with. Uh they do a really great job on the maniccast. Known Payton for a long time for the amount of touchdowns he scored on me. Um he should let me get a little get back by getting the manic. But that was that was a fun that was a fun uh fun deal for me to do. Man, >> when did you >> That was that was at the uh NFL annual meetings. Yeah. >> Knowing the last couple of weeks there have been speeches to the team that have a NASA theme to it. Is there something you have planned this week coming with week one with another something with with NASA involved as well? >> For me, it's, you know, it started with the the NASA buildup with NASA being in our backyard here in Houston. Just really wanted to tie the two together, right? Because Houston is about community. Houston is about us being together. So it was a thought it was a really good way to correlate us preparing right for training camp getting [clears throat] ready just like Artemis 2 they prepared they got ready it took them time right for that buildup and for that moment and now you know come Sunday it's time for the takeoff and that's the next part of the message right how are we taking off on Sunday >> his caller what do you anticipate from him this year second year running the system with the personal he got >> for Kaylee like for anyone right the second time doing it he's much more comfortable with what he's doing he knows what he wants he knows how he want it to look so just him just having that command him coaching up his coaches right everybody's on the same page he's doing a great job of communicating and leading the offensive group coaches and players so I'm fired he's fired up practice today he's fired up barking at guys so I'm excited to See this Kaye? He's fired up. I'm fired up. >> Some of the guys were talking about how you had them eating lunch with each other, like defense, offense, tight ends, linebackers, whatever. Did you get involved in that at all? Is there anything that you learned special, unique, different about somebody you didn't know? >> Yeah, the biggest thing for for me in training camp is how do you like force that interaction amongst the players, right? And that was the main thing is is getting different. It's easy for the linebackers to always eat together. With the linebackers, they meet together. So, you just kind of have to force that interaction. And I'm happy our guys, you know, they took it serious when we had our breakout sessions of different groups, eating lunch together, meeting together, just getting to dive in and learn each other a little bit better. I think that was beneficial towards our growth as a team for 2026. And and I feel like our guys gained a lot of insight from that. Um, we talked to Brevin this week and he said he was uh so grateful for the opportunity and to be here and he said that he doesn't really have any expectations on himself. He's just going out to play. That's the kind of latitude you guys have given him. What do you expect from him? >> I'd like to hear that from Brevin. He just go be free, be himself, and just play football, right? Don't put any pressure on himself to achieve anything. Grant, it's just a matter of Brevin like staying out there, being consistent. We know he's missed a lot of time, you know, these past two years, and it's been a rough go for him, but it's it's great to see him just on the practice field working, right? And he just keeps working, doing what he has to do. We know he can help our team. >> All right. Thank you guys. What's up? What's up? What's up? >> A lot of people outside the organization are saying defense is probably going to be the best in the league. What do you guys think about that and how can you be better than you guys were last year? >> Yeah, I think first is ignoring the noise. Um, keeping everything internally. Um, I think that's a goal of ours of course, but it's about how we show up every day if we want to do something like that. Are we going through our process? Are we having fun? and everybody executing and when you execute you win and you have fun. So for us that's most definitely is a goal for us. But I think for us it's just man keeping the main thing the main thing and that's winning games and being the best defense and to do that you have to go out and execute every uh game. >> There's certain games in the year where they hold implications come playoff time. This is one of those games depending on who could play at home in the playoffs. Is that something you address head on and like make it a big thing or just like whatever you ignore it? >> Yeah, I mean that's a good question. I think for us we already said like this is an AFC championship matchup. Two really good teams. We have a ton of respect for them. Josh Allen leading the way, really great offensive line. Um, uh, James Cook, man, the best running back in the league, one of the best running backs in the league. So, um, it's going to be a great match up for us, but the type of atmosphere that I'm feeling like is going to be on Sunday is going to be that AFC Championship type feel. Like I said, two really great teams battling out. There's been battling these last two years since I've been here. It's going to be a good match up for us. >> When it comes to the whole chasing and catching up with Josh Allen, what's involved in that? What does it take? >> Relentless effort, man. Relentless effort. Everybody's swarming. Like we need all 11 hats to the ball. Plaster in the back end, swarming up front. The rush has to be on point. And I think this what I love about this defense is everybody unselfish. And I say it all the time and coach was showing clips today of just how it looks when everybody's on the job. When the back end is passing, the defensive line is going to hunt. We all being relentless. So to beat a team like this to get to Josh Allen, it just takes relentless. Like you may not get him the first one, but man, pop back up and go get him again. So for us, it's just um four equals one. No independent contractors, everybody doing their job up front and just giving the time giving the guys in the back end OP when you were at Georgia, but what do you remember about James Cook and especially last year's game where he had that very big run and very had to kind of start things off. What do you remember about him? >> Yeah, much hasn't changed. He's still explosive running back, man. He had some big games um against us, a lot of uh great runs against us in Alabama. He was on our um our scout report all the time. He's a really tough running back and he's so patient. He'll wait. He'll wait. He'll wait and he'll just fold to the outside and take off. But that's what makes him so great, man. He's not like a just a oh, I'm going to go right now. He just tries to see and feel everything out. So for us, it's going to be holding gaps, everybody staying where they need to be, get extension, playing with great eyes, great feet, and be in a position to go make the play. >> A group that is as confident as you all not only confident in their abilities, but also confident in each other. >> Yeah. Um it it it it's it's it's very important. I think you look at it in all like phases of every position that we have. Um everybody shows up to work with the right mentality and I think we don't gain that confidence um just by our natural athletic ability. I think it's the preparation that we put in week in and week out and how we watch a film. Like today for instance, coach had JP come up and be the coach. And man, he killed it. And we received that cuz it's like, bro, if JP can get up here and tell him, tell us what his job is, what everybody else doing. That feeds the room. Cuz that's like, if he can do it, why everybody else isn't doing that. Like I should be able to tell you what the DTackle next to me is doing. He should be able to tell you what I'm doing. And so that's how you get a great defense. When you know what everybody else is doing on the field and you can receive that, you go out there and play fast and have fun doing it. >> Might as well. Uh, does that help you as far as when you're playing at defensive line knowing that you have such great, you know, defensive backs behind you? >> Oh yeah, all the time. All the time. It's like we go into the game and it's a certain call or whatever, it be like you like we got Steam Kamari back there. We got JP back there. We got Reed back there. We got Kaylin going sideline to sideline back there. So for us, we was like, man, we just got to get home. Even if we just get a pressure or something to effective like bro like they throw that ball up in the air, one of our guys coming down with it because they all have elite ball skills and I think that's what makes them so special. We're talking about how you guys were in training camp. Demo to Miko had you sit with some offensive guys, vice versa, mix it all up. Yeah. Is there a teammate that you sat with that some stuck with you and something either funny or unique or anything like that? >> Yeah. Um I would say really listen to Dalton Schulz. SH has been a guy that, you know, me and him actually have gotten a little closer and I've learned a lot about him, but to hear how he goes through his process and, you know, not to put everything out there, but just his mentality of how he approaches practice, how he approaches his his real life. Um, just taking it one day at a time, but, you know, having that balance of being able to be with his family and then be up here. I think that's something as a young player that you kind of, you know, you look at like, how do I juggle all those things? But, you know, he's been great with helping with things like that. So he's one player that I really looked up to, you know, during that time, really listen to him, how he balances his football life and his family life. >> How much does the success you guys had against Josh the past couple times? You know, obviously still call now the head coach. How much does that factor into how you guys approach this week um going into the season opener? >> Yeah, we always say last year is last year and it's like what we going to do this year? You know, they're going to come out in something that we've never seen before. They're going to have a play drawn up that we never seen before. But how are we attacking our game plan? How are we going out there and executing? And for us, we've seen the success. Like I said, this is a really great team. So there's no mistake about that. So for us, we have to go out there and be on 10. You know what I'm saying? We have to go play our our brand of football. And so last year, like I said, is last year is like what we going to do this year? Are we going to swarm this year? Are we going to get to the ball this year? Are we going to take the ball? And I think that's one of the biggest things like how many times can we take the ball? How many times can we attack the ball? And so I think that's the growth from last year to this year, man. Let's take the ball from these guys. be a first half for CJ's crowd. >> I'm sorry. >> Any advice you had for CJ as he works through the same negotiating process that you went through? >> Yeah. I mean, at the end of the day, um it's all in God's hand and CJ knows that. Um we've talked, but you know, I think both of us right now, we're headon going into the Bills game. You know, I think that's the biggest focus right now is man, we want to win these ball games and whatever happens after that happens after that. But man, CJ is locked in. He's been coming to work every single day. He's been bringing the guys along with him. The offense is looking really great and I can't wait to go I can't wait to go watch him spin on Sunday. >> Will this be your first time playing in front of you know the home crowd to open up the season? I mean um >> on yesterday I got an opportunity to watch your mom you know in her interview with Hannah and she was talking about how excited you were when you first when you took your visit here. This is before you know you were going to be a Houston. What was it about this Houston Texas organization? What was it about this city? What was it about De Mo that made you so adamant and wanted to play here? >> Yeah, I would say man is the energy that I felt in the building from everybody and then I had previously like I didn't know much about De Mo until like the draft process came and then like obviously watching the Super Bowl and everything like that and like all those good things, but I seen the energy that he had and I seen and then I found out he went to Alabama and I kept following him even more and then I seen that he was a defensive coach and he was a D coordinator at the at the uh 49ers and so when I got here I could just feel the energy when I first met him. I mean, he was excited. I could tell like he's we shared the same mentality like, man, whatever it takes mentality and then it bled through the whole organization. I met with Coach Rod. Coach Rod was the assistant Dline coach and he had energy from the get-go. And that's just when he was the assistant Dline coach. And so for me, like that's what I wanted to surround myself with when I came into the league. I wanted to be somewhere where I actually felt like I was wanted. You know what I'm saying? And that was always my biggest prayer. Like, God, I want to be somewhere where they actually want me. And I left that feeling like, yeah, I feel like this place is the one. I told my agent, I was like, "I don't care what you got to do. Tell them come get me." And man, they made it happen and I couldn't be more happy and more blessed to be here. >> the home crowd. >> Oh, I'm super excited about that. First one, I hope the crowd is rocking, man. Come out and support. It's going to be a big one. So, let's go. >> Like the defense and you specifically has gotten more national attention, the photo shoot and all that. What's that been like uh for you? Is it kind of a natural thing? Rat poison. Rat poison. That's all it's been. No, but it's been fun. It's been It's been really fun because outside of the football, I feel like we've grown together more as a team, especially like with the defensive guys just as far as like hanging out more, getting to do fun stuff like that because sometimes, you know, in the league, guys just go their separate ways and then just go home. You you see it in the locker room. Not everybody can kind of feel the energy at practice every single day. And um it's a lot of fun. That's my job and my goal is to make sure that doesn't dwindle, you know, week 15 or week nine whenever, you know, things are are long or, you know, have a tough week ahead. So, um I think more than anything, let's keep that same level of energy and let's keep that same growth mindset the whole year and and it's going to start, you know, this >> You and um Kell collaborate on the the game plan this week. Do you feel like versus how it was when you were you you had those starts in the second half of the year, do you feel like maybe Kell's giving you a little bit more rogue, letting you, you know, kind of be more vocal in what you want to do? Do do you feel like there's a I guess more of a comfortability between you two at this point than it was last year? >> Yeah, we we've definitely um we've definitely been communicating at a high level, I would say, just this whole off season, putting together ideas for different footworks, different film, um different, you know, kind of play installs and stuff like that. And then now when you get into a game week of preparation, it's um it's kind of right back to where we were started. And and it's been a lot of fun to just continue to learn from him. And I think that's part of the process. And um it's also my job to run what they call and and and do my job in that aspect. But they have been able to give me some more freedom and um and voice some things that I'm I like or or maybe some of the other guys like as well as far as receivers, tight ends, running backs, what they um are comfortable with on certain routes. So Kell's probably the best in the business when it comes to that when you know putting the guys in the right position to go out there and make a play. >> Tyler, when it comes to like ball placement um throwing to certain spots against certain looks or wherever defenders lined up, is that like um is that a field thing in the moment or is that a learn thing you kind of have to go through build up over time practice? Like how would you describe? Yeah, it's it's definitely it's definitely a skill you have to practice um the intentionality of ball placement versus certain leverages, certain coverage, and um obviously there's uh there's easier said than done in some ways and and some guys have a really good feel for it. Um and I feel like for me it feel like I've had decent ball placement, but I've also felt like I've had really bad balls play placement in certain certain coverages. So that's an everyday thing. It's like how can you be perfect on that? And um I always kind of put down little pluses or minuses there. um because sometimes it may be a completion but may not be in the right um spot or sometimes it might be incompletion but it was in a good spot. So you kind of have to just uh keep the same mindset and and go from there but it's it's obviously a crucial part of my job and at least the success of the offense >> like pluses and minuses when you're going back and watching film. >> Yeah, I do like BP plus BP minus um just whether it was even if it's completion or not. Sometimes I'm as you there's like a famous Tom Brady clip like it's rarely ever the the throw that you want and and at least for quarterback you're trying to make sure it's exactly how you want it and that's why we stay after practice and and try and get the that same feel that you are going to feel on game day. >> See do you then also go over that with like receivers and stuff like where they where they like stuff or do you kind of is it kind of like a mutual conversation? >> Yeah, it's just super collaborative. Super collaborative depends on the depends on the down and distance the yard line where we're at in the field. um what type of route it is. It's, you know, that's the whole name of the game. You know, if we're trying to protect them over the middle or we're trying to maybe lead them lead them outside, you know, up and away on the goal line. Um that's kind of the fun part of the game is trying to be super detailed in that aspect. >> What do you think of Detroit? Like what sticks out to you the most about uh about their defense based on watching the film? >> Um 97 sticks out for sure. He's obviously an elite level player and um have to have a good plan for him and and their linebackers um are are really really good. You know, you got Devin White coming onto the team and and and the guy in the middle, Jack Campbell, he's awesome. Um he's a really really physical player and and same thing with Derek Barnes. So, um got to be ready for th those guys and we want to match their physicality, match the intensity, and um and go out there and attack. the the last portions of practice. We got to see the the two weeks of during practice, the the the last week of practice with two lane uh visit, stuff like that. It seemed like you and the offense really found a rhythm. Uh I I know it changes a lot when it's the real thing in week one, but did did everything kind of coales at the end of camp the way you you hoped and expected it would? Yeah, it's it's it's always a funny um narrative and it's a funny because it's I feel like at the end of camp is when we start playing football, you know, it's the beginning of camp is a lot installs and um you may have a screen day today, we may have a an outbreaker day or they they're having a cover zero day and it's just like it's not always the the perfect look and that's always fun because you get to train um what might happen in a game and then once we get rolling in scrimmages and towards the end you start playing call up periods and um I always love that cuz now you know it's not necessarily scripted and you can operate that way. So, uh it starts getting you towards game-like mentality and that's what we've been doing this whole practice, this whole week. >> Were you able to notice improvement in in those weeks to call it weeks and stuff? Like everything you hoped you would from having an entire off season? >> Yeah, I feel like I feel like every every day, every week, I feel like I got a little bit better at at something I was trying to work on. and um and I'm going to sit up here every single week and I'm going to have to work on something and say the same thing. So, it's that's the best part about it. But, uh I feel like over time, over camp, we felt really really good and um we want to continue that and and that's that's our whole goal going into week one in a hostile environment. Um how how can we not have any negative plays, can't have any penalties. Um that's going to be I think a tell of the game and if we're clean there, um it should be a clean operation. >> You play some of your best in those call periods or scrimmage type situations. Same thing with the competition, I guess. >> Yeah, for sure. I I feel like I go out there and compete. I feel like game day um you know, intense practices, what joint, whatever the case may be. I feel like there's a different um sense of energy for me. But I think that's the same thing every single day whenever we're doing indie or um I'm I'm trying to increase that level every single day. But I think more than anything, it's just it's actual football. It's from a like a a huddle perspective from going out there moving the ball. um you get a feel for for certain things, but um that's that's part of the game and and I think as an offense, we've hit a really good stride and we got to continue to keep going. >> The flip side of that is not playing in any preseason games. What were you able to take from watching and communicating and all the mental aspects of those? >> Yeah. Um, I feel like we've learn we've taken a lot from it just from the aspect of negative plays, having, you know, having ball security when it comes in the pocket, obviously out in space for some of our skill position guys. Um, and then just having those chunk plays and taking advantage of them. Um, and more than anything, it's just just the operation. We got to do that pre, you know, game day. From a rep perspective, preseason's always um interesting, you know, going out for potentially a drive or two or whatnot, but I think we did a really good job when it came to joint practice, getting 70 80 plays and um going out there and operating versus a new look, new new defense every single time. So, we feel really prepared to go now and and now it's now it's just going to let it rip. You have a couple rookie wide receivers that are kind of kind of be thrown into the fire in wing one. You know, do you put that on yourself to spend a little extra time and make sure they're ready? Just kind of to trust that they're going to go out there and get the job done. >> Yeah, it's a little bit of both. I'm going to do everything I can to to help those guys prepared you know um as the whole offense you know we're going to do everything we can from that aspect from signaling perspective from the huddle mechanics from you know knowing their job and and how can we beat detailed from that aspect but also they've done an incredible job themselves preparing and and being ready to go and having juice I feel you felt it every single time you know both Bryce and Barry have stepped up to the call so I kind I'm going to let them be them and um but at the same time if we're always having dialogue um because you know we haven't gotten a bunch reps, but you know, as of late, I feel like we've done a really good job of of connecting and um I'm really, you know, proud of the way they've worked and it's going to be a great season for them. >> From your last start to now, I mean, you know, having a whole off season as the guy, being able to grow as your teammates and just mature in the NFL, how much do you think you've grown personally as a player from your last start to now and this week one and um and how much more comfortable are you? Yeah, I feel like I feel like it's night and day for me from a comfortability perspective, from a leadership perspective, just the operation. And uh I used to care a lot about um the end result of maybe a play or the end result of a game. And um that still matters, but like I said before throughout this this process is um this offseason process is caring more about how did how did we get there? What was the energy like? What was you know, what was our intention behind it? And cuz it's going to be ups and downs in the season. So, we got to maintain that same mindset and um that's why I love it. So, I'm really excited to be back because I feel like this has been a long time coming and you watch the film from last year, it's like, man, we got so much more to go. We got so much more to grow from and that's the the fun part. >> Environment. How much do you like guys embrace? It's going to be back toback weeks on the road. Is this a way to gauge how good you are just to go into two very hostile environments against two very good teams? Yeah, it's going to be a great challenge and obviously starting off with Detroit, we're going to um we're going to have to be ready to go and I think we I think we are. I think we're going to have a great week of practice. We have thus far and and we got to match match that intensity and it's going to be fun. You know, I think it's first time for a lot of the guys, but um it's the previous stop for some of our coaching staffs and they've said they've had, you know, shown their own respect for it and um we're going to be ready to go. I'm going to make sure of that and uh I think that's the whole season. It's going to be a great challenge. For those who haven't been there, what is the captain's dinner like? What's the environment like? And how do the coaches actually tell y'all who's going to be a captain this year? >> Yeah. Um it was at Tana and it's really just a great environment. We're all kind of sitting sitting amongst each other. It's kind of position based, but we'll all kind of mingle and then we just break bread, have a dinner, and then kind of towards the end before desserts come out, we'll um kennel to come up and announce the captains and then one by one, we'll give kind of just a little couple words or a speech um and really just about how much it means to us and and kind of our words for the season. And um it's a really cool moment just to kind of hear from everybody and then obviously yourself getting to to share um just how how much everybody means to me as a you know as teammates and uh it's it's obviously one of the cool things I feel like we do and and I think more than anything it's it kind of shapes our vision for the season. >> Can you vote for yourself? >> I don't I don't know. They just write down two other I'm sure some guys did but I I wrote down um I'm not going to tell you who I wrote down but we uh we write down some other names. Kellen actually didn't have us vote for like defense or special teams if you're on offense and um I thought that was that was cool cuz a lot of times you're working with your guys every single day. But um was really proud of everybody who was named captain. I think all deserving and it shows just from their work in the offseason and and that you know how everybody stepped up as a leader. >> David to be a captain you know this this quickly obviously your locker's right next to his. Is that just telling of the impact he's had? >> 100%. He's uh he's one of the most steady guys I've been around. He he knows what it looks like when it comes to um high level play success. Just the energy and the culture of a locker room. And that's kind of the biggest thing I've learned from him is let's let's not freak out about you know what's happening in this moment. How is this going to look and how can we keep building in that way cuz he's he's been a part of you know some Rams teams where they maybe started off you know three and seven or something five and seven and then you kind of climb back and make the playoffs. He's been a part of some really good Bills teams and and it's going to look a lot, you know, it's going to get done in a lot of different ways and he understands that and he's been a really good voice for all of us and and the energy he brings at practice too. Um it's been good. So I think that's the exciting part for having him um up front and Eric doing a really good job and Eric's done a great job of just coming up there being himself and operating um and his physicality has shown up too. And Tyler, when you do a pregame speech, is that something you put a lot of preparation through during the week or you just wake up saying what? >> No, I try and I try and put a lot of intention behind it and think about it. Um, definitely I'm not Deario or Drew just probably I don't know. He probably just wakes up and has like a vision from God I think tomorrow and just like it's just the greatest thing ever. So it's very intimidating trying to follow that. But I try and think about it because it matters to me. I'm I want to make sure that we're ready to go. Um and that the message is clear about, you know, however we're feeling, the week of practice we had, who we're playing, um what we need at that moment. So, it all matters, and I want to be myself in that aspect. So, I'm going to continue to continue to try and get better in that way, too, and and we'll see we'll see how we do. with the receiver group going back to them. Um, is it fair to say beyond Chris that it's really hard to know who's going to contribute how much and that that's just going to be an evolving thing and you're going to have to get a feel for it as the year goes on. >> I think everybody's going to have a a hand and I think everybody's going to be involved. I think that's the best part about having those dynamic players like you got 43 speed and Bryce and Barry on and and Jawan is you can't cover him one-on-one and um at any position Noah he's he's a 44 I mean he's unbelievable his physicality he's extremely hard to cover. You got Oscar as well um and then you got Trav and AK. So, I think being able to distribute to all those guys, put them in different positions, um, is going to be really fun to see. And, uh, I think all those guys are going to have a big role. >> How did that pregame hub? How did how did that develop? Did teammates nominate you or did you just move on board and said, "Okay, I'll do it." Or >> No, I think it's it's just there wasn't like a a poll. There wasn't anything. It was it was just kind of um I feel like earned over time. I wasn't necessarily going to do that in January, but I, you know, it didn't happen just overnight. You know, I feel like every single day I understood that there was going to be that aspect of it, but I wanted to do everything I could this entire off season um to earn that and to have that message. And um we also have a somebody before the before we go out in the locker room talk as well. So, um, there's there's a couple different opportunities and Kellen does a good job of of understanding that, you know, he's not going to scream and cuss and and try and be somebody who he's not, but he's also going to let us as players be leaders and and send a Dish.

title: Saints HC Kellen Moore on naming team captains, preparing for Detroit, Shough and injury updates
text: Medicalwise, Oscar Delp did not practice with the hamstring. Audrey Esme did not uh practice with the thigh. Cam Jordan did not practice with the hamstring. Cam will not play this week. And then uh Alvin uh had the knee. He was limited. He was out there for summer practice. And then the only roster move we made was just on our practice squad. We released Jonah um and signed Kyrie Rowan. So Jonah's just got a medical thing. Um he'll be fine. He's just not quite ready, but u obviously we have a plan for him to uh be a part of this. So, uh, open up to questions. >> How did Alvin look there? [clears throat] >> Good. >> Yeah, good. Good to get him back out there. I thought, uh, hey, did some good things and we'll just kind of see. Again, we just got to see how, uh, anytime you're going through injury stuff, you got to see how things respond and then we'll see. >> Did you ever think that Cam might be able to give it a go this week? I mean, how's he progressing? >> Cam's going to do everything possible to uh, play in this game. So, u, again, uh, he's progressing well. He's done a really good job through this recovery process and uh we'll just take it week by week. >> Thought you didn't place him in IR. Is there a hope [snorts] that he returns within I guess the first four? >> Um I think there's potential. Yeah, we'll just again we'll just see how this thing responds. >> Injury was that coming out of the game or was something? >> Yeah. with um your captains with Chase Young specifically, how much of the work that he did in the voluntary phase? Like he was at every session, right? >> I think so. Just about. Yeah. >> And so like how much of that work that he put in then kind of you think led to his teammates voting their captain on Monday? Yeah, I'll start with the captain thing and just in general, um, we have a lot of captains and again, we have nine there, but we can go I we got a whole lot of guys who had votes and so the guys vote on it. We just find a spot where we can draw a line. Uh, we drew it right there and uh plenty of other guys that are worthy that are, hey, they're leading this team. There's not just nine guys that everyone else just stars and watches those guys. Everyone's a part of this thing. Um, I thought for Chase, he has done a great job through the whole offseason of really being a natural leader. um by how he acts, how he prepares, how he u plays. Um yeah, I thought he's just done an excellent job and certainly you can see the um appreciation his teammates have shown towards him. >> Kevin, same thing for Chris. What kind of stance about him as as a leader? >> I think Chris is a big time leader for our football team, particularly on special teams. Um he's one of the anchor pieces of that as far as leading that group, all the things he does with those guys as far as the preparation, getting prepared each week, the energy, the uh the juice he brings, um you know, on the field and special teams. Uh again, he's a guy who's u you know, certainly well recognized by his guys. >> Kelly, could you go a little more into detail about like how the voting works? Like do they write it down and give you all the the tallies I guess? >> Yeah, offense votes for offense, defense votes for defense. Anybody a part of special teams votes for them. They vote for two players uh in each category and u you know we tally them up and we try and find a line that we can u that we can draw. Again there's uh there's nine here. There's probably 18 20 guys that have votes. Um again um there's a lot of guys that are worthy of this. >> Is that a good sign that so many players think so many of their teammates are worthy of a vote? Yeah, I think it's it shows the the depth of our team from a leadership perspective that um you know on offense you got a bunch of skilled players who aren't necessarily captains that were had a bunch of votes uh you know defensive guys throughout the defensive unit special teams we had plenty of other guys uh that were a part of that not just Zach and Chris and so um again there's a lot of guys that are going to lead this football team. >> What happens at the captain's dinner? Is it is it just the captains or are there more people there? Do the coaches go? >> Full full team coaches players. I thought was a cool tradition that's been here for uh a number of years that uh we've certainly continued with. I think it's kind of that start official start of the regular season uh Monday night just having a dinner together and then we announced the captains. They have an opportunity to kind of share a message with uh with their teammates and the rest of the team and so um I thought it's been a really good experience. >> How has your process changed just like looking back to week one last year going through a season getting to learn some stuff like has anything about your process for going into a game would change? probably just the rhythm of it, just the the timing. Again, week ones, there's an element of unknown. We can we can chase every possible rabbit we want to. Uh just because they've had a whole offseason, we've had a whole offseason. I think you got to put together a good plan. You've invested a lot through the whole offseason on certain, um, you know, concepts, plays, uh, philosophical approaches. And so, uh, we just got to go play football. We just got to play clean football and put oursel in good position, be successful, and they'll do something that we haven't seen. We get that. That's a part of this. And so, uh, that's what week one's about. How do you decide like which rabbit to go after and which one to like? >> Yeah, I think you just got to narrow your focus again. Um, you got a whole season last year you can look at. You can go beyond that previous years. You got preseason football which certainly you still have to keep an eye on some of the things there and u you got to focus also on your football team as far as what you've been doing. Uh, the last thing we want to do is show up and disregard all of the training camp, you know, time on task football that we've put into this uh and try and recreate football. Uh, it's about our guys playing fast and decisive and confident and doing what they they certainly know that they can do. >> Is it hard not to go crazy when you're just looking at the same name for five months? Like there's just so many opportunities like >> I think it's really hard week one uh not to overanalyze it, you know. Um again, this is a really sound football team that's won a lot of games. They have really good schemes. They're going to do a really really good job against us. It's going to be hard a hard game. Um, but you got to allow your guys to play fast and free and confident. And so, um, a lot of that comes to time on task type stuff. Things that, hey, we know how to problem solve, uh, these type of looks. We we've invested a lot of time in it. And then we'll have a few little nuggets here and there that certainly we want to have available to us and we'll see how it goes. >> You guys get the schedule in early May. Just like out of curiosity, anxiousness, when's the first time you looked at any tape of the Lions defense just [snorts] to start formulating ideas in your head? >> I think I've seen it all offseason. And I think our whole offseason goal is really to study the league on u in all phases, you know, and really have an understanding of where it is cuz naturally there's trends with everything. As we're watching what we can do to improve on offense, we're also recognizing, hey, the top defenses in this league, they're going everyone's going to go watch those guys and see what can we add and implement. And so you got to be prepared to solve those challenges as well. And uh you know, these guys have done a really good job. They they a very diverse defense when you talk about from our offense perspective. um you know they they've played a ton of base last year. Certainly they they did a really good job of that versus all personnel groups and they have a lot of other other tools uh at their disposal and so uh you know we got to be prepared to adjust and just play clean ball. >> How's that organized? Is it like it's Tuesday in June it's Lions time or is it like let's look at the base defense of everyone in the league and they're a part of that happen. >> We really focus on oursel all through OTAAS and even most of training camp. um you know, coaches in the background. We're studying those early opponents. We're aware of uh what could be coming down the road the first few weeks. At times, [snorts] you may implement some of it in into training camp just as kind of a we don't announce it's a you know, Detroit play or a Detroit emphasis or uh whoever else we may be playing here in the next few weeks. Um you know, you're just trying to give yourself as much exposure so that week one again, uh we've put time into all this stuff and we're not um recreating football week one. How excited are you for uh for Tyler's opportunity, you know, Sunday having a full off season in training camp and being the guy for him to kind of, you know, enter this thing uh you know, with so much optimism in an offseason for him. >> Yeah, Tyler's had a great offseason. This would be a great opportunity for us just to uh test oursel against a really good football team, one of the best ones in this league in my opinion. Uh they had to navigate a few things last year and they just missed the playoffs. Uh but again, they've had a ton of success the last few years. They're really well coached. Uh they got some some really talented players. They got really clean schemes and u it'll be a lot of fun. It's going to be a great atmosphere. Uh Ford Field's going to uh you know be loud and exciting and uh that'll be fun. >> How would you uh evaluate what you've seen from him even as of late through these preseason games, whatever? We've seen the pregame speeches and whatnot, but um from a leadership perspective, how have you seen him kind of, you know, evolve into that? Yeah, Tyler earned earned being a captain on this football team for a reason because of u you know his presence throughout the whole offseason and the preparation that he's put into this and he he does a really good job of being that vocal leader when necessary like so many of these guys and so uh you know he's done a nice job >> for you kind of in that um we were talking about over analyzing because you have these five months before that start particularly with like calling place or Tyler do do you get to a point where you're like all right here's like what I think could probably recreate the success that he had last here and then it's like all right but what do I call what does that I guess that that do you over analyze that part of it too of like trying to like recreate what you want to have that success with Tyler >> um I mean week ones there's always an element of unknown so I think a lot of times you got to be aware of the opponent and study those guys but they had a whole offseason too so you got to play clean football um you know execute at a really high level and so a lot of that's focusing on the things that we've uh invested a lot in through training camp and some of those things fall back to last year and so uh I think we have enough in the plan. We got plenty of plays in the plan to to navigate whatever may come uh its way and so uh yeah I think our guys have done a nice job with that. >> Is there anything you look for early in games that shows that you guys are locked into the game plan or like it's going the way you thought it would go like that? Again, I think it's just about clean operation, execution, putting yourself uh in favorable situations early in games. And uh yeah, I think that's certainly going to tell you that we're uh we're moving where we need to

title: Saints S Justin Reid and EDGE Chase Young on preparing to face Jahmyr Gibbs and Lions' offense
text: Jaguars, the Cowboys, um, and the Rams. And it gave us a lot of confidence going into the season where we are right now based on how those joint practices went. So, uh, it was a good thing for us. Um, wish we didn't have as many injuries. It kind of hurt. Um, you know, Brian Brazie says his season ending. Um, we lost some other some running backs. I know AK's hurt right now. Uh, Jordan Tyson, of course. So, some of those injuries kind of is cost of doing business. um wish we didn't lose as many guys, but it's opportunity for guys to come and step up and um but all in all um really excited about where we are as a team. I feel like we have a lot of talent. We like guys know what to do like this point where we are right now from this point last year is miles away from each other and just an understanding of the playbook, understanding of responsibilities, confidence in what we're doing. And uh I think that when you're confident, you make more plays. So I think that we're going to have an opportunity to make a lot of plays this year. Justin, how much you guys embrace this first game? Not an easy place to play. You're going against pretty good offense. How much you guys embrace it and see how good you guys are? >> Hey, listen. If you want to win championships, you have to play everybody. Doesn't matter who you play. You know what I mean? So, yeah, bring it on. I mean, competitors love competition and we want to play teams that are the best. The Detroit offense has been one of the top five offenses the last, I don't know, six, seven, eight, nine years, however long we've been. Um, so it's a great challenge for us and we're excited about it. We're excited to show them what we've got. Um, our offense is uh clicking on all seven of this, especially since the second half of last season. So, my mentality is, you know, these first three weeks is a lot of fun. We got Detroit, then we got Baltimore, then I think the next one is Falcons or it's Las Vegas. >> Yeah, Raiders and Falcons. Like, it doesn't matter who you play. Like, I don't care who it is, you know? You got to beat everybody. You want to win a Super Bowl, you have to beat everybody anyway. >> What makes it difficult going against Derrick Golf and the weapons that he has on that offense? Yeah, they have some dynamic playmakers. I mean, they have a lot of skill set playmakers in Laora and Amaras St. Brown and Williams who take the top off in uh Gibbs who just dynamic all over the field. I think he has like a third of the targets in every game like one out of every three plays the balls in some type of way. So, we need to have some awareness there. Isaiah Pekco would have been an addition to him. Probably will later in the season, but he's hurt right now, so we won't see him this week. Um, and then Jared Golf, of course, is one of the best passers in the league whenever his uh pocket is clean, right? So, what does that mean? Can't give him a clean pocket. We got to find ways to find disruption there. Doesn't always mean blist all the time, but just finding ways to just make them uncomfortable. Um, and then making sure we shut down the playmakers, not allowing number one to have deep balls into the uh middle of the field, taking away those post balls. Um, making sure that we have a cap on coming on the corner, you know, and every play knowing where number zero is, right? So, it's a challenge for us. Um, but I think that we stack up well with them. Um, our skill positions and their skill positions and it'll be a good test for us. So, >> I I I know like one of the strategies anytime on defense is you want to make a team win eventually. So, does that like stopping Jir like priority number one for you guys? >> Yeah. I mean, good offenses can win in different ways, right? The same way that good defenses can win in different ways.
