title: QB Malik Willis meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: Yeah, probably somewhere around there. Yeah, it's really cool. I'm super grateful and obviously I'm going to just try to take advantage of the opportunity. >> Seem like a guy that doesn't make more of of something that needs to to be but does first game with the new team where you are the guy. Does that bring any kind of heightened emotion? >> No, it's real cool though. I'm grateful. Obviously it's a blessing and I just want to do everything I can and prepare for that and just take it as it comes. I mean it's a few days out. We still got practice to do. We got a lot of stuff to work on until we can get there. >> Coach Apple he said earlier today that um he'll take [snorts] a moment during the national anthem to kind of take everything in. With this being his head coaching debut, is there a moment between now and kickoff where you'll kind of sit back and reflect on what brought you here? >> I mean, more than anything, I try to been uh I kind of been doing that the whole time since I've been here. I think it's been awesome coming in every day. Uh just trying to work hard as I can, getting to know my teammates, and trying to be the best I can be. And I feel like that's all a part of it. I don't think it's a one moment thing for me. >> What would you tell the kid who had to switch to wide receiver at Westlake um now that you're preparing for your first NFL start as the guy? >> Uh I wouldn't tell him nothing. I'd just keep doing what you're doing. Apparently, uh you know, God's got a plan for you. Just keep working. Just keep working. Keep working. And focus on what you can control. That's the main thing. >> Malik, uh Caleb and Chris both listed as as starters. Jeff says that they deserve to start. What have you seen from them in your experience building chemistry that uh I just tells you they need to be on that field? >> Uh I think they've been doing a great job. Just obviously making plays and uh physical abilities they have. And obviously, they haven't got to show you all that to you guys. And uh maybe not on the game field. But I think they've been doing a great job working hard, trying to do everything they can to learn the offense and make sure they're as detailed as they are talented. >> You might have um rookie receivers, rookie tight ends, a rookie guard, and a rookie fullback. Maybe all of them on the field or many of them on the field at the same time. How do you plan to help them during the game? >> Uh just taking it one play at a time, making sure we're prepared before we even get there. And that's the main thing. Each week, you got to prepare. So, when the game comes, it's a lot easier as far as mental gymnastics and hoops that you have to go through to execute a play. I mean, we'll get I don't know how many reps. We got 80 reps today. We'll continue to just build and get those reps, mental reps, and uh just continue to learn and get better. Obviously, there's going to be mistakes, but if we can learn from those mistakes, in the long run, we'll be better off. >> Well, like when you have a pitch count for Chris, now, how much do you like to hear that? >> I think that's awesome. I think he's been working hard the whole off-season to get back to where he's at the point to be in the game, obviously in practice, and uh I think he's attacking it the right way as far as trying to be as detailed as he can be, and uh just work hard as he can. >> Speaking of receivers, you got to spend some time with the certain receiver at Charleston State. >> Yeah, my brother. >> Yeah, what was that like to be able to experience that with him? >> That was awesome. I'm super grateful that I got a chance to just go and see him play. He went through a lot to get to where he is now, and obviously, uh all the work he's put in just to see it come to fruition in the first couple weeks. Obviously, there's a lot of season left, but just to keep going out there and playing, I think it's awesome. I'm glad to get back out there whenever the opportunity arises. >> Pretty big win. >> [clears throat] >> Yeah, facts. They got Army last year. >> That's right. That's right. >> Yeah, facts. They always do. >> What What are your >> Playing against a pass rusher like Max Crosby, how much does that accelerate your your clock as a quarterback? >> Uh Um I think that's more of a feel thing. Every play is a separate play. It's not like uh he's on the field, now I have to be blah blah blah. It's more or less uh just being aware of him. Obviously, he's a great player, and he's been for a long time in this league, but uh we just try to do the best to do my job, and that's what's important more than worrying about that type of thing. Obviously, like I said, you got to be aware of him, and you got to know where he's at, but you got to play ball, too. >> How excited are you to kind of like kick things things off, you know, you're you have that calm, cool, collected demeanor, but, you know, the excitement of finally getting the season started? >> Yeah, it's exciting. I'm excited. >> [laughter] >> I am. I think it's cool. >> leader of this offense? Um obviously, what are the some of the conversations you've had with the rookies, with some of the younger players? It's a young team in general, but how do you keep them motivated? >> Um if they're not motivated, then we got the wrong guys. They're self-motivators and obviously I do what I can to get them going, but at the same time, like this is an opportunity that not many people get. Uh, not many people get a chance to play in this league and to come in as a rookie and have an opportunity to play, I think they're excited enough and uh, they're obviously uh, have the stuff that they want to work on and they want to get better at and I think they're doing a great job attacking the details. >> Mike, in week one, obviously you have a couple more days to prepare. How do you balance the concept of doing enough to get ready versus maybe doing too much to where you maybe you have paralysis by analysis? Do you think about that in terms of how you approach this week one preparation? >> Uh, no, we just Oh, you almost got You got me, bro. Good job. Uh, no, I wouldn't say that. I think it's more just preparing yourself and uh, putting yourself in position to go out there and be successful or whatever they may do. >> What does What does a week of preparation look like to where you feel comfortable on Sunday? Like when when you go out there, halfway talked about if you do enough in the preparation, then you'll be able to play fast and free. What does it look like for you to be able to play fast and free on Sunday? >> Uh, just go through a week of practice and uh, good or bad, make mistakes or or successful every time, it doesn't matter. I think just getting those reps and being able to go through it uh, on the field and in the walk-throughs and all those mental reps, I think that's what's important, just having that in your mind to continue to grow and when an opportunity comes and when you face that situation in the game, you have had it, you have a rep on it, you can you can know what to do. >> Mike, what are your game day rituals? >> Uh, really nothing, you know, I listen to a little music. >> [snorts] >> Any specific playlist? What do you What do you like? >> No, I got a playlist. My playlist got everything on it. I'll be listening to a old school, might be listening to some hip hop. I got a little indie rock, you know you need to know I had that on there. A little gospel. I'll be chilling. I like I like music. >> With your little combination of Devon Achane running the ball and also with an unproven receiving core, a lot of people expect defenses to stack the box against you guys. How will you approach that if you see that kind of a >> Uh you know, expectation versus reality. I mean, people can expect whatever, but when we get out there, we'll see what they try to do to attack us and we'll try to do our best to play against it. We just play ball. I mean, obviously, everybody has these mindsets and thoughts on what it's going to be and what it if people could see the future, everybody played the lottery. I mean, but people can't. So, we obviously just going to try and go do the best we can do and uh be detailed as we can through the week of practice so we can go out there and execute our plays. >> Malik, what do you tell going [clears throat] into a game relative to wanting to be aggressive and create big plays, but also limiting mistakes? Like, it seems to me that both of those things would be weighing on your mind. So, how do you process that? >> I mean, if you going out there thinking about mistakes, you are in the hole already. You can't go out there thinking about mistakes. You got to go out there and play ball. Mistakes will happen. It's I mean, they get paid, too. And the defense is going to make a play. We just got to go play ball and not be aggressive doing that. Obviously, situationally, it's how aggressive can we be? Sometimes, it's aggressive is hitting the check down. You aggressively got there fast enough where he can transition and get extra yards. Like, it's just a a mentality of being convicted in what we're doing and that comes from the preparation. >> And the crowd noise getting pumped into that, how Sorry to um to that help you guys at all or do you find that during practice at all? >> think that's always a cool thing, especially for the young guys. I don't even be hearing it half the time. I just be worried about what we got to do. And I think that's what we continue to just try to focus on with them and say, like, that doesn't matter. That's why we play it. It's we have to focus on what we're doing and it's a mental gymnastics, a mental hurdle to get over and I think that's cool that he uh implemented that. >> Yeah, one word to describe this team, you know, with all the outside noise, how would you describe your teammates and yourself? family. I think the guys are all sticking together. I think it's a we're all on this train together. We're on this journey together and we'll obviously go out there and try to do what we can to get better each and every day so we can go out there and get better each and every week and that's all we can do. >> One last question. >> Leek, what are your personal goals for the season just being week one, big opportunity for you and everything's in front of you. >> Uh just go out there and have as much fun as possible. I mean, this is a opportunity of a lifetime, bro. Not many people get to play and start football games in the National Football League. I just want to go out there and have some fun and obviously do what I can to make sure that our team is successful and we go out there and execute. >> Thank you very much. Appreciate it. >> Very nice.

title: Coach Jeff Hafley meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: Oh, not today. It's fine. >> Uh although it's not an important one, but I was curious about it. >> Every coach is different with the depth chart that is released to the media by all 32 teams every week. With you, should we take yesterday's as gospel in terms of these are the starters for Sunday? >> Um some of it. Not all of it. >> If you could go one by one, no. Uh the one one interesting thing, there were several of them that stood out. Uh Chris Bell, obviously just a couple weeks removed. He Caleb Williams started. With the two rookies, how much about I know winning is a priority, but how much for at that position do you want to know what you have long-term with Caleb and Chris this year? Uh do do you have a sense of that yet with their talents? And is that important to know that this year? >> Well, we're going to find out. Winning is a priority. We're going to put a guy out there week one uh just to see what we have. We believe those guys we believe those guys deserve to start. And we're going to start them. And we'll find out um what we need to work on, how we need to develop them. Um with winning as a priority. >> Is the performance staff sort of recommending a Chris Bell pitch count ramp up situation? Or is he not requiring any pitch count? >> Um we we're going to we're going to play him, see how he feels. And but there's no there's no pitch count on Chris. >> With all of those now listed with the safeties uh do you see that as a full-time move now? Or do you still see him as this versatile piece just listed up with the >> Versatile piece. He's been working more with the safeties. So, when they told me I had to have a home for him and I couldn't have both, I picked the safety position because that's been where he's been working with right now. But he's also still lining up at linebacker and he'll be a versatile piece. I just had to have a home for him. >> How have Have seen him grow over the last however many weeks in that role? >> Um I I think he's done a good job. You know, we've put him truly as a linebacker. We've put him as more of a you know, like a an apex cover down nickel as you'll call him. We've put him in safety. I think he's getting more comfortable with the different roles. >> When it comes to health and performance after practice, I noticed it's at 1:00 today. Is that by design with so many 1:00 starts to be in that time frame? >> It helps, um for sure. Is that the only reason? No. That time also allows us to maximize meeting time, install time, walk-through time. Um but but that certainly was taken into consideration. Every game this year will be at 1:00. >> I I'd asked you last week whether Dante and Zane would start at safety. You understandably didn't want to answer. The depth chart yesterday did have both of them as starting safeties. Are they your starting >> I see all three of them as starters and I think you're going to see the same thing as we play in the game on um Sunday. >> I ask obviously. >> Yeah, I I see I I see all three of those guys that we're going to count on, rely on. And and all three of them are going to play. >> Josh, you got an appointment? >> During the during the summer, you know, as Caleb and Chris progress, like what kind of benchmarks, what kind of things are you looking for in order to be convinced that the light bulb is starting to click and turn on for them? >> Um it it's just learning learning the plays, lining up, giving great effort, doing your job consistently. I think the key is being consistent within [clears throat] the scheme of the offense and when their opportunity comes uh to make plays that they make those plays. I mean just like all the rookies, I mean, we're going to play a lot of them on Sunday. I mean, I think that's very clear. I don't I don't know what the number is, but there's a lot of guys, so I there there's no expectation. Our our our process is to do everything we can. We just finished a walk through. We have practice coming up now. Then we're going to go out and practice. Then we're going to watch the practice. And then they're going to recover and they're going to go home. Our goal is to do everything we can every single day. So, when it come time for Sunday, I'm not worried about that. I just want them to go play free, play as fast as they can, as physical as they can, you know, clear mind, fast feet, um and and let it rip. And however that falls, we'll look at it. We'll We'll get We'll work to get better and improve as we go. And And that's going to be the way for all these guys. >> Jeff, will you allow yourself a moment on Sunday to take in your first NFL head coaching day and what that moment means to you in your journey? >> Um My guess is it will probably happen, like if I'm answering truthfully, during the national anthem when I finally can like take a deep breath cuz leading up to the game will be about the team, will be about the game plan, it will be about adjustments, it will be constantly going over the call sheet, um talking to Bobby, talking to Tabor. And probably during the national anthem is usually sometimes when I can finally take a deep breath for a few seconds and just reflect on important people that have helped me throughout my life. And usually in that time I'll, you know, think about them. >> Coach, how How unique is the challenge of getting ready for so much unknown in a week one? You got a a new play caller for a new offense. The quarterback he hasn't coached before. Just how unique is that compared to the preparation the rest of the season? >> Yeah, ask me that again. >> How unique is preparation in a game where you have a quarterback and a coach or sorry Yeah, a new head coach and a play caller and a quarterback that's all new together and you don't have much tape on what they might do. How unique is that compared to prep for other weeks and other games? >> I I I think it's the same situation exactly that they're in. I mean, that's why week one, two, and three, there there's not a lot of tendencies, right? I can go back and I can study Seattle, which is what we're doing, right? We're watching Seattle, but we're trying to watch the Raiders players and a bunch of free agents that they brought in to kind of figure out the personnel, but trying to piece together how, you know, for example, Kubiak is going to use X, Y, and Z within his scheme now that he has these guys. I mean, it's it's a big challenge. I think early in the season it's it's got to be about yourself. And and that's my message to the team. It's got to be about using our rules. It's got to be about the fundamentals and techniques that we've talked about all training camp cuz we don't know what it's going like. And and they truly they don't know what it's going to look like. I'm sure they're watching Packer tape right now with players that that are not going to play against and trying to figure out how we are going to use these guys within multiple things that we've all done throughout our careers. So, when you start building later in the season and you have tendencies down, distance, personnel, how are they using a guy, who's getting the ball on third down, who's their red zone target? Like that's when it becomes different, but this is it it's got to be worry about yourself, right? Focus on the little things, the details of the game, the things that can get you beat fast, and then you got to adjust as you go and you see it on the fly. They're they're in the same situation that we are. >> A question >> just kind of how you think and getting to know you. Number one, >> You want to know how I think? >> Yeah, yeah, [laughter] yeah. This is going deep. >> I'm glad you want to get to know me, too. I appreciate that. So, is it going to be a personal question or a football question? >> Football question. >> All right. >> Um are you one of those coaches who believes the biggest one week jump a team can make in the season is between weeks one and two? >> Uh no. I I think you can make strides throughout the season and I think that's that's our job with growth and development. Um but no, I I don't think you can pigeonhole it into week one to week two. >> And the the other one is is there a a stat or two stats that you value more than other, whether it's turnover margin, points allowed, etc.? >> Turnover margin. Turnover margin is going to be huge, especially early in the season. you got to protect the ball and um and then and then penalties early in the season. I mean, I just think if you look at early games, it's you know, it's it's first and 10, now it's first and 15 because, you know, a guy moved or it's third and two and you're all excited by your third and two call and now it's third and seven cuz there was a miss motion or a guy was covered up and a lot of self-inflicted things that cause you to go backward. Um but but those are probably the two biggest things early in the season that you're going to see. So, you know, starting tonight, those are the things that you're going to see. Um and then you got to clean those up as you go. I mean, that first game and there're going to be some anxious guys and some guys that are fired up to play the game and you got to take a deep breath and trust your training. >> I know that defense is I know that defense is multiple >> [clears throat] >> and I know that a lot of it is match-up based. So, I know at times we'll see four defensive linemen, at times we'll see three, at times we'll see one, two, or three linebackers, but I'm curious, the depth chart was a 4-2-5. >> Mhm. >> Do you think that that will end up being the uh sort of the alignment that the team ends up using most? >> That was our depth chart versus 11 personnel. So, yes. So, you have four D-linemen, two linebackers listed a nickel, two corners, and two safeties. So, when we did the depth chart, we did it versus 11 personnel. So, so we're not listing a Joker and a Sam and then all of a sudden it's or we, you know, we got 15 positions. We just we took a normal personnel grouping, we put it out there, and had a depth chart. >> be correct to say that a 4-2 base 4-2-5 base >> Well, yeah, if you're looking at it just squarely by people, right? Could be 4-3. Depends who we put at that spot and what you want to call this guy versus that guy, but I mean, 4-2 versus 4-3, if you really want to get technical, it's it's the same thing. You got four D-linemen, three guys, four secondary guys. You want to get really deep and you're just calling guy like two backers and then five DBs, it's just what do you call that guy? Is he a linebacker or is he a is he a DB? So, it's all going to look the same. It's just a matter of who that person is. >> Coach, I want to ask you about Jabrill because for a rookie to wear the green dot on defense takes a very special type of person. I can only imagine the trust that you have on him in him. And if you can talk about some of those attributes Jacob as well as any challenges that have come along the way with that communication in order or any anecdotes that you want to share with us in order for him to be translating those responsibilities from college now into the NFL. >> Yeah, it is a challenge. I'm excited for him. You know, he's earned it. He he works really hard at it. Like I've mentioned before, I mean, the guy's here all the time. He was in my office this morning going over the call sheet before 7:00 a.m. You know, and we're talking, here are the calls that I like in this situation, here's why I like it. So, if you hear me call it on this down and distance, we need to start thinking alike and I might tag it with this, so you need to listen for this and you know, we joke back and forth. Some of the calls get long and I'll try I'll say, "No, say it like this cuz there's a cadence to it, so it can come out." And he'll say, "Well, I like it more like this." And I'll say, "Well, that's we got to work on that stuff together." There's certainly challenges. I mean, that's a big responsibility in this league. I think I'd be curious to know how many rookies in the NFL wear the green dot. but I'm excited for him and and he's um he's going to do a really good job and and he'll get better at it as we go. >> Coach, when you talk about the excitement or you know, guys fired up, is there an eagerness kind of finally display on Sunday where you guys have been working hard towards it? Like what's the level of excitement or what do you how are you feeling or how do you see your players just kind of get eager to get things started? >> It should all be excitement. I mean, that's why we do what we do. I mean, training camp's hard. Training camp was long. And as much as we love practicing football, we all love playing football and And nothing better there's nothing better than Sundays. And that's why we do what we do. It's why we coach. It's why we play. And you know, it you make a really good point though. I want to make sure that towards the end of this week, as hard as we're working and preparing, there's some guys doing it for the first time. I also want them to take a step back and and enjoy it. I mean, because we're playing a game. And they need to enjoy it. They need to play free. And they need to play with that mindset and not worry about anything else. They've already put in the work, right? So, yeah, I I I can't wait. I mean, that's that's why we do what we do. >> What have you seen out of Malik this week that kind of reinforces the idea like, yeah, I have the right guy? >> Well, we've we've only really had the one quick practice for this week. Um you know, just the guy's here studying. He's meeting with the wide receivers. He's you know, he's got a smile on his face. And it's really nothing this week. It's everything that he's done up to this week and been consistent with it that that gives me confidence in him. >> Coach, play calling question for you. How much do you believe in kind of saving your bullets or have an ace up your sleeve because everything's unscouted at this point versus throwing your best stuff week one to make sure that you get a win early? >> Um that's a good question. I'm going to call what I believe our guys can execute on a high level. So, right now the call sheet, if I have one on me, it's probably bigger than it will be on game day. I just feel like it's really important early on to throw this is what we want to do. And as we go through say, all right, we can handle this, this, this, and this. And let's hold off on this or I I got to see where we're at and what these guys can execute at a high level. There's plenty of bullets. Um as we go throughout the year, the goal at each year is to continue to evolve. So, what we look like week one might not be week seven cuz there's a heavy self-scout component where I'm going to look back and say, you know what, I'm going to call No, I'm not going to call it anymore. And then you come back to it, right? So, there there's a That's a big deal and it's a really good question, but I'm not going to go on with the intent of saving bullets for a later time. I'm going to do everything that we possibly can do to win the game with whatever calls that I need as long as our players can execute them at a high level cuz it's not about me tricking anybody. It's about our guys playing good football. >> With that, and you talked about all the unknowns at this point. At what point in the season do you expect to have the clearest vision of what you have in your team as far as strengths, weaknesses, identity? >> I think it's going to I think it's going to evolve as we go, and I think it's going to take time as that clears up and we get film and we get guys comfortable and and figure out on game day exactly, you know, what some can do as they get more experience and more reps and I mean, I think that's going to be a huge part of this season. >> You have two talented young big boundary corners with Jason and with JuJu. title: How Much Does Week 1 Matter For The Seahawks?
text: As we look at just week one historically, like what should people know about this, Brian? Like I'm glad we get to watch football. I can't stand week one. Like I I it makes me so uncomfortable because it is so misleading and you can be the best team ever and not be the best team week one. Um I think see how do I say this without without taking a shot at anybody else? Um not all NFL teams is like the Lincoln. I feel like the Lincoln is one of those I feel like I'm at I feel like there's more people at Beaver Stadium but it's just as crazy. title: Jalen Hurts On Facing the Washington Commanders
text: week one, what have you found in your career, some of the challenges of going up against a first-time coordinator? >> Um Well, you don't really know what you're going to get. Do you get a feel for the chemistry you guys have, do you get a feel for where the offense is going into week one? >> It's an ongoing thing. It's It's every year. Every year is different. And you assess it given where you are, and I think we're just going on our journey, we're on our process right now. So, we're we're here. Uh had our first day of practice in this official week, and we're just building from there. >> Do you feel like you're where you guys need to be heading into the first game? >> We're taking it a day at a time. Yeah, we're taking it a day at a time. I think the guys have built uh a lot of confidence, and we've gotten a lot of reps, and we've been very intentional over the time we've shared together. So, um we're just going to continue to work. It's about the work. >> Is there any theory you had for your week one success? I mean, keeping the main thing the main thing, and um having the time to prepare, um and uh playing together. I think it's just um the it's a reflection of the work and the preparation that we've had. title: Robert Saleh Previews Week 1 vs. the Jets | Press Conference
text: I'll just start off with the whole thing with said. He's in the concussion protocol. Has a chance to clear, so we're going to let him go through that process. Like I said, every game's important. He can he he can run a very high-functioning offense and uh fully expect them to be a really really good offense as the year progresses and I would not be surprised if this unit is finishes in the top half of the league. Um Mosolino uh uh McCray Ball is uh is one of the better special teams guys in all of football. And uh so it's going to be a challenge in all three phases. They're more of a 3-4 scheme. Um but at the end of the day, we we we love his ability. Uh his his bend, his get-off, his ability to convert speed to power. Uh he's he's going to be a really really good edge rusher in this league. Um and I wouldn't be surprised if off the get he's he's producing at a high level. Okay, you're you're talking about if one of your teammates are I just think that's natural. Uh like he is your brother, you know, and uh um I do think I do think when you watch tape and you see your quarterback on the ground just take a look at the offensive line to see what their mindset is. So, uh but when it comes to Jeff and Jeffrey Jeff and JFM, um you know, I I'm biased. I I think they're two of the that's probably one of the best combinations of interior D-linemen uh uh in all of football when it comes to rushing the passer.

I mean, the leaders have been the leaders uh for the past couple years. You know, we just got uh season we got blessed enough to be named season long captains and and stuff like that. have a CR on our jersey. Um, but he's always been, you guys run everything and we had a lot of different guys throughout my first couple years here. Um, you know, be vest, be leaders, stuff like that. So, um, it's kind of been the same thing. Uh, bless you. But the only thing different, we just got to see on our on her jersey now. >> What's up, Jaden? Um, [clears throat] going into your third year, you've matured as a player obviously, but do you see the the talent around you? Does it make life that much easier for you? >> Yeah, I think um just the guys that they brought in, drafted uh offensively, defensively, special teams, uh you know, we got a lot of guys that fly around the ball and honestly just guys that like um bonding and you know, chemistry, like being around each other, hanging out, stuff like that. So, it's a good group of guys that we have in the locker room. As far as you just processing everything out on the field, do you feel like everything is is sped up for you or is it slowed down considerably in this offense? >> Um, I think it slow down. Uh, I think it's still some moving parts and you know, as the season go on, you get more comfortable stuff. Um, you know, like I said, I don't want to be my [snorts] final product week one. Um, you know, I just want to go out there and continue to just get better each and every day, each and every game. And, you know, like I said, do whatever it takes to help the team win some football games. Last one. >> Jaden, 2024 was obviously a fun season for you and this team. 2025 much tougher personally and as a franchise. How much fun are you having right now? And how do you balance that with some of your leadership responsibilities? I don't know. I don't think you balance fun. I think that's just football, man. Like, if you're not having fun, then why are you doing it? Um, so you got to go out there, have fun. It's a kids game at the end of the day. We just get paid a lot of money to go out there and play it right. Um, so for us it's just going out there having fun. But, you know, when it's time to joke around, it's time to, you know, do stuff like that. But when it's time to work, like we got to go work. But at the end of the day, like you should wake up every day and, you know, have a gratitude, humbleness of like, man, I get to do this for a living. So, it's most definitely fun for me. >> Go ahead. Last one. [clears throat] >> Jad J, >> what did you say? >> Since week one. >> Appreciate it. Jaden, I know there's times where in your career so far, you know, you've been the hero big moments. And how much faith do you have kind of in the weapons on this offense to be able to step up in those moments as well? >> Like I said, I trust those guys to go out there and make plays. text: and definitely like even in the building just like an energy that the when the season begins and so certainly we have that. Yeah, I think the main thing um DA coming into it is always wants to see us, you know, be able to run our systems and play, you know, like winning football in all three phases. So, that would look like the elimination of errors and mistakes into that space. But, um I just want to see us cleanly executed. Um, but I really want to see us play fast. I want to see this be explosive. Um, I want to see, you know, good good speed, good hitting, like those things that I've seen in practice now, like carry over like much like we were talking about with Jaden. I wonder what sort of point of emphasis or difference that kind of makes it. >> I like it as the difference. The players, they get to they have more familiarity of what they can and can't do. So, I think for the league and for the teams, it's a good feeling starting with division teams. You have a little more familiarity. What you've been to that stadium, you've gone against that play, you know what I'm saying? So, I think there's an it's not an advantage for either team, but I think it's just good for football. >> Hey, coach. So, how do you play good team defense? You better tackle well and limit the explosive plays. One thing that's um kind of defined what he is, it's good, it's good play, good play, good tackle, big one. And that's the ones you want to take those big chunk plays off the tape. So for him to have that and throw, you know, a challenging defense on top of that, I think that adds a lot of value and he's somebody that doesn't get fooled a lot and um makes good decisions. Um they've got a fantastic guy who plays the nickel, two really good linebackers, but the inside that's that's the straw that that stirs the drink for sure. But um yeah, that's that's definitely the challenge. And then um on defense, you know, I know you guys released the depth chart with the base defense, but when you're in that nickel package, do you expect um Mike Sandra still to be the guy there or is he going to move around? >> We will move Mike around. We're certainly not going to give everybody the game plan just today, but um it's a fair question. I appreciate you taking your shot. Um but there'll be somes that will use safeties, some that you know will Mike or others inside. And um but that's kind of the beauty of the package I think in some ways where it's not going to be one look all the time. Um when there's some downs you need to go deny the ball and play it a certain way, we'll do that, but that won't be every down. >> Dan over here. Um good to see you. Um over the last couple of weeks, you guys have been mentioning about how what you've shown in joint practices and preseason games, especially offensively, has been very vanilla. Like you've been keeping things close to the vest. So you guys have been repping against each other. How do you know like those reps of like you're going to have the big reveal obviously what it's going to be looking like on Sunday. How do you know you guys are ready just repping against each other? >> Yeah, I think it's um think of it much like a fight. And you know, year to year, you probably have a feeling going into the season maybe what this team is capable of. Where are you at? like as we are on the precipice of of the season opener, like what does your gut tell you about this team? >> Yeah, I love our locker room and the men that make it up. That's what you're looking for from a team where there's been very few times I'm the one, you know, at the front saying not good enough, not to this. And so to see that take place with them um and the connection they've had in a short time, that's a big deal. The best teams I've been a part of had a strong connection in the locker room first and that spilled out onto the field at practice, the way they compete. And so to see that take place early um especially with some new players, how do they fit in as veterans and rookies add to it. So, this team has just connected um maybe more quickly than we had. Um perhaps going through for the guys that are returning, you know, a difficult experience and you share that together. Um you want to make sure you're really ready to go. >> Good afternoon, coach. >> Good afternoon. >> I know uh both your coordinators obviously have done a lot of work installing the overall scheme of of what the team is going to be this year. when you transition that into actual strategy against a live opponent. What are some of the hurdles those guys are facing for the first time this week? >> Yeah. And uh so being in that seat at some point that's you know clearly part of my job to think about the contingencies that can come up whether it's a player whether it's a new system or a scheme that goes to that. And so how do you think ahead on those and what do you plan for you know could be player related scheme related of all those things. So, we just try to think of as many contingencies um as we can and make sure we can put those guys into that. And that's really part of my job weekly firing more and more and more at them. Okay, what else? And so I like those conversations taking place. There's no [snorts] substitute for being in the fire. You know that. So, I think that speaks a lot to how far, you know, he's returned back from the injury and like putting his stake down that hey, these are the standards, how we want to do it. So, he's had a really good camp. He's strong. Um, he's protecting well and so I thought like every once in a while you stay in that good groove and that's what I keep telling him, man, just the pocket that you're in, like stay right in it. >> Have time for three more. >> Hey, Dan. Uh, just to follow up on the coordinator thing. um in game when you get to kind of a key moment third and six whatever offensive or defense how involved will you be kind of in play calling and decision-m there or is this we planned all through training camp and you know now we put you guys in these positions we'll we'll trust what you guys are thinking >> yep kind of two-part I'll answer it if that's okay so in between I'll often give some insight so I don't want to be the person while they're making the call like man that's a good call or why did you call that and so I try to lead ahead of it to So, um if there's um some examples that I can throw out in that time, I definitely will. I can like clearly remember an example where Pete Carol did that with me and I said, "Okay." So, like when I hear one of those and it's my time to step in to say, "This is that time. Take your shot. Do that. I'll definitely do that." Um but I try to give guidance in between in the space in between, you know, not while they're about to make it, but you know, leading up to it, the play ends. Think of this. think of this and then as it goes to like the game and on the line or you specific things you know like I've had good visits with Donte pre you know I've had like good experience against them in terms of the planning you know from previous to here so going against Billy for five years in the division like that helps so those are you know wisdom to share and say this is these are some of the scars this is some of the things that have been good and sharing some of that so that's parts during the week in-game it's insight but not not during the call. So, I think it's a little bit of everything, Ben, that goes into that mix. But, yeah, that's that's my role for all the coaches to make sure, hey, be on top of this. It means that this guy's going to be like a excellent play caller in the NFL. >> Last one. >> Almost won >> yesterday, right? >> Almost. Man, was that awesome? I uh uh we're really pumped to see that to say in fact I talked to the team about that of playing that long how good a shape you have to be in and have the steadiness to go about it.
